board.value: Alabama Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The Alabama Board of Physical Therapy is now an active member state.

education.value: Applicants must have completed a CAPTE-approved physical therapy education program; foreign-educated applicants must complete a credentials review through FCCPT.
education.quote: must have completed a CAPTE approved program of physical therapy education appropriate for preparation as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Exam (NPTE) and have their NPTE score sent to the Board.
national_exam.quote: appropriate for preparation as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant and successfully passed the National Physical Therapy Exam (NPTE)

state_exam.value: Since 10/07/2024, all applicants (new graduates and endorsement) must pass the Alabama Jurisprudence Exam (AL JAM), provided by FSBPT; passing requires 80% correct and the FSBPT fee is $48.00.
state_exam.quote: Applicants are required to answer 80% of the questions correctly to pass the AL JAM.

background_check.value: Since June 14, 2024, applicants must complete a fingerprint-based federal and state criminal background check through the Board's vendor, Fieldprint, after submitting their application.
background_check.quote: an applicant for licensure as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant must submit to a fingerprint-based federal and state criminal background check

application_fee.value: Applicants must pay a $100 application fee with the online application.
application_fee.quote: Completed online application with $100 application fee paid.

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed elsewhere apply by endorsement/score transfer: they need official verification from each state where they hold a license, must pass the AL JAM, and must show 10 hours of continuing education from the last 12 months unless they graduated within the past 12 months.
endorsement.quote: Licensure by score transfer/endorsement - 10 hours of continuing education completed in the last 12 months unless graduation was within the past 12 months.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A temporary license is available once all application requirements, including the background check and AL JAM, are met; a Temp Supervisory Agreement Form is part of the process.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: All application requirements met, including background check and AL JAM.

renewal.value: Licenses are renewed annually and expire on October 1; the renewal period runs July 1 through September 30, and the PT renewal fee is $130.
renewal.quote: Each license expires on October 1 of the year following its issuance.

continuing_education.value: PTs must complete 10 hours of continuing education with each annual renewal (12 hours for PTs providing Direct Access); 2 hours of Alabama jurisprudence covering the Practice Act and Administrative Code are required at the first renewal and thereafter in years ending in 0 or 5.
continuing_education.quote: Ten (10) hours of continuing education are required with each renewal application.

compact.value: Alabama is an active member state of the Physical Therapy Compact; Alabama-resident licensees can apply through the Compact Commission for compact privileges, and therapists from other states must pass Alabama's jurisprudence exam before purchasing a privilege to practice in Alabama.
compact.quote: The Alabama Board of Physical Therapy is now an active member state in the Physical Therapy Compact.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the board's online licensee portal, linked as Application for Licensure on the board's Online Services page.
apply_url.quote: Please follow the links below to obtain our available services:

board.value: Alabama State Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: Welcome to the website of the Alabama State Board of Occupational Therapy.

education.value: Applicants must have completed the academic requirements of an occupational therapy program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association.
education.quote: The program shall be accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass a Board-approved written examination and have the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) send the Board a verification letter confirming they met certification requirements.
national_exam.quote: Each applicant must request that a letter of verification be issued by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

application_fee.value: The initial license fee for an occupational therapist is $140.00.
application_fee.quote: Initial license fee: Occupational Therapist $140.00; Occupational Therapy Assistant

endorsement.value: The Board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements for an applicant who holds a current OT license in another state, the District of Columbia or a U.S. territory whose licensing standards the Board considers equivalent.
endorsement.quote: license to any applicant who shall present proof of current licensure as an occupational therapist or an occupational therapy assistant in another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have not yet passed the NBCOT exam may obtain a limited permit to practice under supervision; it costs $25.00, expires 120 days after issuance or on notice of exam failure, and is not renewable.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Limited permits shall expire 120 days after issuance or upon notification of failure of examination by the National Board of Certification in Occupational Therapy

renewal.value: Current licenses expire on October 31, 2026; the OT renewal fee is $140.00, and a $50.00 late fee applies if the renewal is not completed by midnight on August 31, 2026 (60 days before expiration).
renewal.quote: Renewal fee ($140.00 for OTs and $115.00 for OTAs) will be collected at the end of the application

continuing_education.value: OTs must obtain 15 contact hours (1.5 CEUs) annually or 30 contact hours (3.0 CEUs) biennially; no more than 1/3 may be administration, management or academic, with the rest related to direct patient treatment.
continuing_education.quote: An Occupational Therapist must obtain 1.5 CEUs (or 15 contact hours) annually or 3.0 CEUs (or 30 contact hours) biennially.

compact.value: Alabama is one of 32 states that are members of the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact, according to the board.
compact.quote: Currently, 32 states, including Alabama, are already compact members with current Legislation enacted to adopt the OTCC rules and regulations.

apply_url.value: Applicants can download the license application or submit it online from the board's Applications and Forms page.
apply_url.quote: The following forms are available for download in PDF format:

board.value: Alabama Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: ABESPA - Alabama Board of Examiners for Speech Language Pathology and Audiology

education.value: SLP applicants must have at least a master's degree or equivalent, plus Board-approved supervised clinical practicum and postgraduate professional experience.
education.quote: Possess evidence of at least a master's degree or equivalent

national_exam.value: Applicants without ASHA's Certificate of Clinical Competence must pass the ETS Praxis II Speech-Language Pathology exam (or a Board-approved equivalent) at or above the Board's cutoff score, with the score sent to the Board by ETS.
national_exam.quote: The Educational Testing Service (ETS) national examination Praxis II Audiology exam or the Praxis II Speech-Language Pathology exam may serve as the approved examination

application_fee.value: Applications must be accompanied by a non-refundable $200.00 application fee; a $75.00 license fee (prorated for approvals after August) is due on Board approval.
application_fee.quote: Applications must be accompanied by a $200.00 application fee, which can in no case be refunded.

endorsement.value: The Board may grant a license by reciprocity to a holder of ASHA's Certificate of Clinical Competence or of a current license in another state whose standards meet or exceed Alabama's, on payment of the fee and proof of the out-of-state license.
endorsement.quote: or who holds a current license in another state in speech-language pathology or audiology may be granted a license according to the following conditions

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical Fellows and fourth-year interns must apply for a provisional license within 30 days of beginning employment or an internship, with a $200 application fee and a notarized supervisor statement; the Clinical Fellowship must be completed within a maximum of 36 months.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: are required to apply for a provisional license with the Board within thirty (30) days of beginning employment or an internship.

renewal.value: All licenses expire on December 31 and must be renewed every year with a $100.00 renewal fee and documentation of 12 clock hours of continuing education submitted before December 31.
renewal.quote: ALL LICENSES EXPIRE ON DECEMBER 31. To maintain license a $100.00 annual renewal fee and documentation of twelve (12) clock hours of continuing education

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 12 hours of continuing education each year (January 1 to December 31), at least 10 of them in the area of licensure, one of which should be in ethics, and at most 2 in related areas.
continuing_education.quote: Content Area I; one of the ten hours should be in the area of ethics; and a maximum of (2)

compact.value: Alabama is not among the ASLP-IC states issuing compact privileges: the Commission says registration for privileges is open only for practitioners licensed in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee and West Virginia.
compact.quote: Registration is open for licensed practitioners in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, and West Virginia

apply_url.value: Applicants find the licensure application, including the online application link, on the board's Applications and Forms page.
apply_url.quote: Completion of Licensure Process (For Clinical Fellows and 4th Year Interns only)

board.value: State Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Board
board.quote: Creation and membership of board. (a) There is created the State Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Board, which consists of seven members.

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from a CAPTE-accredited physical therapy program, with an official transcript of the first professional degree sent directly from the school to the division.
education.quote: An official transcript (first professional conferred degree) sent directly from the CAPTE-accredited school of physical therapy to our division.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the national physical therapy examination with at least the FSBPT-recommended passing score, which equals a scaled score of 600 on a scale of 200 to 800.
national_exam.quote: The passing score will equal a scaled score of 600 based on a scale ranging from 200 to 800.

state_exam.value: All applicants must complete the board's Jurisprudence Questionnaire, answering questions by reviewing Alaska's physical therapy and occupational therapy statutes and regulations and citing where each answer is found.
state_exam.quote: All applicants for licensure must complete the following questionnaire prepared by the Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit an FD-258 fingerprint card to the board, which forwards it to the Alaska Department of Public Safety for a state and FBI criminal background check; the fingerprint processing fee is $75.
background_check.quote: who will submit it to the Department of Public Safety (DPS) to perform a criminal background check through the State and Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI)

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $150 nonrefundable application fee, a $200 license fee and a $75 fingerprint processing fee, for total fees due of $425.
application_fee.quote: Nonrefundable Application Fee: $150.00 License Fee: $200.00 Fingerprint Processing Fee: $ 75.00 Total Fees Due: $425.00

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state apply for licensure by credentials, submitting NPTE scores, license verification from every jurisdiction where they have been licensed, and proof of at least 60 hours of physical therapy employment in the prior 24 months (or NPTE passage in that window, or a board-approved 150-hour internship).
endorsement.quote: at least 60 hours of physical therapy employment within the 24 months immediately preceding the date the application is received by the department

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may issue a temporary permit that lets a licensure-by-credentials applicant practice while the application is processed; it requires a complete application and an additional $65 temporary permit fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: To receive a temporary permit, numbers 1-2 and 4-9 in the section above must have been received along with the additional $65.00 temporary permit fee.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on June 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance.
renewal.quote: Licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on June 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists licensed for 12 months or more of the licensing period must complete 24 contact hours of continuing education per period, and renewal also requires 60 hours of practice (or an approved alternative) and the board's jurisprudence questionnaire.
continuing_education.quote: physical therapist assistant license who has been licensed for 12 months or more of the concluding licensing period shall have completed 24 contact hours of continuing education during that period.

compact.value: Alaska accepts PT Compact privileges: the board's application states that therapists may purchase a PT Compact Privilege instead of applying for an Alaska license.
compact.quote: If you are interested in purchasing a PT Compact Privilege instead of applying for licensure

apply_url.value: Applicants apply by mailing the board's application form to the Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy, PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811; faxed or emailed applications are not accepted.
apply_url.quote: Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811 Phone: (907) 465-2550

board.value: State Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Board
board.quote: Creation and membership of board. (a) There is created the State Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Board, which consists of seven members.

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from an accredited professional occupational therapy education program that includes supervised field work.
education.quote: have graduated from a professional occupational therapy education program that includes supervised field work and is accredited by a national accreditation agency approved by the board;

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT certification examination, which they arrange directly with NBCOT, and the division retrieves verification of initial NBCOT certification.
national_exam.quote: Verification of initial certification by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, Inc. (NBCOT). Our agency will retrieve the certification from the NBCOT for you.

state_exam.value: All applicants must complete the board's Jurisprudence Questionnaire, answering questions by reviewing Alaska's physical therapy and occupational therapy statutes and regulations and citing where each answer is found.
state_exam.quote: All applicants for licensure must complete the following questionnaire prepared by the Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit an FD-258 fingerprint card to the board, which forwards it to the Alaska Department of Public Safety for a state and FBI criminal background check; the fingerprint processing fee is $75.
background_check.quote: who will submit it to the Department of Public Safety (DPS) to perform a criminal background check through the State and Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI)

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $150 nonrefundable application fee, a $200 license fee and a $75 fingerprint processing fee, for total fees due of $425.
application_fee.quote: Nonrefundable Application Fee: $150.00 License Fee: $200.00 Fingerprint Processing Fee: $ 75.00 Total Fees Due: $425.00

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed in another state apply for licensure by credentials, submitting license verification from every jurisdiction where they have been licensed, NBCOT certification, and proof of at least 60 hours of occupational therapy service in the prior 24 months (or exam passage in that window, or a board-approved 150-hour internship).
endorsement.quote: at least 60 hours of occupational therapy service within the 24 months immediately preceding the date the application is received by the department

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may issue a temporary permit that lets a licensure-by-credentials applicant practice while the application is processed; it requires a complete application and an additional $65 temporary permit fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: To receive a temporary permit, numbers 1-2 and 4-8 in the section above must have been received along with the additional $65.00 temporary permit fee.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on June 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance.
renewal.quote: Licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on June 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists licensed for 12 months or more of the licensing period must complete 24 contact hours of continuing education or show current NBCOT certification, and renewal also requires 60 hours of practice (or an approved alternative) and a jurisprudence questionnaire.
continuing_education.quote: (1) completed, during that period, 24 contact hours of continuing education; or (2) evidence of current certification by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).

compact.value: Alaska has enacted the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact into state law; this source does not say whether OT compact privileges are being issued yet.
compact.quote: Compact enacted. The Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact as contained in this section is enacted into law and entered into on behalf of the state

apply_url.value: Applicants apply by mailing the board's application form to the Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy, PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811; faxed or emailed applications are not accepted.
apply_url.quote: Board of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811 Phone: (907) 465-2550

board.value: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathologist Program
board.quote: Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathologist Program

education.value: Applicants must hold the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence in speech-language pathology, or its equivalent, and be at least 18 years old.
education.quote: furnishes evidence satisfactory to the department that the person holds a Certificate of Clinical Competence in speech-language pathology from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association or the equivalent of the certificate

background_check.value: Applicants must submit an FD-258 fingerprint card, which the program forwards to the Alaska Department of Public Safety and the FBI for a criminal background check; the fingerprint processing fee is $75.
background_check.quote: who will submit it to the Department of Public Safety (DPS) and the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) to perform a criminal background check (AS 12.62.400).

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $200 nonrefundable application fee, a $70 license fee and a $75 fingerprint processing fee, for total fees due of $345.
application_fee.quote: Nonrefundable Application Fee: $200.00 Speech-Language Pathologist License Fee: $ 70.00 Fingerprint Processing Fee: $ 75.00 Total Fees Due $345.00

endorsement.value: Speech-language pathologists licensed in another state use the standard license application (with ASHA certification and verification from every jurisdiction where they have been licensed) and may receive a temporary license while it is pending by paying an additional $70 temporary license fee.
endorsement.quote: an individual who is licensed to practice speech-language pathology in another state and has submitted items #1, #2, #4 and #5 listed above and the additional $70.00 temporary license fee.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Alaska issues a temporary speech-language pathologist license to clinical fellows, resident or not, who are completing the supervised clinical year for the ASHA CCC; fees are a $200 nonrefundable application fee and a $70 temporary license fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license may be issued to an applicant who whether a resident or not, is in the process of completing a year of supervised clinical experience for the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competency (CCC).

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on September 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance.
renewal.quote: Licenses are issued for a two-year period and expire on September 30 of even-numbered years, regardless of the date of issuance

compact.value: Alaska has enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, which the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development is directed to implement; this source does not say whether privileges are being issued yet.
compact.quote: The Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development shall implement the audiology and speech-language interstate compact enacted under this section.

processing_time.value: The division says processing a paper application varies by program but can take several weeks from the date a complete application with all fees is received.
processing_time.quote: The average time to process a paper application varies by program but can take several weeks from the date it is received in this office

apply_url.value: Applicants apply by submitting the speech-language pathologist license application to the Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathologist Program, PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811.
apply_url.quote: Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathologist Program PO Box 110806, Juneau, AK 99811 Phone: (907) 465-2550

education.value: U.S.-educated applicants must be graduates of a professional physical therapy education program accredited by a national accreditation agency approved by the Board.
education.quote: Be a graduate of a professional physical therapy education program that is accredited by a national accreditation agency approved by the board.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), which is administered at Prometric testing sites on fixed dates; exam registration and payment are completed through FSBPT.
national_exam.quote: The NPTE is administered at Prometric Testing Sites on fixed dates. AZ JAM is available online and on-demand.

state_exam.value: All applicants for a new Arizona license must pass the Arizona Jurisprudence Assessment Module (AZ JAM), an online, on-demand assessment of 50 questions in 90 minutes that requires 80% correct and costs $48. It is also required to purchase or renew an Arizona compact privilege.
state_exam.quote: All applicants for a new license in Arizona must take and pass the Arizona Jurisprudence Assessment Module prior to licensure.

background_check.value: Applicants must obtain a valid fingerprint clearance card issued pursuant to A.R.S. 41-1758.03.
background_check.quote: Obtain a valid fingerprint clearance card issued pursuant to section 41-1758.03.

application_fee.value: The standard PT application fee is $260; applications submitted in year 2 of a renewal cycle pay a prorated PT application fee of $190. Application fees are non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: Standard Application Fee: PT: $260 PTA: $160 Prorated Application Fee (applications submitted in year 2 of a renewal cycle; 9/1/odd year-8/31/even year): PT: $190

endorsement.value: PTs with a valid unrestricted license in another U.S. jurisdiction may apply by endorsement; they must be graduates of an accredited program, have passed the NPTE, pass the AZ JAM and obtain a fingerprint clearance card. Arizona residents licensed in another state for at least 1 year may instead apply by universal recognition.
endorsement.quote: Application by Endorsement is for an Arizona Physical Therapist or Physical Therapist Assistant license by Endorsement, which means the applicant has a valid unrestricted license in another US jurisdiction.

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board issues interim permits for a supervised clinical practice period to foreign-educated applicants who meet the licensure requirements, and to U.S.-educated applicants whose competence is in question; an interim permit lasts at least ninety days but not more than six months, under the continuous on-site supervision of a licensed PT.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The board may issue an interim permit for at least ninety days but not more than six months.

compact.value: Arizona is a member state of the Physical Therapy Compact, and its member states are listed as actively issuing and accepting compact privileges. Compact privilege purchasers must also pass the AZ JAM.
compact.quote: Member States (38) Alabama Alaska Arizona Arkansas Colorado Connecticut Delaware

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted and paid for through the Board's online portal, linked from its New Applicants page.
apply_url.quote: Applications are required for licensure and must be submitted through your online portal with payment in full.

education.value: Applicants must complete the academic and fieldwork requirements of an educational program meeting Board standards, including at least nine hundred twenty-eight hours of supervised fieldwork experience for occupational therapists.
education.quote: For an occupational therapist, a minimum of nine hundred twenty-eight hours of supervised fieldwork experience as determined by the supervising institution, organization or sponsor.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the written examination approved and administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).
national_exam.quote: An applicant for licensure shall take a written examination approved and administered by the national board for certification in occupational therapy, incorporated.

background_check.value: Since January 1, 2022, applicants for original licensure, license renewal, reinstatement or a limited license must possess a valid fingerprint clearance card.
background_check.quote: Beginning January 1, 2022, an applicant for original licensure, license renewal, license reinstatement or a limited license pursuant to this chapter shall possess a valid fingerprint clearance card

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board may grant a limited license to a person who has completed the academic and fieldwork requirements but has not taken the licensure examination; the holder must practice under a licensed OT's supervision, and the license is valid for four months and becomes void if the person fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A limited license is valid for four months and becomes void if a person fails the examination.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses are subject to renewal every two years and expire unless renewed.
renewal.quote: Except as provided in section 32-4301, a license issued under this chapter is subject to renewal every two years and expires unless renewed.

compact.value: Arizona is an OT Compact state, but the OT Compact Commission lists Arizona as not yet accepting applications for compact privileges to practice.
compact.quote: $75 Arizona Not Yet $0 $0 $75 Arkansas October 5, 2026 not required

board.value: Arizona Department of Health Services, Bureau of Licensing for Professions & Occupations (Speech & Hearing Professionals)
board.quote: The bureau issues licenses for individuals, which include, Community Health Workers, Doulas, Laser Technicians, Medical Radiologic Technologists, Midwives

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's degree in speech-language pathology or the equivalent from a nationally or regionally accredited college or university, complete a supervised clinical practicum, and complete postgraduate professional experience approved by the director.
education.quote: A master's degree in speech-language pathology or the equivalent from a nationally or regionally accredited college or university in a program consistent with the standards of this state's universities.

national_exam.value: Applicants must document completion of the ETS NESLP (Praxis) exam, or may instead submit a valid ASHA CCC-SLP certification.
national_exam.quote: Documentation of the applicant's completion of the ETSNESLP (Praxis) as required in ARS

background_check.value: Applicants convicted of a misdemeanor or felony (including DUI) must submit court records documenting the disposition and verification that the disposition was completed.
background_check.quote: If convicted of a misdemeanor or felony (including DUI), photocopy of court records documenting disposition and verification of completion of disposition must be submitted with application.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a nonrefundable $100 initial application fee plus a $200 initial license fee by cashier's check or money order; qualifying first-time applicants may instead request a fee waiver.
application_fee.quote: A nonrefundable initial application fee of $100 plus an initial license fee of $200 via cashier's check or money order

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another state may apply by reciprocity with documentation of each professional license they hold; the license must be at least 1 year old to qualify for reciprocity.
endorsement.quote: Documentation of the valid professional license issued to the applicant by each state in which the applicant holds a professional license. The valid license must be at least 1 year old to qualify for reciprocity.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants completing their clinical fellowship may hold a temporary speech-language pathologist license, effective for 24 months from issuance and renewable only once, and must practice under the supervision of a licensed SLP.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license issued is effective for 24 months from the date of issuance.

renewal.value: A regular license is renewed every two years on payment of the renewal fee, with a thirty-day grace period after expiration during which a late fee applies.
renewal.quote: A licensee shall renew a regular license every two years on payment of the renewal fee prescribed in section 36-1908.

continuing_education.value: When renewing, SLPs must provide proof of at least twenty hours of continuing education completed within the prior twenty-four months.
continuing_education.quote: When renewing a regular license in audiology or in speech-language pathology, the licensee shall provide proof of having completed at least twenty hours of continuing education within the prior twenty-four months.

compact.value: Arizona is listed by the ASLP Compact Commission as not yet accepting applications for audiology and speech-language pathology compact privileges.
compact.quote: Arizona not yet AZ Jurisprudence AZ Practice Act and TBD $50

processing_time.value: Applications may take three to four weeks to process and are processed in the order received; expedited services are not available.
processing_time.quote: Applications may take three to four weeks to process and are processed in the order received.

apply_url.value: Applicants submit the Department's Speech-Language Pathologist Initial Application with all checklist items before a license can be issued.
apply_url.quote: all requirements listed below must be submitted before a license can be issued by the Department.

board.value: Arkansas State Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The Arkansas State Board of Physical Therapy was created by Act 1232 of 1991.

education.value: Applicants must be graduates of a Board-approved physical therapy program in the United States or its territories; graduates of other programs must have their education evaluated for equivalency.
education.quote: Applicants must be graduates of a Board approved physical therapy program at a school, college or university located within the continental United States or its territories.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by FSBPT, with a scaled score of at least 600 on a 200-800 scale.
national_exam.quote: Exam score must meet the criterion-referenced passing point equal to a scaled score of 600 based on a range of 200-800.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Arkansas jurisprudence exam, 20 questions on the Practice Act and Rules taken online, with a passing score of 70% and a $10.00 fee.
state_exam.quote: A passing score on the Arkansas State Board of Physical Therapy Jurisprudence Exam is required for initial licensure and for license renewal.

background_check.value: Applicants must apply to the Identification Bureau of the Arkansas State Police for state and national criminal background checks, and no license is issued until the results are received.
background_check.quote: No Applicant will be issued licensure until the results of the criminal background check are received.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state apply by reciprocity with a $5.00 application fee, a jurisprudence exam certificate, a passing national exam score, verification of every license ever held, and a criminal background check.
endorsement.quote: Official verification of all current and/or all previously issued licenses to practice physical therapy.

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board issues a temporary and provisional license on request to applicants holding a substantially similar license in good standing in another jurisdiction; it is valid for 90 days or until the Board decides the application, whichever comes first.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The temporary license shall be effective for 90 days or until the Board makes a decision on the application, whichever occurs first.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses must be renewed annually by March 1.
renewal.quote: Licenses must be renewed annually by March 1. Physical Therapists and Physical Therapist Assistants who have not paid annual renewal fees by March 1

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 2 CEUs (20 hours) each two-year biennium before the odd-numbered-year renewal, no more than 50% online, and passing the jurisprudence exam (counted as 1 online hour) is part of the requirement.
continuing_education.quote: physical therapists must complete, in each biennium (two-year period), two (2) CEUs (20 hours)

compact.value: Arkansas is listed among the 38 PT Compact member states, which the compact describes as actively issuing and accepting compact privileges.
compact.quote: Member States (38) Alabama Alaska Arizona Arkansas Colorado Connecticut Delaware

apply_url.value: Applicants by examination submit the Board's paper application packet with the required forms, fees and documents to the Board.
apply_url.quote: To apply for the PT or PTA examination, all forms, fees and documentation outlined below must be returned to ARPTB.

board.value: Arkansas State Medical Board
board.quote: While the compact is not yet operational, the Arkansas State Medical Board is actively onboarding with the IMLCC and reviewing specific technology-related requirements.

education.value: Occupational therapists must complete an educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education leading to a bachelor's or master's level degree or advanced standing certification, plus at least 6 months of supervised fieldwork.
education.quote: For an Occupational Therapist, the program shall be accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education and shall lead to the awarding of a bachelor's or master's level degree

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), which the Board has adopted as its licensing exam.
national_exam.quote: The Board has adopted for this purpose the examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

state_exam.value: Applicants must return a questionnaire on the Arkansas OT Practice Act and Rule No. 6, together with a signed Medical Practices Act and Rules affidavit, with the application.
state_exam.quote: This questionnaire is an extension of the Medical Practice Act and Rules Affidavit, also enclosed. Both documents must be returned with your application.

background_check.value: All applicants must undergo state and federal criminal background checks; Arkansas residents are fingerprinted electronically and out-of-state applicants receive a background check packet by mail.
background_check.quote: Act 1249 of 2005 authorizes the Arkansas State Medical Board to conduct criminal background checks (both state and federal) on ALL applicants for licensure.

endorsement.value: An occupational therapist licensed in another state or territory whose requirements were equal to Arkansas's at the time of registration may be licensed by reciprocity, at the Board's discretion.
endorsement.quote: who has been issued a license to practice occupational therapy in another state or territory whose requirements for registration and licensure were equal at the time of his or her registration

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet the education requirements but have not yet passed the NBCOT exam may request a temporary permit for a $1 fee; it expires 30 days after the NBCOT eligibility date and can be extended one time.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: permits expire 30 days after the NBCOT eligibility date, and can be extended ONE time by submitting a written request and an additional $1 (one) fee.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses must be renewed annually on or before the last day of the licensee's birth month, with no grace period.
renewal.quote: must be renewed annually on or before the last day of your birth month. There is no grace period.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 10 continuing education credits each year as a prerequisite for license renewal.
continuing_education.quote: Each occupational therapist and occupational therapy assistant shall be required to complete ten (10) continuing education credits each year, as a prerequisite for license renewal in the State of Arkansas.

compact.value: The Arkansas State Medical Board states that OT Compact implementation is scheduled to begin October 5, 2026.
compact.quote: Additionally, OT Compact implementation is scheduled to begin October 5, 2026.

processing_time.value: The Board states that processing a permanent license application will take several weeks, and applications are processed in the order received.
processing_time.quote: Processing a permanent license application will take several weeks to complete. Please plan for this.

apply_url.value: Applicants use the Board's Occupational Therapy Licensure Information Packet, which contains the application and all required forms.
apply_url.quote: This packet contains all of the documents you will need to apply for an Occupational Therapy or Occupational Therapy Assistant license in Arkansas.

board.value: Arkansas Board of Examiners in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The function of the Board is to examine the credentials and qualifications of Speech-Language Pathologists, Speech-Language Pathology Assistants, and Audiologists who wish to provide services to the people of Arkansas

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree in communicative disorders (speech-language pathology) meeting the requirements of a nationally recognized accrediting body.
education.quote: Applicants for licensure must hold a master's or doctoral degree in communicative disorders (speech language pathology or audiology)

national_exam.value: Applicants without ASHA certification must submit an official Praxis score of 162 or better sent directly from ETS.
national_exam.quote: Official Praxis score of 162 or better obtained directly from ETS.

application_fee.value: The application fee has been reduced from $100 to $5 under Act 114 of 2023, and it is non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: Starting July 16, 2023, the application fee is reduced from $100 to $5.

endorsement.value: An applicant holding a current speech-language pathology license from another state with standards the Board considers equivalent may be licensed by reciprocity, and must provide verification of good standing from every state where licensed.
endorsement.quote: may be so licensed if s/he possesses a current license in speech-language pathology and/or audiology from another state which maintains professional standards considered by the Board to be equivalent to those set forth in the Act.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows completing the 36-week professional experience are eligible for a provisional license only; it is renewable annually but cannot be renewed after 36 months from the start of the experience.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license is renewable annually but will expire and shall not be renewed after 36 months from the initiation of the professional experience.

renewal.value: Licenses must be renewed online annually by October 31, or by a mailed renewal postmarked on or before November 15, to avoid delinquent renewal fees.
renewal.quote: All licenses shall be renewed online annually by October 31, or postmarked on or before November 15, to avoid delinquent renewal fees.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 10 clock hours of continuing professional education each license period (November 1 through October 31), at least 5 of them in Content Area I; dual licensees need 15 hours.
continuing_education.quote: The licensee must participate in CPE activities of at least ten (10) clock hours for each license period (November 1 through October 31 of each year).

compact.value: Arkansas appears in the ASLP-IC Commission's state table as not yet accepting compact privilege applications, with no jurisprudence exam required.
compact.quote: Arkansas not yet not required AR Practice Act TBD $50

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the online application linked from the Board's Application Information page and may begin work during a 30-day grace period once a complete packet is received.
apply_url.quote: Upon receipt of a completed application packet, an applicant is granted a 30-day grace period to begin work while his/her initial application is being processed.

board.value: Physical Therapy Board of California
board.quote: To protect the people of California by the effective administration of the Physical Therapy Practice Act.

education.value: You must complete a physical therapist program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE).
education.quote: To qualify for Physical Therapist licensure, an individual must complete a physical therapist program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE)

national_exam.value: You must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered through the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT). The PT exam has 225 questions over five hours and can be taken up to three times in 12 months.
national_exam.quote: The PT NPTE is 225 questions, and you have five hours to complete it. You may take the NPTE three times in a 12-month period.

state_exam.value: California requires its law exam, the CAL-JAM (California Jurisprudence Assessment Module). It is taken online through FSBPT, costs $50, has 50 questions, and you pass by answering 80% correctly, with no limit on attempts.
state_exam.quote: Takers are required to answer 80% of the questions correctly to pass the CAL-JAM. There is no limit on the number of attempts.

background_check.value: All applicants must be fingerprinted for a DOJ and FBI background check. Use Live Scan if you will be in California during the process; out-of-state applicants who will not be in California use fingerprint hard cards ($49 processing fee).
background_check.quote: If you will be in California at any time during the application process, or if you are a California resident, submit your fingerprints via a California Live Scan location.

application_fee.value: For a physical therapist, the application processing fee is $300 (nonrefundable) and the initial license fee is $150. Fingerprint hard cards add $49.
application_fee.quote: Application Processing Fee: $300 The application processing fee is nonrefundable. Initial License Fee (ILF): $150

endorsement.value: PTs already licensed in another U.S. state apply by Endorsement through BreEZe. They must still pass the CAL-JAM, submit fingerprints and a passport-style photo, and pay the application and initial license fees.
endorsement.quote: If you already hold a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license in another U.S. physical therapy licensing jurisdiction, you will apply for licensure in California by way of Endorsement.

temporary_or_provisional.value: California grants License Applicant Status (PTLA), which lets an applicant work under supervision before the full license is issued. You may work as a PTLA only after the PTBC sends a notice granting that status.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: You are not authorized to work as a physical therapist license applicant/physical therapist assistant license applicant (PTLA/PTALA) until you receive a notice from PTBC granting you license applicant status.

renewal.value: A PT license must be renewed every two years. It expires on the last day of the licensee's birth month. The biennial renewal fee is $300.
renewal.quote: A license to practice physical therapy must be renewed every two years. The expiration date is the last day of the licensee's birth month.

continuing_education.value: PTs need 30 hours of continuing competency per two-year renewal, including 4 hours of basic life support (hands-on) and 2 hours of ethics, laws and regulations. A first renewal paid on time needs 15 hours.
continuing_education.quote: The same expiration date will apply and another 30 hours of continuing competency activity will be required at the time of your next renewal.

compact.value: California is not a member of the PT Compact. The compact commission lists it among non-member states, so compact privileges cannot be used to practice in California.
compact.quote: Non-Members (10) California Florida Hawaii Idaho Minnesota New Mexico New York

processing_time.value: The PTBC acknowledges receipt of an application within 30 days. Once all deficiencies are resolved and exam scores are received, it generally issues the license within 45 days.
processing_time.quote: Once all deficiencies in your application are satisfied and your scores are received, a license is generally issued within 45 days.

apply_url.value: Apply online through DCA BreEZe; the board's Apply Now page linked here has the link.
apply_url.quote: Continue below to create your BreEZe account and apply online.

board.value: California Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants work with people experiencing different medical conditions or disabilities to develop, improve or restore functional daily living skills.

education.value: You need a degree from an occupational therapy program. For licensure the board requires an official sealed transcript from the program showing the degree and graduation date.
education.quote: Official transcripts must be received in the original sealed envelope from the OT/OTA program and have the degree and graduation date posted.

national_exam.value: California uses the NBCOT certification examination as its licensing exam. A permanent license is issued after you pass the NBCOT exam.
national_exam.quote: How do I get my permanent license after I pass the NBCOT exam?

background_check.value: Every applicant must pass a DOJ and FBI criminal background check. Use Live Scan in California, or the board's fingerprint cards (with a $49 processing fee) if you live out of state.
background_check.quote: The Board requires a Department of Justice (DOJ) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) criminal history background check on all applicants.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $50. The initial license fee is separate. It is prorated based on your birth date and the month the license is issued, and the board states the amount in your approval letter.
application_fee.quote: The application fee is $50.00 and must be submitted with the application. The application processing fee is not the same as the initial license fee

endorsement.value: California has no separate endorsement license. Out-of-state OTs file the standard application. An OT with a valid license in another state who has passed the national exam may work in California for 60 calendar days after the board receives the application, in association with a California-licensed OT.
endorsement.quote: allows an OT or OTA who holds a valid license in another state, has taken and passed the national exam, and has not been previously denied a license in California, to work in California for 60 calendar days

temporary_or_provisional.value: Recent graduates can get a limited permit to work under supervision while waiting to take the NBCOT exam. Applicants must apply to NBCOT within 4 months of finishing their education. The permit lasts up to 3 months and ends immediately if the applicant fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Limited permits are issued to recent graduates in order to allow them to work under supervision while waiting to take the national examination.

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years. They expire at midnight on the last day of your birth month, in odd or even years depending on your birth year.
renewal.quote: The term of a license or certificate is two years. Licenses and certificates expire at midnight on the last day of your birth month in odd or even years depending on your birth year.

continuing_education.value: Each two-year renewal requires 24 professional development units (PDUs). Twelve of them must relate directly to delivering OT services, and up to 6 extra PDUs can carry over to the next period.
continuing_education.quote: You are required to complete 24 PDUs, which may be earned any time during your renewal period.

processing_time.value: The board reviews initial license applications within 30 days of submission.
processing_time.quote: Initial License applications are reviewed within 30 days from the submission date.

apply_url.value: Apply online through DCA BreEZe; the board page linked here has the link.
apply_url.quote: Submit the Initial License application for OT or OTA online via your BreEZe account.

board.value: Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology and Hearing Aid Dispensers Board
board.quote: Welcome to the Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology and Hearing Aid Dispensers Board

education.value: You need a master's degree or equivalent in speech-language pathology from an accredited educational institution, plus 300 hours of supervised clinical practicum in three different clinical settings.
education.quote: Hold a Master's degree or equivalent in speech-language pathology from an accredited educational institution.

national_exam.value: You must pass the ETS Praxis speech-language pathology exam with a minimum score of 162, taken within the last five years. Report your score to the board with code R8544.
national_exam.quote: pass the national speech-language pathology exam administered by the Educational Testing Service (ETS) Praxis Series with a minimum score of 162.

background_check.value: All applicants must pass a DOJ and FBI background check. California residents must use Live Scan; applicants outside California submit FD-258 fingerprint hard cards.
background_check.quote: The Board requires both a Department of Justice (DOJ) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) criminal history background check on all applicants for licensure or registration.

application_fee.value: The SLP application and license fee is $150. Applicants who already paid the $35 RPE temporary license application fee pay the remaining $115. A 6-month temporary license for out-of-state licensees costs $30.
application_fee.quote: Applicants who already paid a $35 RPE Application Fee only need to pay the remaining $115 towards the full $150 Application Fee.

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another state apply under the 'Licensed in Another State' pathway, which offers both a temporary and a full license application. Holders of a current ASHA CCC must use the Equivalent Qualifications pathway instead.
endorsement.quote: Must possess an active and current license from another state. If you also hold a current ASHA certification, you must use Option #2.

temporary_or_provisional.value: New graduates complete their Required Professional Experience (RPE) under an RPE temporary license: 36 weeks full-time or 72 weeks part-time. California also offers a one-time 6-month temporary license to SLPs who hold a current license in another state.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Have completed 36 weeks of full-time or 72 weeks of part-time supervised Required Professional Experience (RPE) while holding an RPE temporary license.

renewal.value: SLP licenses renew every 2 years, on the last day of your birth month.
renewal.quote: Speech-Language Pathologist 2 Years Last day of birth month

continuing_education.value: SLPs need 24 hours of continuing professional development per two-year renewal (12 hours for a first renewal). No more than 12 hours may be self-study, and no more than 6 hours may be indirect patient/client care.
continuing_education.quote: Speech-Language Pathologist or Audiologist 24 hours 12 hours 6 hours

compact.value: California is not among the states issuing ASLP-IC compact privileges. Registration is open only to practitioners licensed in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee and West Virginia.
compact.quote: Registration for compact privileges to practice is open for licensed practitioners in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, and West Virginia.

processing_time.value: The board asks applicants to allow at least four weeks from receipt for processing. Times may be longer in the peak season, about May through October.
processing_time.quote: Please allow at least four weeks from the date received for processing.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through the 'Application Package' links (DCA online forms) on the board's Speech-Language Pathologist applicant page, one per licensure pathway.
apply_url.quote: Application Package for Licensed in Another State (Full License)

board.value: Colorado State Physical Therapy Board
board.quote: Program Information Yukon Morford, Program Director State Physical Therapy Board 1560 Broadway, Suite 1350 Denver, CO 80202

education.value: Applicants must have completed a physical therapy program that is either accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency or determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent.
education.quote: An applicant is required to demonstrate that they have successfully completed a physical therapy program that is either

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) developed by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT), at the passing score set by FSBPT. Applicants by examination must graduate and pass the NPTE within the two years immediately preceding the application.
national_exam.quote: The examination developed by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) entitled the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) for physical therapists is approved as the required examination in the licensure process.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit fingerprints for a criminal history record check with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Colorado Bureau of Investigation.
background_check.quote: An applicant must submit fingerprints for the purpose of obtaining criminal history record information from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Colorado Bureau of Investigation

endorsement.value: Physical therapists who hold a current, unrestricted license in good standing in another jurisdiction may apply for licensure by endorsement, attesting to an accredited or substantially equivalent education and passage of the NPTE. They must also verify every license held and show at least one year of licensure in a jurisdiction with a substantially similar scope of practice.
endorsement.quote: An applicant who possesses a current and unrestricted license, in good standing, to practice physical therapy under the laws of another jurisdiction may apply for licensure by endorsement.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Colorado issues a provisional physical therapist license (applied for by the original method). All provisional physical therapist licenses expire 120 days after issuance and cannot be renewed.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: All Provisional Physical Therapist licenses expire 120 days after issuance and cannot be renewed.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses expire on October 31 of even-numbered years, and renewals open approximately 4-5 weeks before the expiration date.
renewal.quote: All Physical Therapist and Physical Therapist Assistant licenses expire on October 31 of even-numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least 30 professional development activity (PDA) hours during each 2-year license period, with at least 20 of them in educational coursework, fellowships or residencies. Continuing competency requirements begin after the first renewal of the license.
continuing_education.quote: Physical Therapists must complete at least 30 PDA during each 2-year license period. A minimum of 20 of the 30 required PDA hours must be completed in one or more of the following PDA categories

compact.value: Colorado participates in the PT Compact and compact privileges for Colorado can be purchased: the physical therapist compact privilege fee is $95 total ($50 state fee plus $45 Commission fee), and Colorado has no jurisprudence exam requirement.
compact.quote: Colorado PT Fees $95 Total CP Fee $50 State CP Fee $45 Commission CP Fee

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the Division of Professions and Occupations (DPO) Online Services system, linked from the board's Applications and Forms page.
apply_url.quote: There you can apply for an initial license, Reinstate an Expired license, Renew your license, update your contact information, review the progress of your application and much more.

board.value: Colorado Office of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: Program Information Zen Mayhugh, Program Director Office of Occupational Therapy 1560 Broadway, Suite 1350 Denver, CO 80202

education.value: Applicants must have completed an educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE), WFOT-approved education, or another program approved by the Director, plus the supervised fieldwork that program requires.
education.quote: An applicant for licensure must have successfully completed an educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT examination at the passing score set by NBCOT. To be licensed by examination, the passing score must have been achieved within two years immediately preceding the application.
national_exam.quote: The examination developed by NBCOT is approved. An applicant must achieve at least the passing score as determined by NBCOT in order to be eligible for licensure.

background_check.value: Applicants who must be fingerprinted submit fingerprints through an approved vendor (IdentoGO or American BioIdentity) for a state and national criminal history check by the CBI and FBI; the Division lists occupational therapists among the license types for fingerprint background checks.
background_check.quote: Some applicants for licensure must submit fingerprints for a background check to one of the approved vendors for processing by the Colorado Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed in a jurisdiction with substantially equivalent qualifications apply by endorsement; any jurisdiction that requires or accepts the NBCOT exam is deemed equivalent. Applicants must also show recent practice (at least 400 hours in a twelve month period within the prior two years), at least one year of licensure elsewhere, or otherwise maintained competency.
endorsement.quote: For purposes of this Rule, a jurisdiction that requires or accepts passage of the NBCOT examination shall be deemed to have qualifications substantially equivalent to those required in Colorado.

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Office of Occupational Therapy offers a provisional occupational therapist (OTP) initial application.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Occupational Therapy Assistant Provisional (OTAP): OTAP Initial Application Preview Occupational Therapist Provisional (OTP): OTP Initial Application Preview

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses expire on December 31 of even-numbered years and must be renewed to continue practicing; renewals open approximately 4-5 weeks before the expiration date.
renewal.quote: All Occupational Therapist and Occupational Therapy Assistant licenses expire on December 31 of even-numbered years and must be renewed to continue practicing.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete at least 24 professional development activity (PDA) hours during each 2-year license period, across at least two PDA categories. Continuing competency requirements begin after the first renewal of the license.
continuing_education.quote: You must complete at least 24 PDA during each 2-year license period. A licensee must complete the required 24 PDA through a minimum of two PDA categories

compact.value: Colorado is a member of the Occupational Therapy Compact but is not yet accepting OT Compact privilege applications; the Commission lists Colorado's jurisprudence requirement as not required.
compact.quote: Colorado Not Yet not required CO OT Practice Act TBD TBD $75

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the Division of Professions and Occupations (DPO) Online Services system, linked from the Office's Applications and Forms page.
apply_url.quote: There you can apply for an initial license, Reinstate an Expired license, Renew your license, update your contact information, review the progress of your application and much more.

board.value: Colorado Office of Speech-Language Pathology Certification
board.quote: Program Information Zen Mayhugh, Program Director Office of Speech-Language Pathology Certification 1560 Broadway, Suite 1350 Denver, CO 80202

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or higher degree in communication sciences and disorders from an accredited institution (a program accredited by ASHA's Council on Academic Accreditation is presumed to qualify) and must complete a speech-language pathology clinical fellowship approved by the Director or by ASHA.
education.quote: An applicant for certification must have successfully completed a master's or higher degree in communication sciences and disorders granted by an accredited institution of higher education recognized by the United States Department of Education.

national_exam.value: Applicants must have passed the national examination approved by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), an examination the Director finds substantially equivalent, or hold a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC).
national_exam.quote: Has passed an examination that, in the Director's determination, is substantially equivalent to the examination approved by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association

background_check.value: Applicants who must be fingerprinted submit fingerprints through an approved vendor (IdentoGO or American BioIdentity) for a state and national criminal history check by the CBI and FBI; the Division lists speech-language pathologists among the license types for fingerprint background checks.
background_check.quote: Some applicants for licensure must submit fingerprints for a background check to one of the approved vendors for processing by the Colorado Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

endorsement.value: Speech-language pathologists holding a current, valid license or certification in another jurisdiction may apply for certification by endorsement; those licensed elsewhere on the basis of a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence are deemed to meet the education and examination requirements.
endorsement.quote: An applicant who holds a current, valid license or certification as a speech-language pathologist in another jurisdiction or through the federal government

temporary_or_provisional.value: Colorado issues a provisional speech-language pathologist certificate to applicants who have the required degree and exam and attest to a written plan for completing a clinical fellowship. It expires no later than twenty-four months after issuance unless a one-time twelve month hardship extension is granted.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional speech-language pathologist certificate expires no later than twenty-four months from the date of issuance unless a one time twelve month extension is granted

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist certifications expire on November 30 of every year and must be renewed annually; renewals open approximately 4-5 weeks before the expiration date.
renewal.quote: All Speech-Language Pathologist certifications expire on November 30 of every year and must be renewed to continue practicing.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete at least 10 professional development activity (PDA) hours during each one-year certification period. Continuing competency requirements begin after the first renewal of the certification.
continuing_education.quote: You must complete at least 10 PDA during each one-year certification period.

compact.value: The ASLP-IC Commission lists Colorado as not yet accepting compact privilege applications, with no jurisprudence exam required (current as of May 28, 2026).
compact.quote: Colorado not yet not required CO Aud TBD $50

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the Division of Professions and Occupations (DPO) Online Services system, linked from the Office's Applications and Forms page.
apply_url.quote: There you can apply for an initial certification, Reinstate an Expired certification, Renew your certification, update your contact information, review the progress of your application and much more.

board.value: Connecticut State Board of Examiners for Physical Therapists
board.quote: Board of Examiners for Physical Therapists Meeting Agendas and Minutes Board Members Michael J. Parisi, PT (Chair)

education.value: Applicants must successfully complete a physical therapy program of study approved by the American Physical Therapy Association (APTA).
education.quote: Successful completion of a program of study approved by the American Physical Therapy Association

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy, with a criterion-referenced passing score.
national_exam.quote: administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy with a criterion-referenced passing score for the respective administration of the examination.

background_check.value: Applicants for physical therapist licensure must submit to a state and national fingerprint-based criminal history records check.
background_check.quote: The Commissioner of Public Health shall require each person applying for licensure as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant to submit to a state and national fingerprint-based criminal history records check

application_fee.value: The initial application fee for physical therapist licensure is $285.
application_fee.quote: A completed application with photograph and fee of $285.00.

endorsement.value: Applicants who hold a current license in at least one other U.S. jurisdiction, have practiced for at least four years and have all licenses in good standing may be licensed without transcripts, training verification or an examination.
endorsement.quote: Holds a current license, permit, certification or registration in at least one other jurisdiction in the United States in the occupation or profession applied for;

temporary_or_provisional.value: Recent graduates of APTA-accredited programs (or foreign graduates with a favorable FCCPT evaluation) may apply for a temporary permit to practice under the direct and immediate supervision of a Connecticut-licensed physical therapist, valid for 120 calendar days from the date of application. The permit is not renewable and becomes void if the applicant fails the examination.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The permit is valid for 120 calendar days from date of application.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses expire in the first birth month following issuance and are renewed annually thereafter, with a 90-day grace period after expiration.
renewal.quote: Most licenses expire in the first birth month following issuance and are renewable annually thereafter.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least twenty hours of continuing education in each twelve-month registration period, including at least two hours on screening for post-traumatic stress disorder, suicide risk, depression and grief and on suicide prevention during the first registration period in which continuing education is required and at least once every six years thereafter. First-time renewals are exempt.
continuing_education.quote: each physical therapist licensed pursuant to this chapter shall complete a minimum of twenty hours of continuing education during each registration period.

compact.value: Connecticut is a PT Compact member state: physical therapists fully licensed in another compact state can purchase a compact privilege to work in Connecticut, bought directly from the Compact rather than the state.
compact.quote: Physical Therapists and Physical Therapist Assistants who are fully licensed in another state and have purchased the ability to work in Connecticut.

processing_time.value: Once an application is complete, the Department of Public Health makes an eligibility determination within three to four weeks and notifies the applicant.
processing_time.quote: This determination will be made within three to four weeks and the applicant will be notified with regard to the determination.

apply_url.value: Applications are accepted online only, through the link on the Department of Public Health's physical therapist licensing requirements page.
apply_url.quote: Applications are only accepted online. Please select this link to apply online

board.value: Connecticut Department of Public Health (Practitioner Licensing and Investigations Section)
board.quote: All supporting documents should be mailed directly from the source to: Connecticut Department of Public Health Occupational Therapist Licensure

education.value: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree in occupational therapy from a program accredited by the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA) and complete at least 24 weeks of supervised fieldwork.
education.quote: Hold a baccalaureate degree in occupational therapy from a program accredited by the American Occupational Therapy Association

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) certification examination.
national_exam.quote: Successfully completed the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

background_check.value: The Department of Public Health reviews applicants with criminal or disciplinary backgrounds individually and has authority to deny licensure to anyone who has committed or been found guilty of committing a felony.
background_check.quote: the Department has the authority to deny licensure to an individual who has committed or been found guilty of committing a felony

application_fee.value: The initial application fee for occupational therapist licensure is $200.
application_fee.quote: A complete application with photo and fee of $200.00.

endorsement.value: Applicants who hold a current license in at least one other U.S. jurisdiction, have practiced for at least four years and have all licenses in good standing may be licensed without transcripts, training verification or an examination.
endorsement.quote: Holds a current license, permit, certification or registration in at least one other jurisdiction in the United States in the occupation or profession applied for;

temporary_or_provisional.value: Recent graduates of AOTA-accredited programs (or equivalent programs outside the United States) may apply for a temporary permit to practice under the direct and immediate supervision of a Connecticut-licensed occupational therapist, valid for 120 calendar days from the date of application, with a $50 fee. The permit is not renewable and becomes void if the applicant fails the examination.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The permit is valid for 120 calendar days from date of application. Temporary permits are not renewable

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses renew biennially and expire on July 31 of odd-numbered years.
renewal.quote: License expires biennially on July 31 of odd numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete at least 24 contact hours of qualifying continued competency activity in the two-year period before renewal, with a contact hour defined as at least 50 minutes. First-time renewals are exempt.
continuing_education.quote: each licensee applying for license renewal shall complete a minimum of 24 contact hours of qualifying continued competency activity during the preceding two-year period for which the license is being renewed.

processing_time.value: Once an application is complete, the Department of Public Health makes an eligibility determination within three to four weeks and notifies the applicant.

apply_url.value: Applications are accepted online only, through the link on the Department of Public Health's occupational therapist licensure requirements page.
apply_url.quote: Applications are only accepted online. Please select this link to apply online.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NTE Specialty Area Test in speech and language pathology administered by ETS, with a scaled score of 162 for exams taken on or after September 1, 2014. The exam may be waived for holders of a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence.
national_exam.quote: For examinations administered on and after September 1, 2014, the passing score for Connecticut licensure is a scaled score of 162.

background_check.value: The Department of Public Health reviews applicants with criminal or disciplinary backgrounds individually and has authority to deny licensure to anyone who has committed or been found guilty of committing a felony.

application_fee.value: The application fee for speech and language pathologist licensure is $200.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants must complete a Supervised Professional Experience (SPE) of at least 36 weeks and 1,080 hours full-time or 48 weeks and 1,440 hours part-time under a licensed speech and language pathologist; an SPE in Connecticut requires prior Department approval through an application with a $200 fee.

renewal.quote: Most licenses expire in the first birth month following issuance and are renewable annually thereafter.

continuing_education.value: Speech and language pathologists must complete at least 20 hours of qualifying continuing education within the preceding twenty-four-month period before renewal, with content accepted by ASHA or offered by other listed providers. First-time renewals are exempt.

board.value: Examining Board of Physical Therapists and Athletic Trainers
