education.value: U.S.-educated applicants must have an official transcript showing a physical therapy degree from a school accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE); a transitional DPT degree is not accepted, and foreign-educated applicants need a credential evaluation.
education.quote: The school must be accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE).

national_exam.value: Physical therapists must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE); the passing score is 600, the criterion-referenced score set by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy.
national_exam.quote: For licensure as a Physical Therapist or Physical Therapist Assistant, you must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE). The passing score is 600

state_exam.value: Delaware does not require an examination on Delaware law and regulations for physical therapist licensure, and the TOEFL is not required.
state_exam.quote: There is no examination on Delaware law and regulations, and the TOEFL is not required.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a new State of Delaware and FBI fingerprint-based criminal background check; checks completed for any other purpose, such as employment or licensure in other states, are not accepted.
background_check.quote: Criminal background checks completed for any other purpose (e.g., employment, licensure in other states) will not meet this requirement

application_fee.value: The Physical Therapist license application fee is $193, and the temporary license application fee is $40.
application_fee.quote: Physical Therapist $193 Physical Therapist Reinstatement $290 Temporary (All Types) $40

endorsement.value: Physical therapists already licensed in another jurisdiction apply by reciprocity, having their national exam scores sent from their original state of licensure or FSBPT and proving completion of two hours of ethics training related to physical therapy practice.
endorsement.quote: Proof that you have completed two hours of training in ethics related to the practice of physical therapy.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants awaiting the NPTE who have been offered a job in Delaware may get a temporary license, good for 90 days, and must work under direct supervision; it expires immediately if the applicant fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: You may apply for a temporary license only if you are offered a job in Delaware. The temporary license is good for 90 days.

required_courses.value: All physical therapist applicants must hold current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) certification, and online CPR courses are not accepted.
required_courses.quote: Current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) certification. Online courses are not accepted

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses must be renewed in DELPROS every two years and expire on January 31 of odd-numbered years.
renewal.quote: Licenses expire on January 31 of odd years (e.g., 2017, 2019).

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists generally must complete 3.0 continuing education units (CEUs) every two years, including 0.2 units (two hours) of ethics and a CPR course that counts for 0.1 unit; the first renewal is prorated.
continuing_education.quote: Generally, you are required to complete 3.0 continuing education units (CEUs) to renew your license every two years. Your CEUs for each renewal must include 0.2 units (two hours) of ethics

compact.value: Delaware is listed as a member state of the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact, and the PT Compact Commission lists its 38 member states as actively issuing and accepting compact privileges.
compact.quote: Compact Privilege Availability 38 Member States Actively Issuing and Accepting Compact Privileges

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through DELPROS (Delaware Professional Regulation Online Services), which requires a DELPROS user account.
apply_url.quote: In order to apply for a license or submit a service request, you must first have a DELPROS user account.

board.value: Board of Occupational Therapy Practice
board.quote: The primary objective of the Delaware Board of Occupational Therapy Practice is to protect the public from unsafe practices

education.value: Examination applicants must have an official transcript sent directly from a school accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE), and the transcript should show fieldwork experience.
education.quote: Your school must be accredited by Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE).

national_exam.value: Applicants must achieve the passing score on the written standardized examination developed by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a new State of Delaware and FBI fingerprint-based criminal background check; checks completed for any other purpose, such as employment or licensure in other states, are not accepted.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 24 hours of approved continuing education during each full renewal period (August 1 to July 31 of even-numbered years); the first renewal is prorated.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through DELPROS (Delaware Professional Regulation Online Services), which requires a DELPROS user account.

board.value: Board of Speech Pathologists, Audiologists, and Hearing Aid Dispensers

education.quote: The transcript must show that you earned at least a master’s degree or its equivalent with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology

national_exam.value: Speech-language pathologists must pass the national examination; temporary licensees are expected to complete the Clinical Fellowship and pass the national examination during the one-year temporary license.
national_exam.quote: The temporary license is good for one year, during which you should complete your Clinical Fellowship (CF) and pass the national examination.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a new State of Delaware and FBI fingerprint-based criminal background check; checks completed for any other purpose, such as employment or licensure in other states, are not accepted.
background_check.quote: Criminal background checks completed for any other purpose (e.g., employment, licensure in other states) will not meet this requirement

application_fee.value: The Speech/Language Pathologist license application fee is $175, and the temporary license application fee is $65.
application_fee.quote: Speech/Language Pathologist $175 Speech/Language Pathology Assistant $175 Temporary (All Types) $65

endorsement.value: SLPs holding current ASHA CCC-SLP certification apply by certification even if licensed elsewhere; those with an active license in another jurisdiction who lack the CCC but completed a clinical fellowship apply by reciprocity.
endorsement.quote: when you hold an active license in another jurisdiction AND do not hold current CCC-SLP ASHA certification but completed your CF.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Graduates who must complete the ASHA Clinical Fellowship need a temporary license, valid one year and extendable up to 3 times for a maximum of 48 months, with Board approval.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Your temporary license can be extended up to 3 times for maximum of 48 months.

renewal.value: Speech/Language Pathologist licenses must be renewed in DELPROS every two years and expire on July 31 of odd-numbered years.
renewal.quote: Speech/Language Pathologist, Speech/Language Pathology Assistant, Audiology and Hearing Aid Dispenser licenses expire on July 31 of odd years (e.g., 2017, 2019).

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete 30 hours of approved continuing education during each full renewal period; the first renewal is prorated.

national_exam.value: Applicants for licensure by examination must pass a Board-approved national licensure examination in physical therapy; the passing score is set by the body administering the exam.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the District of Columbia Jurisprudence Examination, registering online through FSBPT and uploading the registration confirmation with the application.

endorsement.quote: All states and jurisdictions in which you have EVER held a professional license, regardless of status must be submitted.

temporary_or_provisional.value: An eligible applicant with an active application on file may work under supervised practice, once a Board representative signs the supervised practice form, for a maximum of 90 days; the form is issued only one time.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: an eligible applicant may work under supervised practice from the date of signature on this form by an authorized representative for the Board of Physical Therapy for a maximum of 90 days.

renewal.quote: Please note the license will expire on the last day of your birthday month.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 40 hours of continuing education per renewal, including 2 hours in LGBTQ topics and 10% (4 hours) in public health priorities, with half of the hours in live programs; first-time renewals are exempt.

application_fee.value: The application and license fee is $264, paid online with the application.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed in another state apply by endorsement, submitting official license verifications from every state where they have ever held a license and an NBCOT certification verification letter.
endorsement.quote: All states and jurisdictions in which you have EVER held a professional license, regardless of status must be submitted.

temporary_or_provisional.value: An eligible applicant with an application on file may work under supervised practice from the date a Board representative signs the supervised practice form until the 60-day application file period expires; the form is issued only one time.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Applications for licensure are kept on file for no more than sixty (60) days and thus an eligible applicant may work under supervised practice

renewal.value: Licenses are on a birth-month renewal cycle: credentials issued on or after June 16, 2024 expire on the last day of the holder's birth month, with renewals in odd or even years matching the birth year.

continuing_education.quote: Two (2) hours of CEUs of the twenty-four (24) for Occupational Therapy applications are required in cultural competence and appropriate clinical treatment

endorsement.quote: All states and jurisdictions in which you have EVER held a professional license, regardless of status must be submitted.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Speech-language pathology clinical fellows apply for a separate Clinical Fellow license, which requires a master's degree or higher in speech-language pathology or a related field and a $210 application and license fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Payment (Fee) (ONLINE) $210 (USD) for Application and License Fee.

board.value: Florida Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: Welcome to the State of Florida's Online Resource for Physical Therapist and Physical Therapist Assistant Licensure, Renewal and Information.

education.value: A physical therapy degree from a program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE). Foreign-trained applicants need a credential evaluation showing equivalent education.
education.quote: Applicants must have received a degree as a physical therapist from an institution that has been approved for the training of physical therapists by the Commission on Accreditation for Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE).

national_exam.value: The National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT); scores must be transferred from FSBPT to the board. The NPTE fee to FSBPT is $485.
national_exam.quote: If you have passed the NPTE, you must have your score report transferred from the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT)

state_exam.value: Yes. Exam applicants must also pass the Florida Laws and Rules exam, registered through FSBPT ($65 fee to FSBPT). Passing it is also a requirement for the PT temporary permit.
state_exam.quote: Applicants must register with the FSBPT for the NPTE and the Florida laws and rules exam.

background_check.value: Required. Applicants must submit electronic fingerprints through an FDLE-approved Livescan provider for a Florida and national criminal history check; the applicant pays the cost.
background_check.quote: Florida passed House Bill 975 following the 2024 legislative session, which requires this profession to complete electronic fingerprinting.

application_fee.value: $180 application and licensing fee to the Board of Physical Therapy. Exam applicants also pay FSBPT $485 for the NPTE and $65 for the Florida Laws and Rules exam, plus Prometric fees; endorsement applicants pay FSBPT a $90 score transfer fee.
application_fee.quote: $180.00 Application and Licensing Fee to Board of Physical Therapy

endorsement.value: Through the MOBILE Endorsement pathway (s. 456.0145, F.S.): an active, unencumbered license in another U.S. jurisdiction, a passing national exam score, at least two years of active practice in the last four, and no recent discipline. Applicants request license verification from each state and an NPTE score transfer from FSBPT.
endorsement.quote: Must have actively practiced the profession for at least two years during the four-year period immediately preceding the date of submission of this application.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A temporary permit is available to graduates of approved U.S. programs who have not yet passed the NPTE. They must pass the Florida Laws and Rules Examination, carry malpractice insurance, and work under the direct supervision of a licensed PT. The permit is valid for six months from graduation.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Temporary permits are valid for six months from the date of graduation.

required_courses.value: A 1-hour HIV/AIDS course is required at the first renewal only, not before initial licensure. Every renewal also requires a 2-hour Prevention of Medical Errors course.
required_courses.quote: HIV/AIDS course required for first renewal only and are accepted if approved by any Board within the Division of Medical Quality Assurance

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years (biennially). Current PT licenses expire at midnight Eastern Time on November 30, 2027.
renewal.quote: Current licenses expire at midnight, Eastern Time, on November 30, 2027

continuing_education.value: 24 contact hours per two-year cycle, including 2 hours of Prevention of Medical Errors each renewal (plus 1 hour of HIV/AIDS at the first renewal). No more than 12 hours may be home study. Licenses issued in the second half of the cycle need only the Medical Errors and HIV/AIDS hours.
continuing_education.quote: Twenty-four (24) contact hours of continuing education (CE/CEU*) must be completed within the current biennium for which the license is being renewed.

compact.value: Florida is not a PT Compact member. Florida passed a compact law (SB 7016), but the Compact Commission found that it conflicts with the model statute, so Florida PTs cannot get compact privileges and other states' PTs cannot use compact privileges in Florida.
compact.quote: As a result of this determination, Florida is deemed ineligible for Compact membership and shall not be entitled to any of the rights, privileges, or benefits of a Member State

processing_time.value: The board says to allow up to 10 business days for initial review of a new application. Under Florida law, initial review must happen within 30 days, and a MOBILE endorsement license is issued within 7 days after all requirements are met.
processing_time.quote: Please allow up to 10 business days for initial review of new applications.

apply_url.value: Apply online through the Florida Department of Health MQA Online Services Portal (create a new applicant account).
apply_url.quote: NOTE: Not all mobile devices are fully compatible with the online system at this time.

board.value: Florida Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: Welcome to the State of Florida's Online Resource for Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants Licensing, Renewals and Information.

education.value: Graduation from an occupational therapy program accredited through the American Occupational Therapy Association, plus 24 weeks of supervised fieldwork.
education.quote: Have graduated from an accredited occupational therapy program accredited by the American Occupational Therapy Association

national_exam.value: The NBCOT certification exam for occupational therapists. Candidates apply to NBCOT directly; the Florida board does not give the exam.
national_exam.quote: Have passed an examination approved by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) for occupational therapists.

background_check.value: Required. OT applicants must complete electronic fingerprinting (Livescan) for a background screening before the application can be approved.
background_check.quote: Florida passed House Bill 975 following the 2024 legislative session, which requires this profession to complete electronic fingerprinting.

application_fee.value: $180 total due with the application: a $100 non-refundable application fee, a $75 initial license fee and a $5 unlicensed activity fee. The fee is the same for exam and MOBILE endorsement applicants.
application_fee.quote: You may submit your State of Florida licensure application and $180 application fee ONLINE -or- mail in your application and fee

endorsement.value: Through the MOBILE Endorsement pathway (s. 456.0145, F.S.): an active, unencumbered OT license in another U.S. jurisdiction, NBCOT exam passage or current certification, at least two years of active practice in the last four, and no recent discipline. Applicants request license verification from each state where they were licensed.
endorsement.quote: Must have actively practiced the profession for at least two years during the four-year period immediately preceding the date of submission of this application.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Florida law allows (but does not require) the board to issue a temporary permit to an applicant who meets all other requirements and is registered for the next exam. The permit lets them practice under a licensed OT's supervision until exam results arrive. The board's website does not describe an application for it.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: the board may issue the applicant a temporary permit allowing her or him to practice occupational therapy under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist until notification of the results of the examination

required_courses.value: A 1-hour HIV/AIDS course is required at the first renewal only (not before initial licensure), along with 2 hours of Prevention of Medical Errors from a Florida OT Board approved provider.
required_courses.quote: For the HIV/AIDS course this is a first renewal only requirement, and any course approved by any of the professions regulated within the Department of Health

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years (biennially). Current OT licenses expire at midnight Eastern Time on February 28, 2027.
renewal.quote: Current licenses expire at midnight, Eastern Time, on February 28, 2027

continuing_education.value: 26 hours per two-year cycle: 22 general hours, 2 hours of Prevention of Medical Errors and 2 hours of Florida Laws and Rules (both from board-approved providers), plus 1 hour of HIV/AIDS at the first renewal. At least 14 hours must be live; no more than 12 may be home study.
continuing_education.quote: are required to complete all 26 as stated above, including the HIV/AIDS 1 hour (for first renewal only) requirement.

processing_time.value: For MOBILE endorsement applications, the board says to allow up to 5 business days for initial review. Under Florida law, initial review must happen within 30 days, and the license is issued within 7 days after all requirements are met.
processing_time.quote: Please allow up to 5 business days for initial review of new applications.

apply_url.value: Apply online through the Florida Department of Health MQA Online Services Portal (create a new applicant account).
apply_url.quote: NOTE: Not all mobile devices are fully compatible with the online system at this time.

board.value: Florida Board of Speech-Language Pathology & Audiology
board.quote: Welcome to the State of Florida's Online Resource for Speech-Language Pathologists & Audiologists Licensure, Renewal and Information.

education.value: A master's degree, or completion of the academic requirements of a doctoral program, with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology. Also required: 300 clock hours of supervised clinical experience (at least 200 in speech-language pathology) and nine months of professional employment experience.
education.quote: Master’s degree or completion of the academic requirements of a doctoral program, with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology

national_exam.value: The Praxis exam in speech-language pathology (ETS), passed no more than three years before the application date. ETS must send the official score report directly to the board. The board page does not state a passing score.
national_exam.quote: Proof of passing the Praxis exam no more than three (3) years prior to the date of this application

background_check.value: Required. SLP applicants must complete electronic fingerprinting (Livescan) for a background screening before the application can be approved.
background_check.quote: Florida passed House Bill 975 following the 2024 legislative session, which requires this profession to complete electronic fingerprinting.

application_fee.value: $75 non-refundable application fee. The full license totals $280 ($75 + $200 license fee + $5) if issued Aug 1 of an odd year through Dec 31 of an even year, or $180 ($75 + $100 + $5) if issued Jan 1 through Jul 31 of an odd year. The provisional license totals $180, including the $75 fee.
application_fee.quote: $180.00 (includes a $75.00 non-refundable application processing fee)

endorsement.value: Through the MOBILE Endorsement pathway (s. 456.0145, F.S.): an active, unencumbered license in another U.S. jurisdiction, a passing national exam score, at least two years of active practice in the last four, no National Practitioner Data Bank report, and no recent discipline.
endorsement.quote: Must have actively practiced the profession for at least two years during the four-year period immediately preceding the date of submission of this application.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who cannot yet document nine months of supervised professional employment experience and a passing Praxis score (for example, clinical fellows) must hold a provisional license before starting that experience.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license shall be required of all applicants for a license in speech-language pathology who cannot document a minimum of 9 months of supervised professional employment experience and a passing score on the national examination.

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years and are due by December 31 of each odd-numbered year. Current licenses expire at midnight Eastern Time on December 31, 2027.
renewal.quote: Licenses are renewable by December 31st of each odd year.

continuing_education.value: 30 hours per two-year cycle: 18 clinically related hours, 10 general hours (which may also be clinical) and a 2-hour Prevention of Medical Errors course approved by the board. First-time renewers licensed after July 1 of an odd year are exempt.
continuing_education.quote: complete 30 credit hours, 18 of which shall be clinically related, 10 non clinical hours and a 2 hour course relating to the prevention of medical errors

compact.value: Florida has joined the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact (ASLP-IC) through SB 7016 (2024). The board says privileges to practice will become available once the commission is operational and member states are connected to the compact's data system.
compact.quote: Florida joined the ASLP-IC as the 30th member state upon the passage of Senate Bill 7016 during the 2024 legislative session.

processing_time.value: Once the application is complete, the license is issued within 4 to 7 working days. Under Florida law, initial review must happen within 30 days.
processing_time.quote: Once the application has been deemed complete, a license is issued within 4-7 working days.

apply_url.value: Apply online through the Florida Department of Health MQA Online Services Portal (create a new applicant account).
apply_url.quote: NOTE: Not all mobile devices are fully compatible with the online system at this time.

board.value: Georgia State Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: Georgia State Board of Physical Therapy For Georgia Physical Therapists, Physical Therapists Assistants and prospective applicants.

education.value: Applicants must be graduates of an educational program accredited by a recognized accrediting agency and approved by the board; the board notes that CAPTE does not accredit transitional DPT or post-professional programs.
education.quote: requires that all applicants be graduates of an educational program which is accredited by a recognized accrediting agency and approved by the board

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE); scores range from 200 to 800 and the minimum passing score is 600 for both PTs and PTAs.
national_exam.quote: Scoring for the NPTE ranges from 200 - 800. The minimum passing score is 600 for both PT and PTA.

state_exam.value: All PT and PTA license applicants must pass the computer-based Georgia Jurisprudence Assessment Module (GA JAM) by answering 80% of the questions correctly.
state_exam.quote: Applicants must answer 80% of the questions correctly to pass the GA Jurisprudence Exam (GA JAM).

endorsement.value: The Board may license a PT from another state without examination by reciprocity; CAPTE graduates must provide verification of an active license in good standing, active practice in the two years before applying or 26 hours of continuing education, NPTE scores and passing Georgia Ethics and Jurisprudence Examination scores.
endorsement.quote: Verification of active practice in the two years immediately preceding the date of application; or proof of completion of 26 hours of acceptable continuing education coursework

temporary_or_provisional.value: Georgia issues training permits for supervised traineeships to qualified applicants, such as graduates who have passed the national exam and the Georgia laws and rules exam, and reinstatement or endorsement applicants who have not practiced for two or more years; a 480-hour traineeship must be completed within three months.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Graduates of entry-level programs for physical therapists or physical therapist assistants from either a CAPTE or a non-CAPTE-accredited school who have taken and passed the national licensing examination

renewal.value: Licenses must be renewed every two years by December 31 of odd-numbered years, with proof of continuing competency and the renewal fee; licenses not renewed on time are assessed a late fee.
renewal.quote: shall biennially apply to the Board for renewal of his/her license, submit proof of continuing competency requirements and pay a renewal fee by December 31st of odd years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 30 hours of continuing competence per two-year renewal period, including at least 4 contact hours in Georgia Ethics and Jurisprudence (or passing the Georgia Ethics and Jurisprudence Examination), with no more than 10 hours credited per calendar day.
continuing_education.quote: hours of continuing competence per biennium shall include a minimum of four (4) contact hours specifically in Georgia Ethics and Jurisprudence as defined in the Georgia Physical Therapy Act

compact.value: Georgia participates in the PT Compact and issues compact privileges to practice in Georgia; applicants must pay the required fees and pass the Georgia Jurisprudence Assessment Module (GA-JAM) before the privilege is issued.
compact.quote: Individuals applying for a compact privilege to Georgia must pay the necessary fees and take and pass the Georgia Jurisprudence Assessment Module (GA-JAM) prior to issuance of the compact privilege

processing_time.value: Individual application documents are generally reviewed within 15 business days of receipt, and the full review can take up to 25 business days if staff find deficiencies.
processing_time.quote: Individual application documents are generally reviewed/processed within 15 business days according to the date which they were received. As a result, it may take up to 25 business days

national_exam.value: All OT and OTA applicants must pass the national examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), with the passing score set by NBCOT.
national_exam.quote: All applicants for licensure as occupational therapists and occupational therapy assistants are required to pass the nationally recognized examination administered by National Board of Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT)

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have met every licensure requirement except the exam may receive a 90-day limited permit to practice under the supervision of a Georgia-licensed OT; limited permits are not renewable and must be surrendered if the applicant fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: all requirements for licensure have been met except for the examination, a ninety (90) day limited permit shall be issued and shall allow the applicant to practice occupational therapy under the supervision

renewal.value: Licenses expire on March 31 of even-numbered years and are renewed every two years by application and fee; late renewal is available April 1 through April 30 with a late fee, after which the license is revoked by operation of law.
renewal.quote: A license issued by the Board shall expire on March 31st of even numbered years. The license may be renewed upon submission of the renewal application and payment of the required fee

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 24 continuing education hours each two-year renewal period, including at least 12 hours on direct patient care through live or real-time interactive formats and at least 2 hours in occupational therapy ethics; the Board has approved CE Broker for recording CE.
continuing_education.quote: Each licensee must complete a minimum of two (2) hours of the required twenty-four (24) continuing education hours in the ethics of occupational therapy practice.

board.value: State Board of Examiners of Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensing
board.quote: Information for Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensing licensees, applicants, and stakeholders.

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or higher degree with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology from an accredited program, with 75 semester hours of academic credit and 375 clock hours of supervised clinical practicum plus 25 hours of observation.
education.quote: The applicant shall submit certified evidence of completion of 375 clock hours of directly supervised clinical practicum, and 25 clock hours of observation with cases representative of a wide spectrum of ages and communicative disorders.

endorsement.value: SLPs who hold a license in another jurisdiction or ASHA's Certificate of Clinical Competence may apply for a Georgia license without examination if they meet Georgia's eligibility requirements; the Board compares the other jurisdiction's licensure law with Georgia's.
endorsement.quote: A person who holds a license in another jurisdiction or holds a Certificate of Clinical Competence as issued by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows must obtain Board approval and a Paid Clinical Experience (PCE) provisional license before starting the PCE, which requires at least 36 weeks of full-time employment of at least 30 hours per week; the provisional license is valid for one year.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The PCE/RPE applicant may not begin the PCE/RPE until Board approval is received and provisional license number issued.

renewal.value: Full SLP licenses expire on March 31 of odd-numbered years, and the renewal application, biennial renewal fee and continuing education documentation are due by that date.
renewal.quote: All full licenses shall expire on March 31 of odd numbered years. (b) Application, biennial renewal fee (See Fee Schedule) and documentation of continuing education must be received by March 31 of odd numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn at least 2.0 CEUs (20 clock hours) of continuing education per two-year licensure period, with no more than 1.0 CEU (10 clock hours) in any 24-hour period.
continuing_education.quote: In order to renew a license, the licensee must obtain a minimum of 2.0 CEUs (20 clock hours) during each biennium period of licensure.

board.value: Hawaii Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The official Board of Physical Therapy, together with its schedule of meetings and meeting minutes

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from a physical therapy program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE); graduates of non-CAPTE programs outside the U.S. must submit a credentials evaluation from a board-approved service showing equivalent education.
education.quote: Graduated from a Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE) accredited physical therapy program.

national_exam.value: Applicants must take and pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE); exam registration is handled through the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) after the Board confirms eligibility.
national_exam.quote: all applicants must provide proof of taking and passing the physical therapist licensure examination.

background_check.value: The application asks whether the applicant has ever been convicted of a crime that has not been annulled or expunged; applicants with a conviction must submit a signed explanation, court records and a current criminal history record check.
background_check.quote: Have you ever been convicted of a crime in any jurisdiction that has not been annulled or expunged?

application_fee.value: Applicants for licensure by exam submit a $50 non-refundable application fee, with license fees assessed after passing the exam; exam-waiver applicants pay $300 if licensed in an odd-numbered year or $185 if licensed in an even-numbered year.
application_fee.quote: If you are applying for a license through exam, submit the $50 non-refundable application fee.

endorsement.value: Hawaii does not reciprocate with other states; physical therapists who already passed the NPTE may apply for licensure through the exam waiver provision, having the FSBPT Score Transfer Service send their scores and each state of licensure send a license verification directly to the Board.
endorsement.quote: Hawaii does not reciprocate with any other state or country.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants for a permanent license may obtain one temporary license by submitting a Statement of Supervising Licensed Physical Therapist and an additional $50 fee; it expires within six months of its effective date or earlier, including on failure to pass the NPTE.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Only one temporary license will be issued per applicant. A temporary license shall expire within six months of its effective date

renewal.value: All physical therapist licenses must be renewed by December 31 of every even-numbered year; the on-time renewal fee for an active physical therapist license is $230.
renewal.quote: All licenses regardless of issuance date, are subject to renewal by December 31, every even-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists with active licenses must complete at least 30 continuing competence units per two-year renewal period, including at least 24 in professional practice or patient/client management, 2 in Hawaii ethics, laws and rules (jurisprudence) approved by the Board, and 4 in life support.
continuing_education.quote: each physical therapist with an active Hawaii license is required to obtain at least thirty (30) units of approved continuing competence units

compact.value: Hawaii is listed as a non-member state of the Physical Therapy Compact, so compact privileges are not available for practice in Hawaii.
compact.quote: Non-Members (10) California Florida Hawaii Idaho Minnesota New Mexico New York

apply_url.value: Physical therapist application forms, requirements and instructions are posted on the Board's Application Forms and Publications page; an application is abandoned if the license process is not completed within one year of filing.
apply_url.quote: Your application shall be considered abandoned, will be destroyed, if you fail to complete the license process within one year after filing the application

board.value: Hawaii Occupational Therapy Program
board.quote: There is established an occupational therapy program within the department to be administered by the director.

education.value: Occupational therapists must have completed the educational requirements and supervised field work experience required for certification by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).
education.quote: occupational therapists shall have completed the educational requirements and supervised field work experience required for certification by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

national_exam.value: Applicants must have passed the national certification examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).
national_exam.quote: shall have passed a national certification examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

background_check.value: The application asks whether the applicant has ever been convicted of a crime that has not been annulled or expunged; applicants with a conviction must submit a signed explanation, court records and a criminal history record check dated within six months.
background_check.quote: Have you ever been convicted of a crime in any jurisdiction that has not been annulled or expunged?

application_fee.value: The application fee is $50 and is not refundable; total initial fees are $279 if the license is issued in an odd-numbered year or $186 if issued in an even-numbered year.
application_fee.quote: (Application Fee - $50* + License Fee - $86 + Compliance Resolution Fund - $50)

temporary_or_provisional.value: Hawaii offers a temporary military spouse license for occupational therapists, allowing practice for the duration of the active-duty military member's service in Hawaii.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Temporary license to practice for the duration of the active-duty military member

renewal.value: All occupational therapist licenses must be renewed by December 31 of every even-numbered year; the on-time renewal fee for an active occupational therapist license is $186.
renewal.quote: All Licenses regardless of issuance date, are subject to renewal by December 31 of every even-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: The program's FAQ states there are no continuing education requirements for occupational therapist license renewal.
continuing_education.quote: No, there are no CE requirements for renewal.

processing_time.value: The program states it takes approximately 15 to 20 business days to process an application for completeness, after which a license may be issued if there are no deficiencies.
processing_time.quote: It takes approximately 15 to 20 business days to process an application for completeness

apply_url.value: Occupational therapist application forms and requirements are posted on the program's Application Forms and Publications page; an application is abandoned if the license process is not completed within one year of filing.
apply_url.quote: Your application shall be considered abandoned, will be destroyed, if you fail to complete the license process within one year after filing the application

board.value: Hawaii Board of Speech Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The official Board of Speech Pathology and Audiology, together with its schedule of meetings and meeting minutes

education.value: Applicants must graduate from an accredited college or university and be eligible for the ASHA certificate of clinical competence, including three hundred seventy-five hours of supervised clinical observation and practicum and a clinical fellowship of at least thirty-six weeks of full-time experience or its part-time equivalent.
education.quote: A minimum of three hundred seventy-five hours of supervised clinical observation and clinical practicum with individuals who present a variety of communication disorders

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis examination in speech-language pathology administered by ETS, with the passing score set by ASHA's Council for Clinical Certification.
national_exam.quote: also known as the Praxis examination in Speech-Language pathology and the Praxis examination in Audiology

background_check.value: The application asks whether the applicant has ever been convicted of a crime that has not been annulled or expunged; applicants with a conviction must submit a signed explanation, court records and affidavits attesting to rehabilitation.
background_check.quote: Have you ever been convicted of a crime in any jurisdiction that has not been annulled or expunged?

application_fee.value: The application fee is $50 and is not refundable; total initial fees are $264 if the license is issued in an even-numbered year or $176 if issued in an odd-numbered year, and a provisional license costs $226.
application_fee.quote: (Application - $50**, License - $76, Compliance Resolution Fund - $50)

endorsement.value: Hawaii offers no reciprocity for out-of-state licenses; speech pathologists holding the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence may apply for licensure by ASHA certification, with an ASHA verification letter dated within six months sent directly to the Board.
endorsement.quote: Be further advised there is no reciprocity or recognition of an Audiologist or Speech Pathologist license from another state to bypass these requirements for permanent licensure.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Speech pathologists with at least a master's degree may obtain a provisional license to complete licensure requirements under supervision of a licensed, ASHA-certified speech pathologist; it is valid for one year and may be renewed for one additional one-year period.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license shall be valid for one (1) year from the date of issuance and may be renewed for an additional one-year

renewal.value: All speech pathologist licenses must be renewed by December 31 of every odd-numbered year; the on-time renewal fee is $176.
renewal.quote: All Licenses regardless of issuance date, are subject to renewal by December 31 of every odd-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: The Board's FAQ states there are no continuing education requirements for speech pathologist license renewal.
continuing_education.quote: No, there are no CE requirements for renewal.

processing_time.value: The Board states it takes approximately 15 to 20 business days to process an application for completeness, after which a license may be issued if there are no deficiencies.
processing_time.quote: It takes approximately 15 to 20 business days to process an application for completeness

apply_url.value: Speech pathologist application forms (by examination, provisional, ASHA certification, temporary services) are posted on the Board's Application Forms and Publications page; an application is abandoned if not completed within one year of filing.
apply_url.quote: Your application shall be considered abandoned, will be destroyed, if you fail to complete the license process within one year after filing the application

board.value: Idaho Physical Therapy Licensure Board
board.quote: The Idaho Physical Therapy Licensure Board has reviewed the Physical Therapy Compact

education.value: Applicants must provide proof of graduation from a nationally accredited physical therapy school with a curriculum acceptable to the board.
education.quote: which shall require proof of graduation from a nationally accredited school, with a curriculum acceptable to the board, for physical therapists or physical therapist assistants

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) with a scaled score of at least 600. Candidates may sit for the NPTE no more than 90 days before their official graduation date, after first applying to the board.
national_exam.quote: Board requires submission of proof that the individual has successfully passed the NPTE with a scaled score of at least six hundred (600).

background_check.value: Applicants must disclose on the application any criminal conviction or charge other than minor traffic infractions, any professional disciplinary action, and any denial of licensure by another state.
background_check.quote: The application shall also require the disclosure of any criminal conviction or charge against the applicant other than minor traffic infractions

application_fee.value: Physical therapist applicants pay a $25 application fee and a $50 initial license fee.
application_fee.quote: Physical Therapist $50 $25 $50 Physical Therapist Assistant $40 $20 $40 Application Fee : $25

endorsement.value: A physical therapist licensed in good standing in another state or territory who passed a substantially similar exam and meets Idaho's education and conviction requirements is entitled to licensure without examination upon paying the licensure fee.
endorsement.quote: who, at the time of application, is a licensed or registered physical therapist or physical therapist assistant in good standing under the laws of another state or territory

temporary_or_provisional.value: Idaho does not issue temporary physical therapist licenses; licensure is available only by endorsement or by examination.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: No. Licensure as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant is available through either endorsement or examination.

renewal.value: Physical therapy licenses are moving to a 2-year renewal cycle that expires on the licensee's birthday, and licensees may renew up to 60 days before expiration.
renewal.quote: You will still be able to renew up to 60 days prior to your license expiration on your birthday.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 32 contact hours of continuing education every two years in areas germane to physical therapy; carryover hours are not permitted.
continuing_education.quote: Every person holding a license issued by the Board must complete thirty-two (32) contact hours of continuing education every two years.

compact.value: Idaho has not joined the PT Compact; the Idaho Physical Therapy Licensure Board has elected to defer membership at this time.
compact.quote: After thorough discussion, the Board has elected to defer membership in the Compact at this time.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through DOPL Online Services, linked from the board's Apply for or Renew a License button.
apply_url.quote: Apply for or Renew a License Search for a License or Registration File a Complaint Against a Licensee

board.value: Occupational Therapy Licensure Board (Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
board.quote: Welcome to the Occupational Therapy Licensure Board As of October 14, 2025, this Board has begun transitioning to biennial licensure.

education.value: Applicants must complete an occupational therapy program accredited by ACOTE (or a predecessor or successor organization) and at least six months of supervised fieldwork experience.
education.quote: For an occupational therapist, a minimum of six (6) months of supervised fieldwork experience

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the written examination established and conducted by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), at the passing score NBCOT sets.
national_exam.quote: The written examination shall be the examination established and conducted by the national board for certification in occupational therapy

background_check.value: Applicants must disclose any criminal conviction or charges other than minor traffic offenses, and any disciplinary action by a state regulatory agency or professional organization.
background_check.quote: The disclosure of any criminal conviction or charges against the applicant other than minor traffic offenses

application_fee.value: The board lists a $160 initial license fee for occupational therapists, with an $80 biennial renewal fee.
application_fee.quote: Occupational Therapist $160 $40 $80 Occupational Therapy Assistant $120 $30 $60

endorsement.value: The board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements for an applicant with current OT licensure in another state, DC or a US territory whose licensure standards the board considers equivalent.
endorsement.quote: grant a license to any applicant who shall present proof of current licensure as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: A limited permit, valid six months or as extended by the board, lets a graduate OT who has completed education and fieldwork practice under supervision. A temporary license may also be issued to an applicant licensed in good standing in another jurisdiction while the endorsement application is processed.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: This permit shall be valid for a period of six (6) months or as extended by the board.

renewal.value: OT licenses are issued for a two-year term and expire on the licensee's birthday unless renewed.
renewal.quote: All licenses issued under the provisions of this chapter shall be for a term of two (2) years and shall expire on the birthday of the licensee

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete and keep proof of 10 hours of germane continuing education each year of the renewal cycle; courses do not need board pre-approval.
continuing_education.quote: Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants must complete and maintain proof of completion of ten (10) hours of germane continuing education each year

processing_time.value: Once an application is complete and compliance is confirmed, a license is issued in approximately 3-5 business days; applications needing board review depend on the next scheduled board meeting.
processing_time.quote: If compliance is confirmed a license will be issued in approximately 3-5 business days.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through DOPL Online Services, linked from the board's Apply for or Renew a License button.
apply_url.quote: Apply for or Renew a License Search for a License or Registration File a Complaint Against a Licensee

board.value: Speech, Hearing and Communication Services Licensure Board
board.quote: DOPL has begun transitioning the Speech, Hearing and Communication Services Licensure Board to biennial licensure.

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree from a nationally accredited speech-language pathology school with a board-acceptable curriculum and complete the board-approved supervised clinical practicum and postgraduate professional experience.
education.quote: degree from a nationally accredited school of speech-language pathology with a curriculum acceptable to the board

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis examination; ASHA's Certificate of Clinical Competence is not required.
national_exam.quote: Yes, for an SLP or AUD license, passage of the PRAXIS examination is required.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit to a fingerprint-based criminal history background check under section 67-9411A, Idaho Code.
background_check.quote: Submit to a fingerprint-based criminal history background check in accordance with section 67-9411A

application_fee.value: Speech-language pathologists pay a $50 initial license fee plus a $25 application fee; the renewal fee is $0 under the board's current fee holiday.
application_fee.quote: Speech Language Pathologist $50 $0 Speech Language Pathologist Assistant $50 N/A

endorsement.value: The board may issue a license by endorsement to an applicant who holds a current, active and unrestricted equivalent license in another state or US territory, on board forms and fees.
endorsement.quote: An applicant for licensure by endorsement shall substantiate to the board that the applicant holds a current, active and unrestricted equivalent license in another state or United States territory.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A provisional permit lets a person practice speech-language pathology while completing the required postgraduate experience, and only under the supervision of a person fully licensed under the chapter.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The board shall adopt rules providing for a provisional permit to allow a person to engage in the practice of audiology or speech-language pathology while completing either the required postgraduate experience

renewal.value: Beginning August 1, 2026, Idaho is moving SLP licenses to a 2-year renewal cycle, with licenses ultimately expiring on the licensee's birthday.
renewal.quote: beginning August 1, 2026, the Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses (DOPL) will continue transitioning to a 2-year renewal cycle.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 10 contact hours of continuing education in the 12 months before each renewal, related to their scope of practice and sponsored by a professional association or institution of higher education.
continuing_education.quote: Each licensee will successfully complete, in the twelve (12) months preceding each renewal of their license, a minimum of ten (10) contact hours of continuing education (CE).

compact.value: The board describes the ASLP-IC as an alternative way for eligible SLPs to practice in member states, but it is still setting up fingerprint-based background checks with the Idaho State Police and FBI and will begin accepting applications once that process is established.
compact.quote: Once this process has been established between all parties, Idaho will begin accepting applications.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through DOPL Online Services, linked from the board's Apply for or Renew a License button.
apply_url.quote: Apply for or Renew a License Search for a License or Registration File a Complaint Against a Licensee

board.value: Physical Therapy Licensing and Disciplinary Board
board.quote: The Committee is composed of seven members appointed by the Secretary, consisting of six licensees actively practicing physical therapy and one public member.

education.value: Applicants must graduate from a physical therapist program that meets Section 1340.20 of the Illinois physical therapy rules; graduates of programs outside the United States must have their education evaluated by the Foreign Credentialing Commission of Physical Therapy (FCCPT).
education.quote: Graduation from a physical therapist program that meets the requirements of Section 1340.20 of the physical therapy rules.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) of the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy; an applicant who fails it 3 times in any jurisdiction must complete a pre-approved remedial training program of no less than 3 months or 360 hours.
national_exam.quote: The examination for a physical therapist license shall be the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) of the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy for physical therapists.

background_check.value: Applicants must disclose criminal convictions on the application; a few convictions (such as offenses requiring sex offender registration) automatically bar licensure, while most others are considered by the Department case by case.
background_check.quote: These are NOT an automatic bar to obtaining a license, but they do need to be disclosed on your application.

application_fee.value: The application fee for a physical therapist license is $100; examination candidates also pay a separate fee to the Division or the designated testing service.
application_fee.quote: The fee for application for a license as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant is $100.

endorsement.value: Applicants for licensure by endorsement must be actively licensed as a physical therapist in a U.S. state or territory; applicants who have practiced without discipline for 10 consecutive years may qualify for endorsement on that basis.
endorsement.quote: Individuals may qualify for licensure by endorsement based on having practiced without discipline for 10 consecutive years as a licensed physical therapist in the United States or its territories.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants found eligible for licensure except for passing the exam are issued a letter of authorization to test that allows them to practice under on-site supervision of a licensed physical therapist; they may not begin practice until the letter is received.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: the applicant shall be issued a letter of authorization to test that allows the applicant to practice under supervision in accordance with Section 2 of the Illinois Physical Therapy Act

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses expire on September 30 of each even-numbered year and may be renewed during the month before expiration by paying the renewal fee and completing continuing education.
renewal.quote: Every physical therapy license issued under the Act shall expire on September 30 of each even-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 40 hours of CE in each 24-month prerenewal period, including at least 3 hours on the ethical practice of physical therapy including jurisprudence; CE is not required for the first renewal after initial licensure.
continuing_education.quote: Every physical therapist shall complete 40 hours of CE relevant to the practice of physical therapy during each prerenewal period as a condition of renewal.

compact.value: Illinois is not one of the 38 PT Compact member states; the PT Compact Commission lists Illinois under Introduced Legislation, so compact privileges are not issued for Illinois.
compact.quote: Enacted Legislation (3) Maine Michigan Rhode Island Introduced Legislation (2) Illinois Massachusetts Non-Members (10)

apply_url.value: New physical therapist applications are filed online through IDFPR's CORE licensing system, linked from the IDFPR Physical Therapy page.
apply_url.quote: a new online system for professionals to apply for licensure in Illinois.

board.value: Occupational Therapy Licensure Board
board.quote: The Board is composed of seven members appointed by the Secretary, consisting of four licensed occupational therapists, two licensed occupational therapy assistants, and one public member.

education.value: Applicants must show completion of a master's degree or higher from a program that meets or exceeds the standards of the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE).
education.quote: you are required to present proof of completion of a master's degree or higher from a program that meets or exceeds standards set by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE).

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) certification examination for Occupational Therapist, Registered; unsuccessful candidates may retake it as many times as they wish.
national_exam.quote: The examination for licensure as a registered occupational therapist shall be the certification examination for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, Inc.

background_check.value: Applicants must disclose criminal convictions on the application; a few convictions (such as offenses requiring sex offender registration) automatically bar licensure, while most others are considered by the Department case by case.
background_check.quote: These are NOT an automatic bar to obtaining a license, but they do need to be disclosed on your application.

application_fee.value: The application fee for an occupational therapist license is $25; examination candidates also pay a separate fee to the Department or the designated testing service.
application_fee.quote: The fee for application for a license as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant is $25.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists currently or previously licensed in another jurisdiction apply by endorsement with the same education and OTR exam proof, plus certification of licensure from the first jurisdiction of licensure and every current jurisdiction.
endorsement.quote: you must provide certification of licensure from the first jurisdiction where you were licensed and for any current jurisdictions in which you are licensed.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet every requirement except passing the exam may request a letter of authorization to practice under supervision, with a licensed occupational therapist onsite at least 75% of work hours; they have six months from the letter's date to pass the exam, and the letter is not a license.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Supervision means that there must be a licensed occupational therapist onsite for at least 75% of your work hours.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses expire on December 31 of each odd-numbered year and may be renewed during the month before expiration by paying the renewal fee; renewal requires 24 contact hours of continuing education.
renewal.quote: Every license issued under the Act shall expire on December 31 of each odd numbered year.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 24 contact hours of CE in each 24-month prerenewal period, including one contact hour each of ethics, sexual harassment prevention and implicit bias awareness, plus one hour of dementia training for those treating adults age 26 or older; CE is not required for the first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: Every occupational therapist and occupational therapy assistant shall complete 24 contact hours of CE relevant to the practice of occupational therapy during each prerenewal period as a condition of renewal.

compact.value: Illinois has not joined the OT Compact: the bill to ratify it (HB4976, 104th General Assembly) was filed in 2026 and its last action was referral to the House Rules Committee on 2/06/2026.
compact.quote: Creates the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact Act. Provides that the State of Illinois ratifies and approves the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact.

apply_url.value: New occupational therapist applications are filed online through IDFPR's CORE licensing system, linked from the IDFPR Occupational Therapy page.
apply_url.quote: a new online system for professionals to apply for licensure in Illinois.

board.value: Board of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The Board is composed of five persons appointed by the Secretary, consisting of two speech-language pathologists, two audiologists and one public member.

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree from a speech-language pathology program approved by the Division; graduates of programs outside the United States must substantially comply with the minimum requirements of an approved program.
education.quote: Certification, on forms provided by the Division, of a master's or doctoral degree from a program approved by the Division in accordance with Section 1465.20(a).

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis examination or another national examination recognized by the Department, with scores sent directly to the Division by the testing service; an ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence is accepted in place of the exam and supervised-experience documents.
national_exam.quote: Passage of the PRAXIS examination or a national examination recognized by the Department set forth in Section 1465.50 or certification from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association

background_check.value: Applicants must disclose criminal convictions on the application; a few convictions (such as offenses requiring sex offender registration) automatically bar licensure, while most others are considered by the Department case by case.
background_check.quote: These are NOT an automatic bar to obtaining a license, but they do need to be disclosed on your application.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $90 for an initial speech-language pathologist license by examination, $100 for an applicant licensed in another state, territory or foreign country, and $75 for a temporary speech-language pathologist license.
application_fee.quote: The fee for application for initial speech-language pathologist or audiologist license by examination is $90.

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another U.S. state or territory apply by endorsement with proof of their degree, 9 months of supervised experience and exam passage (or the ASHA CCC), plus license verifications; those holding the ASHA CCC with no discipline may practice for 90 days after applying or until the application is decided, whichever is sooner.
endorsement.quote: may practice speech-language pathology or audiology without a license for 90 days from the date of application or until disposition of the license application by the Division, whichever is sooner.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have met the education and exam requirements must obtain a temporary license before beginning their supervised professional experience (clinical fellowship), supervised by an Illinois-licensed SLP; it is issued for 18 months and may be renewed only once for good cause. Students who have finished coursework but whose degree is not yet conferred may work in license-pending status for 120 days.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license shall be issued for a period of 18 months and may be renewed only once for good cause shown.

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist licenses expire on October 31 of odd-numbered years and may be renewed during the month before expiration by paying the renewal fee; renewal requires 20 hours of continuing education.
renewal.quote: Every license issued under the Act shall expire on October 31 of odd numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete 20 hours of CE in each 24-month prerenewal period ending October 31 of odd-numbered years, including at least one clock hour of ethics training; CE is not required for the first renewal of an Illinois license.
continuing_education.quote: In order to renew a speech-language pathology or audiology license, a licensee will be required to complete 20 hours of CE in accordance with this Section.

compact.value: Illinois has not joined ASLP-IC: the bill to enter the compact (HB2417, 104th General Assembly) had its last action, a re-referral to the House Rules Committee, on 3/21/2025.
compact.quote: Creates the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact Act. Enters into the compact, which may be entered into by any state, commonwealth, district, or territory of the United States of America

apply_url.value: New speech-language pathologist and SLP temporary applications are filed online through IDFPR's CORE licensing system, linked from the IDFPR Speech-Language Pathology & Audiology page.
apply_url.quote: a new online system for professionals to apply for licensure in Illinois.

board.value: Indiana Physical Therapy Board
board.quote: recordings (archived copies) of the Indiana Physical Therapy Board's public meetings are available here on the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency's (PLA's) YouTube Channel

education.value: Applicants must submit an official (certified) transcript, sent directly from the degree-granting institution, showing the degree has been conferred; graduates of foreign programs must also submit a credentials evaluation completed within the last six months.
education.quote: An official (certified) transcript of grades that shows the degree has been conferred. Transcripts must come directly from the degree granting institution.

national_exam.value: Applicants by examination must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), registering through the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy; the board lists the NPTE fee as $485.00, plus a $65 Prometric testing fee for physical therapists.
national_exam.quote: register online for the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE). The NPTE fee of $485.00 can be paid by credit card or debit card.

background_check.value: Applicants for an initial license must submit to a national fingerprint-based criminal history background check at their own cost (listed as $38.20), after the license application has been submitted; physical therapists are among the license types that require it.
background_check.quote: an individual applying for an initial license or certificate for certain license types shall submit to a national criminal history background check at the cost of the individual.

application_fee.value: The physical therapist application fee (by examination or by reciprocity) is $100.00, paid by credit or debit card; all fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: Application Fee of $100.00: Pay by credit or debit card. All fees are nonrefundable.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state who meet the reciprocal requirements of IC 25-1-21-5 may apply by reciprocity, submitting the $100.00 fee, a criminal background check, and an official license verification sent directly from the other licensing authority.
endorsement.quote: If you are a licensed in another State and meet the reciprocal requirements as defined in IC 25-1-21-5, submit the following with your online application:

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who also apply for full licensure may obtain a temporary permit ($50.00) to practice only under the direct supervision of an Indiana-licensed physical therapist; no more than 2 permits are issued, permits cannot be renewed, and a permit becomes invalid if the applicant fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The board may issue not more than two (2) temporary permits to a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant applying by Examination

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses renew every two years and expire on June 30 of even-numbered years; the renewal fee is $100.00.
renewal.quote: Physical Therapy licenses and Physical Therapy Assistant certifications expire on June 30 of even-numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 22 hours of continuing competency each biennial renewal period, including 2 hours in an ethics and Indiana jurisprudence course; hours cannot be carried over to the next period.
continuing_education.quote: Twenty-two (22) hours of continuing competency activities are required for the biennial renewal period, of which two (2) hours must be in an ethics and Indiana jurisprudence course

compact.value: Indiana adopted the PT Compact under House Enrolled Act 1405-2021; eligible PTs may obtain an Indiana compact privilege for a $100 Indiana fee plus a $45 Commission fee, and Indiana currently requires no jurisprudence exam for the privilege.
compact.quote: The PT Compact was adopted in state of Indiana under House Enrolled Act 1405-2021, and its applicable regulations are provided in statute under Indiana Code

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency's online licensing services, linked from the board's licensing information page.
apply_url.quote: Once you submit your application for the examination and required documentation to the Indiana Physical Therapy Board and meet the requirements for the examination

board.value: Indiana Occupational Therapy Committee
board.quote: Verifications must be completed from the state of issuance and sent to the Indiana Occupational Therapy Committee.

education.value: Applicants must submit a transcript from the school where the occupational therapist obtained the degree showing the degree conferred; graduates of foreign programs must submit an official translation if the transcript is not in English.
education.quote: A transcript of grades from the school from which the occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant obtained his or her degree that shows the degree conferred.

national_exam.value: Applicants by examination must have their NBCOT exam score report sent directly to the Indiana Occupational Therapy Committee.
national_exam.quote: Exam Score Report: Score report submitted directly to the Committee from NBCOT.

background_check.value: Applicants for an initial license must submit to a national fingerprint-based criminal history background check at their own cost (listed as $38.20), after the license application has been submitted; occupational therapists are among the license types that require it.
background_check.quote: an individual applying for an initial license or certificate for certain license types shall submit to a national criminal history background check at the cost of the individual.

application_fee.value: The occupational therapist application fee (by examination or by reciprocity) is $100.00, paid by credit or debit card and nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: Application fee of $100.00: Pay by credit or debit card. All application fees are nonrefundable

endorsement.value: OTs licensed in another state may apply by reciprocity with the $100.00 fee, a criminal background check, and license verification sent from the issuing state; at least 1 verification is needed to issue the license, and any remaining verifications are due by the first Indiana renewal.
endorsement.quote: In order to issue your Indiana license by Reciprocity, you must have at least 1 license verification submitted.

temporary_or_provisional.value: After applying for full licensure, applicants may obtain a temporary permit ($50.00) to practice only under the direct supervision of an Indiana occupational therapist; it expires at the earliest of permanent licensure, disapproval of the application, or 180 days after issuance.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: the date the committee disapproves the person's license application; or one hundred eighty (180) days after the date the permit is issued.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses expire December 31 of even-numbered years; the renewal fee is $100.
renewal.quote: Occupational Therapist and Occupational Therapy Assistant licenses expire December 31 of even-numbered years.

continuing_education.value: OTs must complete at least 18 hours of continuing competency in each 2-year license period, at least 9 of them in Category I courses, with no more than 9 hours from Category II activities.
continuing_education.quote: an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant must complete at least eighteen (18) hours of continuing competency of which at least nine (9) hours must be in Category I courses.

compact.value: Indiana adopted the OT Compact under Senate Enrolled Act 73-2023, and eligible OTs and OTAs may now apply for compact privileges directly through the OT Compact.
compact.quote: applicants may now apply for compact privilege(s) directly through the OT Compact.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency's online licensing services, linked from the committee's licensing information page.
apply_url.quote: Submit the following with your online application AFTER you have submitted your application for full licensure:

board.value: Indiana Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology Board
board.quote: the supervisor must hold a current Indiana license as a speech-language pathologist issued by the Indiana Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology Board

education.value: Applicants by examination must hold a master's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution, document 400 hours of direct supervised clinical experience, and complete a clinical fellowship of at least 9 consecutive months full-time or equivalent.
education.quote: Applicants must submit certification from their educational institution that the applicant has completed four hundred (400) hours of direct supervised clinical experience.

national_exam.value: Applicants must have ETS send an official Praxis score report verifying a passing score directly to the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency; a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence may substitute for the score report.
national_exam.quote: Applicants must submit an official score report from ETS-Praxis Series, verifying a passing score on the examination.

state_exam.value: All SLP applicants, including those applying by reciprocity, must pass a written Indiana jurisprudence examination covering the state statute, Title 880 rules and Health Professions Standards of Practice; the passing score is 75%.
state_exam.quote: The passing score on the jurisprudence examination is seventy-five percent (75%). NO APPLICANT IS EXEMPT FROM TAKING THE LAW EXAMINATION.

background_check.value: Applicants for an initial license must submit to a national fingerprint-based criminal history background check at their own cost (listed as $38.20), after the license application has been submitted; speech pathologists are among the license types that require it.
background_check.quote: an individual applying for an initial license or certificate for certain license types shall submit to a national criminal history background check at the cost of the individual.

application_fee.value: The speech-language pathologist application fee (by examination or by reciprocity) is $150.00, paid by credit or debit card and nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: Application Fee of $150.00: Pay by credit or debit card. All application fees are nonrefundable.

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another state may apply by reciprocity with the $150.00 fee, a criminal background check, an official license verification sent directly from the other licensing authority, and a passing score on the Indiana jurisprudence examination.
endorsement.quote: Current license verification is required. The official license verification must be sent directly from the licensing authority to the Board

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows must register for a Clinical Fellowship Year (CFY) with a $50.00 application fee and a supervisor holding a current Indiana SLP or audiologist license; the fellowship is 9 months full-time or equivalent and may not exceed 18 consecutive months.
