temporary_or_provisional.quote: The clinical fellowship may not exceed a maximum period of eighteen (18) consecutive months. The clinical fellowship shall consist of nine (9) months full-time employment or its equivalent.

renewal.value: SLP licenses renew on a two-year cycle and expire December 31 of odd-numbered years; the renewal fee is $100.00.
renewal.quote: Speech-language pathologists and audiologists are required to have completed thirty-six (36) hours of continuing education for each two-year renewal cycle.

continuing_education.value: SLPs must complete 36 hours of continuing education each two-year renewal cycle, with no more than 6 hours through self-study; hours cannot be carried over, and in-service and competency CEs do not count.
continuing_education.quote: Speech-language pathologists and audiologists are required to have completed thirty-six (36) hours of continuing education for each two-year renewal cycle.

compact.value: The ASLP-IC Commission's state fee table (current as of May 28, 2026) lists Indiana as not yet accepting ASLP compact privilege applications; it shows an Indiana jurisprudence requirement, a $50 state fee and a $50 compact fee.
compact.quote: Indiana not yet IN Jurisprudence IN Practice Act and $50 $50

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency's online licensing services, linked from the board's licensing information page.
apply_url.quote: Please note that once you have completed your CFY you must then apply for licensure as a Speech Language Pathologist through our office.

board.value: Iowa Board of Physical & Occupational Therapy
board.quote: The Iowa Board of Physical & Occupational Therapy evaluates the qualifications of applicants for licensure and grants licenses to those who qualify.

education.value: Applicants must hold a degree from a nationally accredited physical therapy program, with official transcripts sent directly to the board by the school; degrees granted on or after February 1, 2004 must be a master's degree or higher.
education.quote: Official transcripts conferring a degree from a nationally-accredited physical therapy program, sent directly to the board office from the college or university.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), with the score sent directly to the board by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT).
national_exam.quote: Applicants must submit proof of passing the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), sent directly to the board office by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT).

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a fingerprint-based criminal background check (two fingerprint cards and a signed waiver form), and the background check fee is $55.
background_check.quote: Submit a completed background check packet, which will be forwarded after an application is submitted to the board. The background check fee ($55) is non-refundable.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $120, plus a $55 background check fee; application fees are non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: The application fee is $120, and the background check fee is $55. Application fees are non-refundable.

endorsement.value: Applicants previously licensed in another state must submit verification of every state license and show one of: 40 hours of board-approved continuing education in the prior two years, 2,080 hours of practice as a PT in the prior two years, one year as full-time PT faculty, or a passing NPTE score within the prior two years.
endorsement.quote: Proof of completion of 40 hours of board-approved continuing education courses during the two years immediately preceding the Iowa license application submission;

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses renew every two years; the renewal period begins on the sixteenth day of the licensee's birth month and ends on the fifteenth day of the birth month two years later.
renewal.quote: physical therapist assistant shall begin on the sixteenth day of the birth month and end on the fifteenth day of the birth month two years later.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least 40 hours of board-approved continuing education each two-year renewal period; newly licensed therapists are exempt for their first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: Each biennium, each person who is licensed to practice as a physical therapist in this state will be required to complete a minimum of 40 hours of continuing education approved by the board.

compact.value: Iowa participates in the Physical Therapy Compact; therapists who do not live in Iowa may work in Iowa with a PT Compact privilege obtained through the PT Compact website.
compact.quote: As long as you are not living in Iowa, you may work in Iowa with your PT Compact privilege.

processing_time.value: The board says total processing can take up to eight weeks, or longer depending on the outcome of the FBI background check.
processing_time.quote: It may take up to eight weeks of total processing time for us to approve your application.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply and pay online through the licensure portal linked from the board's physical therapist application page.
apply_url.quote: Apply online for licensure as a physical therapist in Iowa.

board.value: Iowa Board of Physical & Occupational Therapy
board.quote: The Iowa Board of Physical & Occupational Therapy evaluates the qualifications of applicants for licensure and grants licenses to those who qualify.

education.value: Applicants must complete an occupational therapy degree from an ACOTE-accredited program, including supervised fieldwork, with official transcripts sent directly to the board by the school.
education.quote: Official transcripts confirming completion of an occupational therapy degree from an occupational therapy program approved by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association,

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT exam, with the score sent to the board by NBCOT score transfer.
national_exam.quote: Proof of passing score for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) Exam, sent by score transfer directly to the Board office by NBCOT.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $120 and is non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: To submit an application, create an account, apply, and pay online. The application fee is $120. Application fees are non-refundable.

endorsement.value: Applicants previously licensed in another state must submit verification of every state license and show one of: 30 hours of Iowa board-approved continuing education in the prior two years, 2,080 hours of practice as an OT in the prior two years, one year as full-time OT faculty, or a passing NBCOT score within the prior two years.
endorsement.quote: Proof of completion of 30 hours of Iowa Board-approved continuing education courses during the two years immediately preceding the Iowa license application submission, OR

temporary_or_provisional.value: Graduates awaiting the NBCOT exam may apply for an occupational therapist limited license ($120 application fee) naming a supervising OT; it expires when exam results become available or 6 months after issue, whichever is sooner, and holders who fail the exam must stop practicing.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Limited permits expire on the date on which the exam results become available, or for 6 months after the permit is issued, whichever is sooner.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses renew every two years; the renewal period begins on the sixteenth day of the licensee's birth month and ends on the fifteenth day of the birth month two years later.
renewal.quote: occupational therapy assistant shall begin on the sixteenth day of the birth month and end on the fifteenth day of the birth month two years later.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete at least 30 hours of board-approved continuing education each two-year renewal period; newly licensed therapists are exempt for their first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: each person who is licensed to practice as an occupational therapist in this state will have the responsibility to finance the cost and be required to complete a minimum of 30 hours of continuing education approved by the board.

compact.value: Iowa has joined the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact but is still completing rule and database updates to become an active member state.
compact.quote: Iowa is actively working to complete rule and database updates to become an active member state.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply and pay online through the licensure portal linked from the board's occupational therapist application page.
apply_url.quote: Apply online for licensure as an occupational therapist in Iowa.

board.value: Iowa Board of Speech Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The Iowa Board of Speech Pathology and Audiology evaluates the qualifications of applicants for licensure and grants licenses to those who qualify.

education.value: Applicants must submit either the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence or proof of a master's degree in speech pathology (or equivalent), at least 400 hours of supervised clinical training, and nine months of full-time supervised clinical experience after the master's degree.
education.quote: Official verification of completion of not less than 400 hours of supervised clinical training; Verification of nine months of full-time clinical experience, or equivalent, completed after the master’s degree under the supervision of a licensed speech pathologist

national_exam.value: Applicants who do not submit the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence must submit results of the Praxis Examination.
national_exam.quote: completed after the master’s degree under the supervision of a licensed speech pathologist; and Results of the Praxis Examination.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $120 and is non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: Apply online for a permanent speech pathologist license in Iowa. The application fee is $120. All application fees are non-refundable.

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed in another state must meet Iowa's licensure requirements, submit license verification from every state where they have been licensed, and verify at least five years of independent licensure in one or more states; those who do not qualify may be eligible for licensure by verification.
endorsement.quote: Applicant must verify at a minimum of five years of licensure as an independent licensee in one or more states.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A speech pathologist temporary license ($120 fee) requires a master's degree transcript, verification of at least 400 hours of supervised clinical training, Praxis results, and a completed, signed Supervised Clinical Experience Plan with a board-approved supervisor before it is issued.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Before the temporary license is issued, the applicant must submit a completed and signed Supervised Clinical Experience Plan.

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years; the renewal period begins January 1 of an even-numbered year and ends December 31 of the next odd-numbered year.
renewal.quote: will begin on January 1 of an even-numbered year and end on December 31 of the next odd-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: Speech pathologists must complete at least 26 hours of board-approved continuing education each two-year period (January 1 of each even-numbered year through December 31 of each odd-numbered year).
continuing_education.quote: Each biennium, a person who is licensed to practice as a speech pathology or audiology licensee in this state will be required to complete a minimum of 26 hours of continuing education approved by the board.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply and pay online through the licensure portal linked from the board's speech pathologist application page.
apply_url.quote: Apply online for a permanent speech pathologist license in Iowa.

board.value: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts
board.quote: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts 800 SW Jackson St., Suite 700 Topeka, KS 66612

education.value: Applicants must have completed the academic requirements of a board-approved physical therapy educational program; applicants from a program not approved by the board must present an evaluation from a board-approved entity showing the program met the board's criteria.
education.quote: the applicant has successfully completed the academic requirements of an educational program in physical therapy approved by the board which is appropriate for the certification or licensure of the applicant

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE); graduates of CAPTE-accredited programs register through FSBPT under the Board's Alternate Approval Pathway, while non-CAPTE graduates must first be approved to test by the Board.
national_exam.quote: The AAP allows candidates who are graduates of CAPTE-accredited programs to be approved to sit for the NPTE by The Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT).

state_exam.value: Physical therapist applicants must complete the Kansas jurisprudence exam and submit it with the application; a score of 80% or higher is required.
state_exam.quote: All Physical Therapist: Complete the jurisprudence exam and submit with your application. A score of 80% or higher is required.

background_check.value: As of December 01, 2025, physical therapist applicants must submit fingerprints for state and national background checks, and the criminal background report fee is $57.
background_check.quote: As of December 01, 2025, Physical Therapists (PTs) and Physical Therapist Assistants (PTAs) must submit fingerprints for state and national background checks.

application_fee.value: The Board's physical therapy application fee is $80.00, whether the application is based on examination or on a certificate of prior examination.
application_fee.quote: Application based upon certificate of prior examination: $80.00 Application based on examination: $80.00

endorsement.value: The Board may license a physical therapist without examination if the applicant shows they passed the board-approved examination or an examination before another state's licensing board whose standards the Board finds to be as high as Kansas's.
endorsement.quote: The board may issue a license in physical therapy without examination to an applicant who presents evidence satisfactory to the board of having passed the examination in physical therapy approved by the board

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet all licensure requirements except the examination may receive one temporary permit, which expires three months after issuance and carries an additional $25 nonrefundable fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: An applicant who meets all the requirements for licensure, except examination, is eligible for a temporary permit. Only one temporary permit may be issued to a person and expires three months after the date of issuance.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses must be renewed annually and expire on December 31; the renewal cycle begins November 15 and ends January 31.
renewal.quote: All Physical Therapist licenses expire on December 31st; the license must be renewed annually.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least 40 contact hours of continuing education within the preceding two-year period, submitted with renewal in odd-numbered years, and must complete the Kansas physical therapy jurisprudence assessment module during each continuing education cycle.
continuing_education.quote: evidence of satisfactory completion within the preceding two-year period of at least 40 contact hours of continuing education for a licensed physical therapist

compact.value: Kansas is a PT Compact member state; the PT Compact Commission lists member states as actively issuing and accepting compact privileges.
compact.quote: Member States (38) Alabama Alaska Arizona Arkansas Colorado Connecticut Delaware District of Columbia Georgia Indiana Iowa Kansas

processing_time.value: The Board states the application process takes on average four to eight weeks, though each application is different.
processing_time.quote: The application process takes on average four to eight weeks; however, each application is different.

apply_url.value: Initial physical therapist applications are submitted using the Initial Licensing Application on the Board's Licensing Forms page.
apply_url.quote: Physical Therapist (P.T.) Initial Licensing Application Reinstatement Application Address Change Request Form

board.value: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts
board.quote: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts 800 SW Jackson St., Suite 700 Topeka, KS 66612

education.value: Applicants must have completed the academic requirements of an occupational therapy educational program recognized by the Board and a period of supervised field work recognized by the Board.
education.quote: Education: The applicant shall present evidence satisfactory to the board of having successfully completed the academic requirements of an educational program in occupational therapy recognized by the board.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the board-approved entry-level certification examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), with a minimum criterion-scaled score of 450.
national_exam.quote: the entry-level certification examination for an occupational therapist administered by the national board for certification in occupational therapy, inc. shall meet the standards for an examination established by the board

application_fee.value: The Board's occupational therapy application fee is $80.00.
application_fee.quote: The following fees shall be collected by the Board: Application for license: $80.00 License renewal: Form renewal: $75.00

endorsement.value: The Board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements for an applicant with current occupational therapy licensure or registration in another state, the District of Columbia or a U.S. territory whose standards the Board finds equivalent to or higher than Kansas's.
endorsement.quote: The board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements and grant licensure to any applicant who presents proof of current licensure or registration as an occupational therapist

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet all licensure requirements except the examination may receive one temporary permit, which expires one year after issuance and carries an additional $25 nonrefundable fee.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: An applicant who meets all the requirements for licensure, except examination, is eligible for a temporary permit. Only one temporary permit may be issued to a person and expires one year after the date of issuance.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses must be renewed annually and expire on March 31; the renewal cycle begins February 15 and ends April 30.
renewal.quote: All Occupational Therapist licenses expire on March 31st; the license must be renewed annually.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 40 contact hours of continuing education during the preceding 24 months, submitted with renewal in each odd-numbered year, with at least 30 contact hours from class I, IV, V or VI activities.
continuing_education.quote: Each licensee shall submit evidence of completing at least 40 contact hours of continuing education during the preceding 24 months. Evidence of this attainment shall be submitted before or with the application for renewal in each odd-numbered year.

compact.value: Kansas enacted the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact through HB 2533, which was signed by the Governor and takes effect upon publication in the statute book.
compact.quote: Enacting the occupational therapy licensure compact, respiratory care interstate compact, esthetics licensure compact and athletic trainer licensure compact to provide interstate practice privileges.

processing_time.value: The Board states the application process takes on average four to eight weeks, though each application is different.
processing_time.quote: The application process takes on average four to eight weeks; however, each application is different.

apply_url.value: Initial occupational therapist applications are submitted using the Initial Licensing Application on the Board's Licensing Forms page.
apply_url.quote: Occupational Therapist (O.T.) Initial Licensing Application Reinstatement Application Address Change Request Form

board.value: Kansas Department for Aging and Disability Services, Health Occupations Credentialing
board.quote: Office Location Health Occupations Credentialing 503 S Kansas Ave. Topeka, KS 66603-3404

education.value: Applicants must hold at least a master's degree or equivalent in speech-language pathology from an institution with standards consistent with those of the state universities of Kansas, complete supervised clinical practicum, and complete a postgraduate professional experience.
education.quote: possession of at least a master's degree or equivalent in speech-language pathology or audiology from an educational institution with standards consistent with those of the state universities of Kansas

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the ETS specialty area test in speech-language pathology (the Praxis) and have ETS send results to the department using recipient code 7272; full or reciprocal applicants may instead submit the Certificate of Clinical Competence.
national_exam.quote: Have you taken and passed the NTE Specialty Area Test in Speech-Language Pathology or audiology? Y/N Request that ETS send the results to the department. The department's score recipient code is 7272.

application_fee.value: The license fee is $135.00; for an initial licensure period of less than 24 months the application fee is prorated at $5.50 per month for any full or partial month.
application_fee.quote: The license fee shall be $135.00. The license application fee for an initial licensure period of less than 24 months shall be prorated at $5.50 per month for any full or partial month

endorsement.value: The Secretary may license a person holding a valid license in another state if the issuing state documents good standing, the applicant meets current education, clinical practicum, postgraduate professional experience and examination requirements, and the applicant pays an endorsement and application fee.
endorsement.quote: The secretary may issue a license to a person holding a valid license in another state if: (1) The secretary receives from the issuing state or states documentation that the licensee is currently in good standing

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have completed education and clinical practicum but not the supervised postgraduate professional experience or the examination must apply for a temporary license, issued for 12 months and renewable for one subsequent 12-month period; the temporary license fee is $65.00.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: shall apply for a temporary license. This temporary license shall be issued for a period of 12 months and may be renewed for one subsequent 12-month period upon request and with the secretary's approval.

renewal.value: Full licenses expire biennially on October 31, and the license renewal fee is $135.00.
renewal.quote: ending on the date the license expires. All full licenses shall expire biennially on October 31.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 20 hours of approved continuing education for a single two-year license, or 30 hours if licensed in both speech-language pathology and audiology; excess hours do not carry over.

compact.value: Kansas enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact through SB 77, approved by the Governor on March 30, 2021.

board.value: Kentucky Board of Physical Therapy

education.value: Applicants must successfully complete a CAPTE-accredited physical therapy program, and the program director must send the board a letter certifying completion of all academic and clinical requirements.
education.quote: Successfully complete a CAPTE accredited Program in Physical Therapy and request the Program Director's certification of completion

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered through FSBPT; Kentucky regulation sets the passing point at the FSBPT-recommended scaled score of 600.
national_exam.quote: a passing score shall be the criterion referenced passing point recommended by the FSBPT set equal to a scaled score of 600

state_exam.value: Applicants must complete Kentucky's Jurisprudence Exam (JE), a free online 20-question exam that the board rewrites every 2 years; it is required for new applicants, compact privilege holders and renewal.
state_exam.quote: JE for new applicants, for compact privileges, and for CEUs obtained between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2027.

background_check.value: Every new applicant must submit fingerprints to the Kentucky State Police for a state and federal (FBI) background check, which costs $57.00; background checks are valid for 6 months from receipt by the board.

application_fee.quote: Mail the application with $225 fee payable to KY Board of Physical Therapy (money order or cashier's check OR you may pay online through our website).

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state apply by endorsement: they must hold an active PT license in at least one jurisdiction, have passed the NPTE (scores sent through the FSBPT Score Transfer Service), complete the Kentucky Jurisprudence Exam and complete the federal and state background check.

temporary_or_provisional.value: First-time exam candidates who want to work before full licensure must submit a Supervisory Agreement Form and receive a one-time temporary permit, valid for six months from issuance or until the board notifies them of their NPTE results.

renewal.value: Credentials are renewed every two years by paying the renewal fee on or before March 31 of each odd-numbered year; credentials not renewed by that date lapse.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 30 contact hours of continued competency per renewal period, including 2 hours awarded for the Jurisprudence Exam and at least 18 hours from Category 1 activities.
continuing_education.quote: For a physical therapist, the board shall require thirty (30) contact hours as a condition of licensure renewal.

compact.value: Kentucky participates in the PT Compact: therapists licensed in another participating state can buy a compact privilege to practice in Kentucky through the PT Compact Commission, but must first take Kentucky's Jurisprudence Exam (no additional cost), and the privilege expires with the home-state license.
compact.quote: you can access the webpage for PT Compact Commission to purchase privileges for practice in the state of Kentucky without obtaining a separate license in Kentucky.

national_exam.quote: An applicant for licensure shall take the appropriate examination as authorized by the NBCOT and shall receive a passing score on the examination.

temporary_or_provisional.quote: in no instance shall the temporary permit extend for more than sixty (60) days following the second examination offered after the applicant has applied

renewal.value: Licenses are renewed annually on or before October 31 with a $50 renewal fee for an OT; a 60-day grace period applies with a $25 late renewal fee.

continuing_education.quote: shall complete a minimum of twelve (12) CCUs of qualified activities for maintaining continuing competence during the preceding annual renewal period.

board.value: Kentucky Board of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The board examines and licenses all eligible candidates for entry into the profession of speech-language pathology and audiology.

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's degree in speech-language pathology or communication disorders from a program accredited by ASHA's Council for Academic Accreditation (or equivalent education, such as a CAA-accredited doctoral degree) and complete the postgraduate professional experience.
education.quote: attainment of a master's degree in the area of speech-language pathology or communication disorders from a program accredited by the Council for Academic Accreditation of the American Speech Language Hearing Association

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass a national Praxis examination in speech-language pathology.
national_exam.quote: The applicant shall have passed a national PRAXIS examination in speech-language pathology.

background_check.value: New applicants must complete an FBI fingerprint background check through IdentoGO (board service code 27GKYV), with results sent directly to the board by the Kentucky State Police; results take 5 to 10 business days to arrive and applicants pay the fees.
background_check.quote: It can take 5 to 10 business days from your appointment with IdentoGO for the board to receive the results.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay $150 ($50 application fee plus $100 licensure fee) by check or money order payable to the Kentucky State Treasurer; applicants who already hold a Kentucky interim license pay $100.
application_fee.quote: made payable to the Kentucky State Treasurer for: a. The fee of $150 ($50 application fee/$100 licensure fee);

endorsement.value: Applicants currently licensed as SLPs in another state may be licensed by reciprocity upon submitting a letter of good standing from that state, documentation of national certification or a passing score on a board-approved national exam, and a certified transcript showing at least a master's degree in communication disorders.
endorsement.quote: The board may grant a license to an applicant currently licensed in another state as a speech-language pathologist upon receipt of the following:

temporary_or_provisional.value: Graduates complete their postgraduate professional experience (clinical fellowship) under an interim license and a Kentucky-licensed supervisor; it requires at least 36 weeks of full-time experience (minimum 35 hours per week) or the part-time equivalent, totaling at least 1,260 hours within 24 months.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The experience shall consist of at least thirty-six (36) weeks of full-time professional experience to consist of a minimum of thirty-five (35) work hours per week

renewal.quote: A license shall be renewed biennially on or before the due date of January 31 and no later than the grace period ending on March 2 of that year.

continuing_education.value: SLPs must complete at least 30 continuing education hours per two-year renewal period, including 2 hours focused on ethics, completed by January 31 of the renewal period.
continuing_education.quote: A minimum of thirty (30) continuing education hours shall be accrued by each person holding licensure as a speech-language pathologist

apply_url.value: Applicants complete the board's paper Application for Licensure and mail it with the fee to the Kentucky Board of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology, P.O. Box 1360, Frankfort, Kentucky 40602.
apply_url.quote: Mail to Kentucky Board of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology, P. O. Box 1360, Frankfort, Kentucky, 40602.

board.value: Louisiana Physical Therapy Board
board.quote: The Louisiana Physical Therapy Board was created within the Department of Health.

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from a CAPTE-accredited school of physical therapy; the minimum qualification to become a PT is a doctorate-level degree in physical therapy.
education.quote: The minimum qualification required to become a PT is a doctorate level degree in physical therapy.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) administered by FSBPT. Louisiana is an Alternate Approval Pathway state, so FSBPT makes CAPTE graduates eligible to test once they register and choose Louisiana.
national_exam.quote: After an individual has registered for the NPTE, FSBPT will be responsible for making them eligible to test if they have chosen Louisiana.

state_exam.value: All applicants must pass the Board's online jurisprudence exam, which is free and consists of 40 questions on the Louisiana Practice Act and Rules, with a score of 75% or higher.
state_exam.quote: All applicants must make a 75% or higher to pass the Board's online jurisprudence. The exam is free of charge and consists of 40 questions from the Louisiana Practice Act and Rules.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a federal background check after submitting the online application; background checks done for a school or employer cannot be used.
background_check.quote: Background check results cannot be shared between entities. Also, the board requires a federal background check

application_fee.value: The non-refundable application fee is $250 or $390, depending on the applicant's birth year and the application year, because a first license is issued for a one-year or two-year term based on birth year.
application_fee.quote: A license issued to an applicant for the first time shall be for a term of one year or two years, to be determined by the birth year of the applicant

endorsement.value: PTs who have held a license in another US state apply by reciprocity, which requires NPTE score transfer through FSBPT, licensure verification sent directly from every jurisdiction where they were licensed, and proof of continuing education compliance for the previous 24 months.
endorsement.quote: Provide proof in the form of completed course certificates of continuing education compliance from all jurisdictions in which the applicant has held an active license in the previous 24 months

temporary_or_provisional.value: New graduates awaiting the NPTE may obtain a provisional license, which is valid for 90 days from the issue date with no extensions.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license is only valid for 90 days from the issue date. There are no extensions.

renewal.value: Licenses renew for two-year terms based on birth year; for odd birth-year licensees the 2027 renewal period runs February 1 to March 31, renewals in April incur a $120 late fee, and licenses expire April 30. The renewal fee is $140 per year.
renewal.quote: The term for license renewal shall be for two years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 30 hours of board-approved continuing education each biennial renewal period, including at least 2 hours of jurisprudence and 2 hours of ethics or professionalism; no carryover is allowed.
continuing_education.quote: licensees shall successfully complete document and report to the board at least 30 hours of board-approved continuing education courses or activities in the biennial renewal period.

compact.value: Louisiana is a PT Compact member state that issues compact privileges; the total PT compact privilege fee is $140 (including a $95 state fee), and the Louisiana jurisprudence exam must be passed before applying.
compact.quote: Registering for an account is required to access and complete the Louisiana jurisprudence exam.

processing_time.value: The Board states that processing time varies by application but in total may take up to 2 months.
processing_time.quote: Processing time varies for each application but in total may take up to 2 months.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the Louisiana Physical Therapy Board's application instructions page, choosing the instructions for their applicant type.
apply_url.quote: All applicants must complete the online application prior to starting the background check process.

board.value: Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners
board.quote: Welcome to the website of the Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners

education.value: Applicants must have successfully completed the academic and supervised fieldwork requirements needed to sit for the occupational therapist certification examination.

national_exam.quote: Licensure applicants - licensure applicants must be currently NBCOT certified.

background_check.value: A background check is required for licensure; the board sends instructions for completing it after the application has been received.

application_fee.value: The non-refundable licensure fee for an occupational therapist is $150.00; a temporary license applicant pays $200.00, which includes a $50.00 temporary license fee and the $150.00 licensure fee.

continuing_education.quote: not less than 14 contact hours, or 1.4 continuing education units (CEUs) which must include: 1 hours of Ethics (approved by AOTA, LOTA, or NBCOT) and a 1 hour course provided by LSBME

apply_url.value: Applicants begin a new online initial application through the LSBME LaMED DashBoard, linked from the board's OT application instructions page.

board.value: Louisiana Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: it is necessary to provide regulatory authority over persons offering speech-language pathology and audiology services to the public.

education.value: Applicants need a master's degree in speech-language pathology and 400 clinical practicum hours if their graduate program began after January 1, 2004.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Graduates with a master's degree and 400 clinical practicum hours can obtain a Provisional Speech-Language Pathology license; provisional SLPs have one year to submit a passing national exam score, and the full license requires 36 weeks of full-time post-graduate professional employment experience.

required_courses.quote: Beginning June 1, 2022, completion of 2 hours of implicit bias training within the 5 years immediately preceding issuance of the license or registration is required.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses are valid for 2 years and renew every 2 years online through MiPLUS; the renewal fee is $165.40, and renewal notices are sent about 90 business days before expiration.
renewal.quote: Your initial license is valid for 2 years. All subsequent renewals will also be valid for 2 years.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 20 board-approved continuing education hours in the 2 years before renewal, including at least 1 hour in pain and symptom management. Renewal also requires 1 hour of implicit bias training for each year of the license cycle and a one-time human trafficking training.
continuing_education.quote: During the 2 years preceding the application for renewal, successful completion of 20 hours of continuing education that are approved by the board.

compact.value: Michigan enacted Public Act 40 of 2026 and Public Act 42 of 2026 to join the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact, but the Bureau does not expect the compact privilege to practice process to begin in Michigan until early 2028, so compact privileges are not yet issued.
compact.quote: In July 2026, the Governor signed Public Act 40 of 2026 and Public Act 42 of 2026 into law, permitting Michigan to begin the process of participating in the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact

apply_url.value: Applicants apply or renew online through the Apply or Renew Online link on the Michigan Board of Occupational Therapists page, which leads to MiPLUS.
apply_url.quote: Users will find the link to apply for or renew an Occupational Therapist license on this page

board.value: Michigan Board of Speech-Language Pathology
board.quote: Welcome to the Michigan Board of Speech Language Pathology website!

education.value: Applicants must have a master's or doctoral degree from an accredited educational program and complete a supervised postgraduate clinical experience; a current ASHA CCC-SLP is presumed to satisfy the education, clinical experience and exam requirements.
education.quote: Provide proof, as directed by the department, verifying completion of a masters or doctoral degree from an accredited educational program

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis Series II exam in Speech-Language Pathology and have ETS send the score to the Michigan Board (recipient code 7430).
national_exam.quote: PRAXIS Series II Exam in Speech-Language Pathology must be completed. Please contact ETS to have your score information be made available to our office.

background_check.value: All applicants must complete a criminal background check; instructions are emailed in an Application Confirmation letter after the application is submitted.
background_check.quote: Once the application is completed and submitted you will be emailed an Application Confirmation letter containing instructions to complete the Criminal Background Check

application_fee.value: The application fee plus 2-year license fee for a speech-language pathologist license by exam or endorsement is $187.40, payable by credit or debit card.
application_fee.quote: Speech Language Pathologist by Exam or Endorsement: $187.40

endorsement.value: Applicants by endorsement must hold a current, full speech-language pathologist license in another state or Canadian province and provide license verification, plus either current ASHA certification or official master's or doctoral transcripts with a passing Praxis or Canadian entry-to-practice exam score.
endorsement.quote: You must hold a current and full speech-language pathologist license in another state or in a province of Canada.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Michigan issues a speech-language pathologist educational limited temporary license that allows practice under the supervision of a fully licensed SLP while gaining the 9 months (1,260 hours) of post-graduate clinical experience required for full licensure. The fee is $187.40 and the license is valid for 2 years from issuance.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The speech language pathologist educational limited temporary license type allows a licensee to engage in the practice of speech and language therapy, under the supervision of a fully licensed SLP

required_courses.value: Before an initial license is issued, applicants must complete 2 hours of implicit bias training within the 5 years before issuance, plus a one-time training in identifying victims of human trafficking.
required_courses.quote: Beginning June 1, 2022, completion of 2 hours of implicit bias training within the 5 years immediately preceding issuance of the license or registration is required.

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist licenses are valid for 2 years and renew every 2 years online through MiPLUS, starting 90 days before expiration; the renewal fee is $165.40.
renewal.quote: Your initial Speech-Language Pathology license is valid for 2 years. All subsequent renewals will also be valid for 2 years.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must earn 20 continuous professional development (CPD) credits per 2-year renewal cycle, including at least 1 credit in pain and symptom management, and only 15 CPD credits may be completed through ASHA. Renewal also requires 1 hour of implicit bias training for each year of the license cycle and a one-time human trafficking training.
continuing_education.quote: Rule 338.629 adds the requirement of 20 Continuous Professional Development (CPD) credits, with at least 1 CPD credit in pain and symptom management for renewal.

compact.value: Michigan has not enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact; House Bill 4509 of 2025, which would provide for the compact, passed the House and was referred to the Senate Committee on Health Policy. No compact privileges are issued in Michigan.
compact.quote: Health occupations: audiologists; audiologist and speech language pathologist licensure compact; provide for.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply or renew online through the Apply / Renew Online link on the Michigan Board of Speech-Language Pathology page, which leads to MiPLUS.
apply_url.quote: Users will find the link to apply for or renew a Speech Language Pathologist license on this page

board.value: Minnesota Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The governor shall appoint a state Board of Physical Therapy to administer sections

education.value: Applicants must complete a CAPTE-accredited physical therapy education program plus an additional 60 academic semester credits (or the quarter equivalent) from a regionally accredited institution, earned outside the physical therapy program.
education.quote: All applicants for licensure as a physical therapist must complete a course in physical therapy education accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE)

national_exam.value: New graduates must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE); the Board approves eligible applicants to test, and applicants also register and pay separately with FSBPT.
national_exam.quote: Your official transcript and completed criminal background check are not required for the Board to make you eligible for the NPTE but are required to be completed before you can be licensed.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a fingerprint-based criminal background check, which is required for final licensure; the criminal background check fee is $35.00.
background_check.quote: The Criminal Background Check Program will email you the fingerprinting and background check information and forms after you submit your online application and pay fees.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $100.00 licensure application fee, a $60.00 annual licensure fee and a $35.00 criminal background check fee; new graduates also pay a $50.00 examination processing fee for each exam attempt. Fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: Licensure Application Fee: $100.00 (Required of all applicants) This fee must be submitted with your completed online application.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state apply through the Board's licensed-in-another-state application; those who have not practiced 320 hours or passed the NPTE in the past 5 years must retake and pass the exam or complete at least 320 hours of Board-approved supervised clinical practice.
endorsement.quote: who have not practiced 320 hours or achieved a passing score on the NPTE in the past 5 years may choose to retake and pass the exam or complete no less than 320 hours

temporary_or_provisional.value: New graduates may obtain a temporary permit ($25.00 fee) to practice under direct, immediate, on-premises supervision before taking the NPTE; the permit may be issued only once and cannot be renewed.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: This permit allows applicants to practice physical therapy under direct, immediate, and on premises supervision. A temporary permit may be issued only once and cannot be renewed.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses are renewed every year; licensees must apply for renewal and pay the renewal fee before January 1 each year.
renewal.quote: Every licensed physical therapist and physical therapist assistant shall, before January 1 each year, apply to the board for an extension of a license and pay a fee in the amount set by the board.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 20 contact hours of continuing education every two years, including at least two hours on professional ethics, and at each annual renewal must pass an open-book jurisprudence examination on the Practice Act.
continuing_education.quote: Every two years, each physical therapist and physical therapist assistant licensed by the board shall obtain 20 contact hours of continuing education credit

compact.value: The PT Compact Commission lists Minnesota as a non-member state, so PT Compact privileges are not available in Minnesota.
compact.quote: Non-Members (10) California Florida Hawaii Idaho Minnesota New Mexico New York Puerto Rico U.S. Virgin Islands Wyoming

apply_url.value: Applicants submit an online application and fees through the Minnesota Board of Physical Therapy's online services account, where they can track their application checklist.
apply_url.quote: After your online application and fees are received, Board staff will email you when your file has been opened with instructions on how to use your online services account

board.value: Minnesota Board of Occupational Therapy Practice
board.quote: The Board of Occupational Therapy Practice consists of 11 members appointed by the governor.

education.value: Applicants educated in the United States must complete all academic and fieldwork requirements of an occupational therapy program approved or accredited by ACOTE; applicants educated abroad must complete a program approved by a member association of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists.
education.quote: must successfully complete all academic and fieldwork requirements of an educational program for occupational therapists approved or accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education

national_exam.value: Applicants must achieve a qualifying score on the occupational therapist certification examination, with the qualifying score set by the Board as recommended by NBCOT; applicants arrange and pay for the exam themselves.
national_exam.quote: as recommended by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, or other national certification organization approved by the board.

state_exam.value: Minnesota law allows the Board to require occupational therapy practitioners to take an open-book jurisprudence examination on state laws and rules governing occupational therapy practice.
state_exam.quote: The board may require occupational therapy practitioners to take an open-book jurisprudence examination on state laws and rules regarding the practice of occupational therapy

background_check.value: Applicants for initial licensure must provide evidence of completing a criminal background check.
background_check.quote: evidence of completing a criminal background check according to section

application_fee.value: Minnesota statute sets the initial licensure fee for occupational therapists at $185; the Board may set licensure fees up to, but not above, the statutory amounts, and all fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: The initial licensure fee for occupational therapists is $185. The initial licensure fee for occupational therapy assistants is $105.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists who hold current NBCOT certification, including those licensed in another state, may be licensed by equivalency by submitting the standard initial application materials.
endorsement.quote: The board may license any person who holds current NBCOT certification as an occupational therapy practitioner.

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board issues temporary licenses to eligible new graduates awaiting the certification exam (who must practice under a licensed occupational therapist's supervision) and to applicants credentialed in another state or certified by NBCOT; a temporary license expires six months after issuance or when licensure is granted or denied, and is not renewable.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license expires six months from the date of issuance or on the date the board grants or denies licensure, whichever occurs first.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses must be renewed every two years, on or before the first day of the month after the licensee's birth month.
renewal.quote: licenses must be renewed every two years on or before the first day of the month after the licensee's birth month.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete at least 24 contact hours of continuing education in each two-year licensure period, and at least half of the required hours must be directly related to occupational therapy practice.
continuing_education.quote: A licensed occupational therapist must obtain a minimum of 24 contact hours of continuing education in the two-year licensure period.

compact.value: The OT Compact Commission lists Minnesota as accepting OT Compact privilege applications since January 12, 2026, with no jurisprudence requirement, a Minnesota state fee of $50 for OTs, and a $75 OT Compact fee.
compact.quote: Minnesota January 12, 2026 not required MN OT Practice Act $50 $50 $75

board.value: Minnesota Department of Health, Speech-Language Pathologist and Audiologist Licensing
board.quote: If you are interested in an educator license for speech-language pathology, please see the

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree, with all graduate coursework and clinical practicum completed at a program accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (or an equivalent determined by the commissioner).
education.quote: must have been initiated and completed at an institution whose program meets the current requirements and was accredited by the Educational Standards Board of the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology

national_exam.value: Applicants must complete the supervised clinical experience required by ASHA (or an equivalent) and achieve a qualifying score on the National Examination in Speech-Language Pathology.
national_exam.quote: must achieve a qualifying examination score on the National Examination in Speech-Language Pathology or Audiology

background_check.value: New applicants must complete an online Department of Human Services applicant background study, paying DHS directly, and pay the Department of Health a one-time $10.50 processing fee.
background_check.quote: New applicants are required to pay a fee to the Department of Human Services (DHS) for an online applicant background study.

application_fee.value: The initial speech-language pathology license fee is $200 plus a one-time $10.50 criminal background check surcharge, for a total of $210.50; background check fees paid to DHS are additional.
application_fee.quote: Initial Speech Language Pathology License Fee $200 + $10.50 CBC Surcharge Fee = $210.50

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed elsewhere may be licensed by reciprocity if they hold a current, unrestricted credential from a jurisdiction with equivalent or higher requirements and have kept unrestricted credentials in each jurisdiction for the last five years.
endorsement.quote: holds a current and unrestricted credential for the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology in another jurisdiction that has requirements equivalent to or higher than those in effect

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows must hold a clinical fellowship license, which expires 18 months after issuance or when the commissioner grants or denies licensure, whichever comes first, and may be renewed once.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A clinical fellowship license or doctoral externship license issued to a person pursuant to subdivision 2 expires 18 months after issuance or on the date the commissioner grants or denies licensure, whichever occurs first.

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist licenses are renewed every two years; the renewal application must be received by the Department of Health or postmarked at least 30 days before the license expiration date.
renewal.quote: An application for licensure renewal must be received by the Department of Health or postmarked at least 30 days before the expiration date.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete at least 30 contact hours of continuing education in the two years before license expiration, at least 20 of them directly related to their area of licensure, or meet ASHA's continuing education requirements.
continuing_education.quote: a minimum of 30 contact hours of continuing education obtained within the two years immediately preceding licensure expiration

compact.value: The ASLP-IC Commission lists Minnesota as not yet accepting compact privilege applications, with no jurisprudence exam required and the Minnesota state fee still to be determined.
compact.quote: Minnesota not yet not required MN Practice Act TBD $50

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the Minnesota Department of Health Licensing System by logging in, completing the application for the specific license, and paying online.
apply_url.quote: Go to the specific license in Minnesota Department of Health Licensing System then log-in to your account, complete the application and make payment.

board.value: Mississippi State Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The Board is a state licensing and regulatory agency authorized by the legislature to protect the public against the unqualified, incompetent, unprofessional and unlawful practice of physical therapy.

education.value: Applicants must be graduates of a CAPTE-accredited physical therapist program, with education verified directly to the Board by the institution or by official transcript; graduates of non-CAPTE programs in foreign countries need an education credential evaluation.
education.quote: Graduates of CAPTE-accredited programs - The education section on the online application must be completed, and verification of education reported directly to this office from the institution.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by FSBPT, with a minimum criterion-referenced scaled score of 600. Mississippi follows the FSBPT lifetime limit of six (6) exam attempts.
national_exam.quote: The score for licensure in Mississippi is automatically reported to the Board office from FSBPT. The minimum acceptable score is a criterion-reference scale score of 600.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Mississippi Jurisprudence Exam, an open-book exam taken through the online application, with a minimum score of 70.
state_exam.quote: No applicant shall be considered for licensure until a passing score is on file. The minimum acceptable score is 70 (seventy).

background_check.value: All new applicants must undergo a criminal history background check. The Board mails a fingerprint card after the application is started and fees are paid, and no license is issued until the results have been received and reviewed.
background_check.quote: All new applicants for licensure will be required to undergo a criminal history background check. After you have initiated the application process and paid applicable fees, the Board will mail a fingerprint card to you.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $125.00 application fee and a $150.00 physical therapist license fee, plus a $50.00 fingerprint/criminal history processing fee; exam applicants also pay a $50.00 Mississippi exam processing fee. All fees are non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: d. Fees: All fees are non-refundable. 1. Application fee - $125.00 2. License fee - PT $150.00 or PTA $125.00

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state may apply by reciprocity if they hold a valid, unrestricted license in good standing from another U.S. jurisdiction whose requirements are equivalent to or greater than Mississippi's.
endorsement.quote: The applicant has a valid unrestricted license from another jurisdiction of the United States. b. That the requirements for said license are equivalent to or greater than those required in this state

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants licensed in another state who have applied for a permanent Mississippi license may receive a temporary license for up to sixty (60) days. Exam candidates may receive a temporary license, practicing under direct supervision, for up to ninety (90) days beyond the next scheduled exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: licensed in another state and has filed an application with the Board for a permanent license in this state. This temporary license will be granted for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days.

renewal.value: Licenses renew biennially. The licensure period runs July 1 through June 30, with surnames A through L renewing in odd-numbered years and M through Z in even-numbered years; renewal applications filed after June 30 are subject to a late fee.
renewal.quote: The licensure period shall be construed as July 1 through June 30 of odd-numbered years for persons whose surnames begin with A through L and the licensure period shall be construed

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn 30 continuing competence units (CCU) each 2 year licensing period, with at least 7.5 CCU directly related to clinical practice, three (3) hours in ethics, professionalism or jurisprudence, and at least 15 CCU from Certified Activities. Compliance is reported through CE Broker.
continuing_education.quote: Regulations set the requirement of 30 continuing competence units (CCU) to be accrued during each 2 year licensing period (July 1- June 30).

compact.value: Mississippi is a member of the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact, effective July 16, 2018, and compact privileges are available. Applicants must pass the Mississippi Jurisprudence Exam before they can be approved for a compact privilege, then purchase it through the PT Compact website.
compact.quote: Physical Therapy Licensure Compact in Mississippi: Effective July 16, 2018

processing_time.value: Once all required documents in the application packet are received, the Board's average processing time is 1 to 2 days.
processing_time.quote: Following receipt of all required documents listed in the application packet, the average processing time is 1 to 2 days.

apply_url.value: New graduates begin the online application from the Board's Applying for Licensure - New Graduates page, which links to the application, the steps to licensure, and the fingerprint background check process.
apply_url.quote: After you have initiated the application process and paid applicable fees, the Board will mail a fingerprint card to you.

board.value: Mississippi State Department of Health, Professional Licensure Division
board.quote: The Mississippi State Department of Health's Professional Licensure division regulates and licenses certain health-related professions in Mississippi.

education.value: Applicants must hold a degree from an occupational therapist program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association or the board-recognized accrediting body, and must have completed a supervised field experience.
education.quote: For an occupational therapist, the program shall be accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association or the board-recognized accrediting body.

national_exam.value: Applicants must have passed an examination approved by the Department. The licensure rule does not name the exam, though the regulations elsewhere refer to certification by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).
national_exam.quote: 4. has passed an examination approved by the Department; and 5. has paid the required fee(s).

background_check.value: MSDH lists the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact among the professional licensure background checks processed through its SAFER system, with a $50.00 application fee and a $25 fingerprinting fee; regular state OT licensure is not on that list.
background_check.quote: Follow the steps outlined below using the SAFER system (administered by the Mississippi Department of Health

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $100.00 application fee and a $150.00 initial licensure fee for an occupational therapist. Fees are non-refundable.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed in another state, territory or jurisdiction may apply by endorsement if their license is in good standing, the requirements were equivalent to or greater than Mississippi's, and their NBCOT certification has not been subject to disciplinary action.
endorsement.quote: 1. the applicant is currently licensed to practice occupational therapy under the laws of another state, territory, or jurisdiction; and

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet licensure requirements but have not taken the approved exam or received results may receive a limited permit for up to ninety (90) days, practicing under the supervision of or in consultation with a Mississippi-licensed occupational therapist. Anyone who has taken but not passed the exam in another jurisdiction is not eligible.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: 1. A limited permit shall be granted for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days.

renewal.value: Occupational therapy licenses renew biennially, with the licensure period running May 1 through April 30 of even-numbered years. The OT renewal fee is $150.00.
renewal.quote: 1. The Board shall issue licenses which shall be subject to renewal biennially. 2. The licensure period shall be construed as May 1 through April 30 of even numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn 20 contact hours (2 CEUs) per licensure period: at least thirteen (13) live hours, of which at least six (6) relate to clinical practice, two (2) hours of ethics, and no more than seven (7) non-live hours. Current NBCOT certification may be submitted in lieu of CE certificates, except for the 2-hour ethics requirement.
continuing_education.quote: Regulations set the requirement of 20 contact hours (CH) or 2 Continuing Education Units (CEU) to be accrued during the licensure period.

compact.value: Mississippi participates in the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact (OTLC). compact.quote: The Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact (OTLC) allows eligible licensed occupational therapists and occupational therapy assistants

processing_time.value: MSDH asks applicants to allow 7 to 14 business days after receipt of all paperwork to receive a license.
