apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through MSDH's Professional Licensure application portal, linked from the Professional Licensure Applications page.
apply_url.quote: Please allow 7 to 14 business days after receipt of all paperwork to receive your license.

board.value: Mississippi State Department of Health, Professional Licensure Division
board.quote: The Mississippi State Department of Health's Professional Licensure division regulates and licenses certain health-related professions in Mississippi.

education.value: Applicants must hold at least a master's degree in speech-language pathology, communicative disorders, or speech and hearing science from an institution with a program accredited by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (or another accrediting body the Board deems appropriate), and complete the equivalent of nine (9) months of full-time Supervised Professional Employment.
education.quote: Education qualifications deemed equivalent to those specified in Section 73-38-9 shall be at least a master's degree, e.g., M.S., M.A., or M.Ed., in speech-language pathology

national_exam.value: Applicants must have passed the National Examination in Speech-Language Pathology, with the passing score recommended each year by the Advisory Council.
national_exam.quote: The applicant must have passed a National Examination in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology, either the National Examination in Speech-Language Pathology or the National Examination in Audiology.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $100.00 initial application fee and a $100.00 initial license fee; the initial temporary license fee is $75.00. Fees are nonrefundable.

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed in another state may apply by reciprocity but must show they meet all of Mississippi's general requirements and qualifications for licensure. A universal license is also available to people who establish residence in Mississippi.
endorsement.quote: An applicant for licensure by reciprocity shall submit to the Department, verified by oath, written evidence in form and content satisfactory to the Department that the applicant has met all requirements

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants entering the Supervised Professional Employment Plan (SPEP) must obtain a temporary license before the plan begins; it is issued for one 2-year period only and requires supervision by a regularly licensed SLP.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license shall be issued for one 2-year period only beginning on the date of issuance.

renewal.value: The licensure period runs July 1 through June 30, with all regular licenses expiring at midnight on June 30 of even-numbered years. The renewal fee is $100.00, and online renewals submitted between July 1 and September 30 carry a $50.00 late renewal penalty.
renewal.quote: The licensure period shall be construed as July 1 through June 30 with all regular licenses expiring at midnight on June 30 of even-numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn 20 contact hours (2 CEUs) per licensing term, with at least fifty (50) percent (10 contact hours) directly related to clinical practice. No carryover between licensure periods is allowed.
continuing_education.quote: Regulations set the requirement of 20 contact hours (CH) or 2 Continuing Education Units (CEU) to be accrued during the licensing term.

compact.value: Mississippi appears on the ASLP-IC Commission's state list but is not yet accepting compact privilege applications under the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact; no Mississippi jurisprudence exam is required and the Mississippi state fee is TBD.
compact.quote: Mississippi not yet not required MS Regulations TBD $50

processing_time.value: MSDH asks applicants to allow 7 to 14 business days after receipt of all paperwork to receive a license.
processing_time.quote: Please allow 7 to 14 business days after receipt of all paperwork to receive your license.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through MSDH's Professional Licensure application portal, linked from the Professional Licensure Applications page.
apply_url.quote: Please allow 7 to 14 business days after receipt of all paperwork to receive your license.

board.value: Missouri State Board of Registration for the Healing Arts (Advisory Commission for Physical Therapists)
board.quote: The Missouri Board of Healing Arts has become aware that someone has been calling licensees claiming to be from the Board of Healing Arts or the Division of Professional Registration

education.value: Applicants must show completion of a board-approved physical therapy education program (or eligibility to graduate from one within ninety days); graduates of a program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Physical Therapy Education (if graduated after 1988) are deemed to meet the education requirement.
education.quote: or if graduated after 1988, the Commission on Accreditation for Physical Therapy Education or its successor, is deemed to have complied with the educational qualifications of this subsection.

national_exam.value: Applicants must register with the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) to sit for the licensing examination, and the passing point is a scaled score of 600 on a scale of 200 to 800.
national_exam.quote: This passing point will be set equal to a scaled score of 600 based on a scale of 200 to 800.

state_exam.value: Applicants must complete the Missouri jurisprudence examination, which is returned with the application and scored by the Board; a score of 75% or higher is required.
state_exam.quote: The Board will score it. A score of 75% or higher is required.

background_check.value: All applicants must complete a criminal background check using the Missouri State Highway Patrol applicant fingerprint process included in the application packet.
background_check.quote: All applicants for licensure are required to complete a criminal background check.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $25; applicants who also request a temporary license pay an additional $10.
application_fee.quote: The application fee is $25. If you are applying for a temporary license, please send an additional fee of $10.

endorsement.value: The board issues a license to a physical therapist who holds an active license in another jurisdiction with substantially equal or greater requirements and has no violations, suspensions or revocations; the applicant must also pass a board test on Missouri physical therapy laws and rules.
endorsement.quote: The board shall issue a license to any physical therapist who possesses an active license in another jurisdiction and who has had no violations, suspensions or revocations of a license to practice physical therapy in any jurisdiction

temporary_or_provisional.value: A first-time examinee may pay a temporary license fee and submit an agreement-to-supervise form signed by a supervising Missouri physical therapist to obtain a nonrenewable temporary license to practice under supervision.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: may pay a temporary license fee and submit an agreement-to-supervise form, which is signed by the applicant's supervising physical therapist, to the board and obtain without examination a nonrenewable temporary license.

renewal.value: Permanent physical therapist licenses expire on January 31 of each even-numbered year.
renewal.quote: All permanent physical therapist licenses expire on January 31 of each even-numbered year.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must accumulate thirty hours of continuing education every two years to be eligible for relicensure, reviewed at renewal in each even-numbered year.
continuing_education.quote: shall accumulate thirty hours of continuing education every two years to be eligible for relicensure

compact.value: Missouri participates in the PT Compact: physical therapists can hold a compact privilege to practice in Missouri, and compact privilege holders must complete a Missouri jurisprudence examination before purchasing a privilege.
compact.quote: Physical Therapists and Physical Therapist Assistants Compact Privilege holders are required to complete a jurisprudence examination before purchasing a compact privilege.

processing_time.value: The board asks applicants to allow a minimum of six (6) weeks for processing once the application and license fee have been received and the application is placed in the queue.
processing_time.quote: Please allow a minimum of six (6) weeks for the processing of your application once the Board has received the application, license fee, and it is placed into the queue.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through a MOPRO account (selecting apply for license) or by using the paper Physical Therapist application posted on the Healing Arts application forms page.
apply_url.quote: Once you have created your account, you can select "apply for license" to search for the appropriate profession type.

board.value: Missouri Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: The data in this website is provided, controlled and maintained by the Missouri Board of Occupational Therapy (Board) and its employees and is not modifiable by any outside source.

education.value: Applicants must be certified by a board-approved certifying entity, whose certification of an occupational therapist requires a degree or certificate from an ACOTE-accredited occupational therapy program, completion of the required fieldwork, and a passing examination score.
education.quote: A degree/certificate in occupational therapy from an occupational therapy educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) or its successor organization

national_exam.value: Applicants apply to NBCOT for the national exam, and the certifying entity must send verification of the applicant's credentials directly to the Missouri Board of Occupational Therapy.
national_exam.quote: Please visit the website for NBCOT to apply for the national exam

state_exam.value: All applicants must pass the open-book Missouri Jurisprudence Examination, taken from the rules and statutes, with a score no lower than 80% and return it with the application.
state_exam.quote: All applicants are required to pass the Jurisprudence Examination with a score no lower than 80%.

background_check.value: All applications received on or after June 30, 2012 require fingerprinting.
background_check.quote: All applications received on or after June 30, 2012 will require fingerprinting.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $40 for an occupational therapist license and $20 for a limited permit; fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: (A) Application for Licensure as an Occupational Therapist Fee $40 (B) Application for Licensure as an Occupational Therapy Assistant Fee $20 (C) Application for Limited Permit Fee $20

endorsement.value: A person who holds a valid current license from another state, U.S. territory or the District of Columbia and has been licensed there for at least one year may apply for a Missouri license by reciprocity in the same profession and at the same practice level.
endorsement.quote: and who has been licensed for at least one year in such other jurisdiction, may submit an application for license in Missouri in the same occupation or profession

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may issue a limited permit to a person eligible to sit for the first available certification examination; it allows practice under the supervision of a Missouri-licensed occupational therapist and ends when second-exam results are received, or stays valid an additional sixty days after the person passes.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The limited permit shall allow the person to practice occupational therapy under the supervision of a person currently licensed

renewal.value: Missouri occupational therapy licenses are renewed on June 30 of odd-numbered years.
renewal.quote: These provisions govern the issuance and renewal of licenses (Renewal of licenses are June 30th of the odd years) as well as the discipline of licensees

continuing_education.value: At license renewal, licensees must verify completion of 24 Continuing Competency Credits (CCC) and keep documentation for two years after renewal; licensees new to a cycle complete a prorated number.
continuing_education.quote: At the time of license renewal, the licensee shall verify completion of twenty-four (24) Continuing Competency Credits (CCC) on the renewal form.

compact.value: The Missouri Board of Occupational Therapy's site points eligible licensees to the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact as an alternative method for providing services in other member states.
compact.quote: The Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact allows eligible licensed occupational therapists an alternative method for providing services in other member states.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the state's MOPRO online system, which the board's home page lists as the place for applying for a license; paper forms are on the board's Applications page.
apply_url.quote: If you need help registering for your account or have other questions, please watch this short video

board.value: Missouri State Board of Registration for the Healing Arts (Advisory Commission for Speech-Language Pathologists and Audiologists)
board.quote: The Missouri Board of Healing Arts has become aware that someone has been calling licensees claiming to be from the Board of Healing Arts or the Division of Professional Registration

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree from a program accredited by, or in accreditation candidate status with, ASHA's Council on Academic Accreditation (or another board-approved accreditor), and must complete a supervised clinical fellowship.
education.quote: Hold a master's or a doctoral degree from a program that was awarded "accreditation candidate" status or is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association

national_exam.value: The required examination is the National Examination for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology (Praxis), with the passing score set at the minimum ASHA requires for the certificate of clinical competence.
national_exam.quote: The examination given pursuant to section 345.050.1(4), RSMo shall be the National Examination for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology.

background_check.value: The Board makes independent inquiries into each applicant's background in addition to the materials the applicant submits.
background_check.quote: In addition to the materials you are required to submit, the Board makes independent inquiries into your background.

application_fee.value: The licensure application fee is $25, payable by personal check, cashier's check or money order; fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: The fee is $25. The Board can accept payment in the form of a personal check, cashier's check, or money order.

endorsement.value: A person with a valid current speech-language pathologist license from another state, U.S. territory, the military or the District of Columbia who has been licensed there for at least one year may apply for a Missouri license, and the board waives examination, education or experience requirements when the other state verifies the person met its requirements.
endorsement.quote: and who has been licensed for at least one year in the other jurisdiction, may submit an application for a speech-language pathologist or audiologist license in Missouri

temporary_or_provisional.value: Missouri issues a provisional license for the clinical fellowship (supervised postgraduate professional experience); it is valid for one year and may be renewed one time with board approval.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The provisional license is valid for one (1) year. The license may be renewed one (1) time with board approval.

renewal.value: Permanent speech-language pathologist licenses expire triennially on January 31, and the expiration date is printed on the license.
renewal.quote: All permanent speech-language pathologist and audiologist licenses expire triennially on January 31. The expiration date will be printed on your license.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete and report at least 30 hours of continuing education per reporting period, which the rule describes as biennial; dual SLP and audiology licensees need 30 hours in each.
continuing_education.quote: Each licensee shall biennially complete and report at least thirty (30) hours of continuing education.

compact.value: Missouri has enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact in statute (section 345.085, RSMo).
compact.quote: The purpose of this Compact is to facilitate interstate practice of audiology and speech-language pathology with the goal of improving public access to audiology and speech-language pathology services.

processing_time.value: The board asks applicants to allow a minimum of six (6) weeks for processing once the application and license fee have been received and the application is placed in the queue.
processing_time.quote: Please allow a minimum of six (6) weeks for the processing of your application once the Board has received the application, license fee, and it is placed into the queue.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through a MOPRO account (selecting apply for license) or by using the paper Speech-Language Pathologist and/or Audiologist application posted on the Healing Arts application forms page.
apply_url.quote: Once you have created your account, you can select "apply for license" to search for the appropriate profession type.

board.value: Montana Board of Physical, Rehabilitative, and Developmental Health Care Professionals

temporary_or_provisional.value: Physical therapist applicants may be issued a provisional license naming a licensed physical therapist who provides direct supervision; it is valid until the applicant passes the exam, and only one is issued per applicant.

renewal.quote: Physical Therapist: April 1 Physical Therapist Assistant: April 1 Speech-Language Pathologist: February 1

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed in a state on the board's substantial equivalency list are treated as routine applications as to education, examination, and experience requirements, though applications may be nonroutine on other grounds.
endorsement.quote: License applications from individuals licensed in substantially equivalent states are routine applications as to the education, examination, and experience requirements for licensure.

renewal.quote: Speech-Language Pathologist: February 1 Speech-Language Pathologist-Audiologist (dual): February 1 Speech-Language Pathology Assistant: February 1 The renewal period for each license type opens 60 days before its renewal date.

continuing_education.quote: On or before November 1 of each odd-numbered year, individuals holding an active license in the State of Nebraska must complete at least 20 hours of acceptable continuing education for a physical therapist

education.quote: A program for the education of occupational therapists which is recognized by the Department and accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT licensure examination, with documentation of passing sent directly to the Department by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy.
national_exam.quote: Documentation of passing the licensure examination sent directly to the Department from the National Board of Certification in Occupational Therapy.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit fingerprints for a criminal background check through the Nebraska State Patrol, which charges a $75 fee.

renewal.quote: The annual renewal date is October 1st of each year. All licenses issued by the board will expire on September 30th of each year.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must earn at least 15 continuing education contact hours per year, during the renewal period of October 1 through September 30; up to 15 hours may be carried over into the next licensing year.
continuing_education.quote: Every licensed occupational therapist and occupational therapy assistant must earn a minimum of 15 continuing education contact hours per year during each year of licensure.

compact.value: New Mexico's 2026 bill to enact the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact (HB 13) did not become law; the Legislature lists it as died.
compact.quote: Title OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY LICENSURE COMPACT Sponsor Elizabeth "Liz" Thomson Gail Armstrong Joshua N. Hernandez Jenifer Jones Current Location Died (API.)

processing_time.value: Once an application file is complete, the board issues a license number within 2 to 5 business days.
processing_time.quote: Q: How long does the application process take? Once your application file is complete, a license number will be issued within 2–5 business days.

apply_url.value: Applications must be submitted online through the NM-PLUS licensing portal, which is linked from the board's licensing page.
apply_url.quote: Application for Licensure The application must be submitted online through NM-PLUS.

board.value: New Mexico Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensing Practices Board
board.quote: Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensing Practices: Overview and Contact Information The board licenses and regulates speech-language pathologists, audiologists, and hearing aid dispensers.

education.value: Applicants need a master's degree plus either ASHA certification or completion of a Clinical Fellow Year (CFY), along with passing national exams.
education.quote: A master’s degree and ASHA Certification, or completion of a Clinical Fellow Year (CFY) and evidence of successful completion of national exams

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass a nationally recognized standard examination in speech-language pathology.
national_exam.quote: proof of having passed a nationally recognized standard examination in speech-language pathology;

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the New Mexico jurisprudence examination with a grade of no less than seventy percent.
state_exam.quote: proof of having passed the jurisprudence examination with a grade of no less than seventy percent.

background_check.value: The board states that it does not require background checks.
background_check.quote: New Mexico Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensers Practicing Board does not require background checks.

application_fee.value: The full licensure application fee is $100 for a speech-language pathologist and $50 for a clinical fellow (CFY); all fees are nonrefundable.
application_fee.quote: Full Licensure Application Speech-Language Pathologist & Audiologist $100 Clinical Fellow (CFY) $50

endorsement.value: A speech-language pathologist with an active license in good standing from a qualifying state can be licensed in New Mexico.
endorsement.quote: evidence of successful completion of national exams, or an active license in good standing from a qualifying state

temporary_or_provisional.value: New Mexico issues a clinical fellow (CF) license, renewed annually; the clinical fellowship year must be completed within 36 consecutive months, and the national exam must be passed within the first 12 months of clinical fellow licensure.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The CFY must be completed within a maximum period of 36 consecutive months. Prior to or during the first 12 months of clinical fellow licensure, the clinical fellow must take and pass a nationally recognized examination

renewal.value: Speech-language pathology licenses are renewed every two years on or before January 30 of the renewal year; a grace period with a late fee ends March 31.
renewal.quote: All licensees except clinical fellows and apprentices shall apply for license renewal biennially on or before January 30 of the renewal year

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 20 hours of continuing education every two years, in the field of licensure or a related field if justified to the board office.
continuing_education.quote: The board requires 20 hours of continuing education every two years. These may be distributed over the two year period, or they may all be obtained in one year.

compact.value: New Mexico's 2026 bill to join the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact (HB 11) did not become law; the Legislature lists it as died.
compact.quote: Title AUDIOLOGY & SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY COMPACT Sponsor Elizabeth "Liz" Thomson Gail Armstrong Jenifer Jones Anita Gonzales Michelle Paulene Abeyta Current Location Died (API.)

processing_time.value: For expedited licensure, the board's staff must process a complete application and issue the expedited license to a qualified applicant within 30 days.
processing_time.quote: Upon receipt of a complete application, the board's staff shall process the application and issue the expedited license to a qualified applicant within 30 days.

apply_url.value: Applications and renewals are submitted through the Regulation and Licensing Department's online licensing system; paper applications are no longer accepted.
apply_url.quote: The New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department has implemented an online licensing system for the Speech-Language Pathology, Audiology, and Hearing Aid Dispensing Practices Board applications and license renewals.

board.value: New York State Board for Physical Therapy
board.quote: NY State Education Department Office of the Professions State Board for Physical Therapy 89 Washington Avenue

education.value: Applicants educated in a New York State registered or CAPTE/APTA-accredited program must hold a doctoral degree in physical therapy.
education.quote: you must have: a doctoral degree in physical therapy. Physical Therapist Program Located Outside the United States

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), or an examination the Department determines to be comparable in content.
national_exam.quote: The National Physical Therapy Examination, or an examination determined by the Department to be comparable in content, is required for physical therapy licensure in New York.

application_fee.value: The fee for licensure as a physical therapist (licensure and first registration) is $294.
application_fee.quote: The fee for licensure as a physical therapist is $294.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another jurisdiction who do not meet current New York education requirements may apply by endorsement if they have at least 3 years of practice acceptable to the State Board in the 7 years before applying and an education acceptable to the Department.
endorsement.quote: have at least 3 years of practice acceptable to the State Board for Physical Therapy in the 7 years immediately preceding the application for licensure by endorsement

temporary_or_provisional.value: A limited permit ($70 fee) lets a licensure applicant practice under the on-site supervision of a New York licensed physical therapist and is valid for 6 months. New graduates of accredited programs may also work under supervision for 90 days after graduation without a permit once they have filed the licensure, limited permit and exam applications.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Limited permits for physical therapists and physical therapist assistants are valid for 6 months, effective February 9, 2003.

renewal.value: Physical therapists must renew their registration every three years; the first renewal after licensure is prorated so that later renewals fall in the licensee's birth month.
renewal.quote: Registration is for a three-year period (except the first renewal after licensure that is prorated to move licensees to month of birth renewal).

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 36 hours of approved continuing education in each three-year registration period; newly licensed physical therapists do not need continuing education during their initial three-year registration period.
continuing_education.quote: you are required to complete 36 hours of approved continuing education during each three-year registration period.

compact.value: The PT Compact Commission lists New York as a non-member state, where PT Compact legislation has not been introduced, so compact privileges are not available in New York.
compact.quote: Non-Members (10) California Florida Hawaii Idaho Minnesota New Mexico New York

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the Online Form 1 application for physical therapists, linked from the Office of the Professions application forms page.
apply_url.quote: All applicants for licensure must initially submit Form 1 along with the $294 (physical therapist) or $103 (physical therapy assistant) licensure and first registration fee.

board.value: New York State Board for Occupational Therapy
board.quote: NY State Education Department Office of the Professions State Board for Occupational Therapy 89 Washington Avenue

education.value: Graduates of New York State registered or AOTA-accredited programs must hold a baccalaureate or entry-level master's degree in occupational therapy, or a post-baccalaureate certificate in occupational therapy from an institution acceptable to the Department.
education.quote: a baccalaureate or entry-level master's degree in occupational therapy, or a post-baccalaureate certificate in occupational therapy from an institution acceptable to the Department.

national_exam.value: Occupational therapists must pass the NBCOT OTR examination; the passing score is 450.
national_exam.quote: Occupational therapists must pass the NBCOT OTR examination and occupational therapy assistants must pass the COTA examination of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, Inc. (NBCOT).

application_fee.value: The fee for licensure as an occupational therapist is $294.
application_fee.quote: The fee for licensure as an occupational therapist is $294.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed elsewhere apply with the standard application and must have each jurisdiction in which they are or have been licensed verify the license on Form 3.
endorsement.quote: Complete this section before sending the entire form to the licensing/certifying authority of each jurisdiction in which you are or have been licensed/certified.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A limited permit ($70 fee) lets a program graduate practice under supervision until licensing exam results are received; it is valid for one year and may be renewed once, at the Department's discretion, for illness or other extenuating circumstances.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The limited permit is valid for one year. A limited permit may be renewed once, at the discretion of the Department, due to personal or family illness

renewal.value: The occupational therapy license is valid for life, but the registration needed to practice must be renewed every 3 years.
renewal.quote: Your professional license is valid for life. However, registrations are valid for 3 years.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 36 hours of continuing competency learning activities every 3-year registration cycle, at least 24 hours in professional subjects, with no more than two-thirds through self-directed online study.
continuing_education.quote: must complete 36 hours of continuing competency learning activities during every 3-year registration cycle.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the Online Form 1 application for occupational therapists, linked from the Office of the Professions application forms page.
apply_url.quote: All applicants for licensure must initially submit Form 1 along with the $294 (occupational therapist) or $147 (occupational therapy assistant) licensure and first registration fee.

board.value: New York State Board for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: NY State Education Department Office of the Professions State Board for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology 89 Washington Avenue

education.value: Applicants must hold a graduate degree in speech-language pathology from a New York State registered program, an ASHA-accredited program, or the equivalent, and must complete at least 36 weeks and 1,260 hours of supervised experience after the degree requirements are met.
education.quote: You must have obtained a graduate degree in speech-language pathology from a New York State registered licensure qualifying program, a program accredited by the American Speech Language and Hearing Association (ASHA), or the equivalent.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass Praxis Examination 5331 (speech-language pathology) with a minimum score of 162, with scores sent directly from ETS to agency code R7747.
national_exam.quote: Candidates for licensure in Speech-Language Pathology must take Praxis Examination 5331. It is scored on a scale of 100-200. 162 the minimum acceptable passing score.

application_fee.value: The fee for licensure and first registration is $294.
application_fee.quote: The fee for licensure and first registration is $294.

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another U.S. jurisdiction may be licensed by endorsement (Path A) with an acceptable program including at least 60 semester hours, at least two years of post-licensure experience within the six years before applying, a passing Praxis score, certification such as ASHA's, and good standing in every jurisdiction.
endorsement.quote: have at least two years of acceptable professional experience in speech-language pathology or audiology, as appropriate, provided that such experience occurs following licensure in such jurisdiction and within six years immediately preceding application for licensure by endorsement

temporary_or_provisional.value: An optional limited license ($70 fee) lets an applicant practice under the supervision of a licensed speech-language pathologist to complete the experience requirement; it is valid for one year and may be renewed for additional one-year periods until the experience is completed.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: You may apply for limited licensure by submitting an Application for Limited License as a Speech-Language Pathologist (Form 1LL) and $70 fee along with, or after submitting an Application for Licensure (Form 1) and fee.

renewal.value: The license does not expire, but the registration required to practice expires and must be renewed every three years.
renewal.quote: Note: Your registration, which is required to practice, expires every three years. Licenses do not expire.

continuing_education.value: SLPs must complete 30 hours of continuing competency learning activities every three-year registration cycle, at least 20 of them in a professional area, with no more than two-thirds through self-directed online study.
continuing_education.quote: Each licensed speech-language pathologist and audiologist in practice is required to complete 30 hours of continuing competency learning activities during every three-year registration cycle.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the Online Form 1 application for speech-language pathologists, linked from the Office of the Professions application forms page.
apply_url.quote: All applicants for licensure must initially submit Form 1 along with the $294 licensure and first registration fee.

board.value: North Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
board.quote: Click here to go to the North Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners website

education.value: Physical therapist applicants must have graduated from a physical therapist program accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Office of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation.
education.quote: has been graduated from a physical therapist program accredited by an agency recognized by either the U.S. Office of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the national physical therapist examination; the Board's passing point is a scaled score of 600 on the 200 to 800 score range adopted by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy.
national_exam.quote: The criterion-referenced passing point shall be equal to a scaled score of 600 based on a score range of 200 - 800 as adopted by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy

state_exam.value: All applicants, whether applying by examination or by endorsement, must complete the Board's online Jurisprudence Exercise 1 on the North Carolina Physical Therapy Practice Act, Board rules and position statements.
state_exam.quote: All applicants for licensure for exam shall furnish proof of completion of the Jurisprudence Exercise 1 as set forth in 21 NCAC 48G .0105(7).

background_check.value: All applicants must consent to a criminal history record check, with fingerprints provided to the State Bureau of Investigation; the cost of the check and fingerprinting is paid by the applicant.
background_check.quote: The cost of the criminal history record check and the fingerprinting shall be borne by the applicant.

application_fee.value: The application fee for physical therapist licensure is $150, and it is not refundable.
application_fee.quote: application for physical therapist licensure, one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00);

endorsement.value: Physical therapists initially licensed in another state by examination may apply for licensure by endorsement; they must show a license in effect when they apply, exam scores meeting the North Carolina passing level, and completion of Jurisprudence Exercise 1.
endorsement.quote: Only those persons initially licensed in another state by virtue of examination shall be considered for endorsement.

temporary_or_provisional.value: North Carolina does not issue temporary permits to new PT graduates: the rules allowing them were repealed in August 1998, and in 2021 a Board task force and rules committee declined to recommend reinstating them.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The Public Protection Task Force and Rules Committee determined they would not support or recommend to the Board reinstatement of Board rules for Temporary Permits for new graduates

renewal.value: Licenses must be renewed every year between November 1 and January 31; licenses that are not renewed automatically lapse.
renewal.quote: Every licensed physical therapist or physical therapist assistant shall, from November 1 through January 31 at close of business of every year, apply to the Board for a renewal of licensure

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must accumulate 30 points of continuing competence activities in each 25-month reporting period to be eligible for renewal, and every licensee must complete a Board jurisprudence exercise each reporting period.
continuing_education.quote: For individuals licensed prior to January 1, 2009, during each reporting period thereafter, each physical therapist must accumulate 30 points

compact.value: North Carolina issues PT Compact privileges, which are purchased through the PT Compact; holders must complete Jurisprudence Exercise 1 within 30 days of purchasing or renewing the privilege or it may be terminated.
compact.quote: In North Carolina, Jurisprudence Exercise 1 must be completed within thirty (30) days of purchasing a Compact Privilege (initial and renewal), or your privilege may be terminated.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the Board's New Applications page, choosing licensure by examination or licensure by endorsement; every application requires a non-refundable fee.
apply_url.quote: All applications must include a non-refundable fee to begin processing by the Board.

board.value: North Carolina Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: North Carolina Board of Occupational Therapy 4140 ParkLake Ave, Suite 100, Raleigh NC 27612

education.value: Occupational therapist applicants must have completed an accredited occupational therapy educational curriculum and the required supervised fieldwork.
education.quote: Applicants for licensure as an occupational therapist must also have successfully completed an accredited occupational therapy educational curriculum and the required supervised fieldwork as determined by the Board.

national_exam.value: Applicants must have passed the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) exam.
national_exam.quote: Licensure is offered to an OT or an OTA who has graduated from an accredited curriculum including field work requirements and passed the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) exam.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Board's online jurisprudence exam on the North Carolina OT Practice Act and Board rules, scoring 100% on 30 multiple-choice questions; there is no fee and it may be retaken.
state_exam.quote: You are required to score a 100% on the exam. The exam is thirty (30) multiple choice questions randomly pulled from a large bank of questions.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay $10 to purchase the online application and a non-refundable $100 licensure fee.
application_fee.quote: Fee: $100.00. This fee is non-refundable, payable by credit card (Visa, Mastercard or Discover)

endorsement.value: The Board may exempt applicants from certain licensure requirements if they prove current OT licensure in another state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or Guam whose standards the Board considers substantially equivalent or higher.
endorsement.quote: The Board may exempt an applicant from certain licensure requirements if the applicant presents proof satisfactory to the Board of current licensure as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board does not offer a temporary license; applicants must complete the licensure process and be issued a regular license before they may practice.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The Board does not offer a temporary license for individuals entering the State who wish to practice before completing the licensure process and being issued a Regular license.

renewal.value: Licenses are renewed every year online between April 1 and June 30; the renewal fee is $50, with an additional $50 late renewal fee.
renewal.quote: Online renewals begin April 1 and end June 30th of every year.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must document at least 15 continuing competence activity points for each annual renewal, including at least one point in ethics; licensees renewing for the first time are not required to provide points.
continuing_education.quote: documentation showing proof of completion of a minimum of 15 continuing competence activity (CCA) points, including at least one CCA point in ethics

compact.value: North Carolina enacted the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact when the Governor signed House Bill 224 on June 11, 2021.
compact.quote: On June 11, Governor Roy Cooper signed House Bill 224 making North Carolina the fifth state to enact the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact (OT Compact).

processing_time.value: Licenses are usually issued within 1 to 2 weeks after the application and all required documentation are received and processed by the Board office.
processing_time.quote: Licenses are usually issued on Fridays within one(1) to two (2) weeks after the application and all required documentation is received and processed by the Board office.

apply_url.value: Applicants purchase an online application from the Board's Application Process page, then complete and submit it online.
apply_url.quote: An application may be purchased online (Visa, MasterCard or Discover) for $10.00.

board.value: North Carolina Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathologists and Audiologists
board.quote: North Carolina Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathologists and Audiologists

education.value: Applicants must hold at least a master's degree in speech and language pathology from an accredited institution, with 75 semester hours of coursework and at least 400 clock hours of supervised clinical experience.
education.quote: Possess at least a master's degree in speech and language pathology or qualifications deemed equivalent by the Board under rules duly adopted by the Board under this Article.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the speech-language pathology specialty examination administered by the Educational Testing Service (ETS), which Board rule designates as the required written examination.
national_exam.quote: The special examinations in speech and language pathology and audiology, which are part of the National Teacher's Examination, administered by the Educational Testing Service, will constitute the written examination required.

state_exam.value: Applicants complete an open-book quiz covering North Carolina licensure at the end of the application.
state_exam.quote: For either license applicant complete the Open Book Quiz at the end of the application. This quiz covers licensure in the state of NC.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $30 and is non-refundable; the permanent license fee is $60, and online payments carry a convenience charge.
application_fee.quote: The application fee is $30, the permanent license fee is $60, and for online payments a convenience charge is applied.

endorsement.value: SLPs who hold an active, full, unrestricted license in another state apply for reciprocal licensure, submitting an official license verification from one state and official transcripts showing the master's or doctoral degree conferred.
endorsement.quote: This page is for licensees who hold an active, full, unrestricted license to practice speech-language pathology or audiology in another state.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have not yet completed the required supervised professional experience and passed the exam must hold a temporary license, which is valid only during the supervised experience period, cannot be renewed, and carries a fee of up to $40.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A temporary license is required when an applicant has not completed the required supervised experience and passed the required examination.

renewal.value: Licenses are renewed annually; the renewal fee is $60 and is due on the date the license was issued.
renewal.quote: The renewal fee is $60.00 and is due on the date your license was issued.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 30 hours of continuing professional education every three years, sponsored by ASHA, the North Carolina Speech-Hearing-Language Association, the NC Department of Public Instruction, or other Board-approved equivalents.
continuing_education.quote: Beginning January 1, 2009 each licensee must complete 30 hours every three years of continuing professional education in their fields

compact.value: North Carolina has enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, codified in the General Statutes as the Interstate Compact for Audiology and Speech Pathology.
compact.quote: The purpose of this Compact is to facilitate interstate practice of audiology and speech-language pathology with the goal of improving public access to audiology and speech-language pathology services.

apply_url.value: Out-of-state licensees apply online using the Board's Reciprocal Application form, linked from its Reciprocal Licensure page.
apply_url.quote: To apply online please fill out your application using the Reciprocal Application form

board.value: North Dakota State Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: © 2026 ND Board of Physical Therapy. All Rights Reserved.

education.value: Applicants must have an official transcript showing completion of an accredited physical therapist program sent directly from the school (electronic transcripts from the school are accepted) before a license is issued.
education.quote: Official Transcript indicating completion of an accredited physical therapist program, must be sent directly from the school of graduation prior to being issued a license.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), registering online through the FSBPT; FSBPT, not the North Dakota board, determines exam eligibility.
national_exam.quote: Applications for the NPTE must be done online through the FSBPT. Your school will need to notify FSBPT that you have either graduated or are on track to graduate.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass an open-book jurisprudence exam on the North Dakota PT rules and practice act, which is included in the online application, before a license is issued.
state_exam.quote: The Juris Prudence is included in the online application. The Juris Prudence Exam must be passed prior to issuance of a license.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a fingerprint-based criminal background check, required since July 1, 2018; the $43.00 BCI fee is paid to the board with the application and the board mails a fingerprint packet.
background_check.quote: Effective July 1, 2018 criminal background checks are required for licensure as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant in North Dakota.

application_fee.value: Physical therapist applicants must pay a non-refundable $200 application fee plus the criminal background check fee.
application_fee.quote: Applicants must pay a $200 application fee plus the current criminal background fee.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed in another state apply by endorsement: they complete the online application and jurisprudence exam, have every state where they hold or held a license send verification, have FSBPT forward their NPTE scores, and upload employment verification from their last two employers.
endorsement.quote: Contact all states you hold/held a license in and have that Board send a verification of your license to the ND Board.

renewal.value: Licenses renew every year by January 31st, and the renewal fee is $100; a license not renewed by that date is expired.
renewal.quote: The license renewal fee is $100. Licenses must be renewed by January 31st every year.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must obtain twenty-five units of continuing competence every two years to be eligible for renewal, with no carryover of units to the next reporting period.
continuing_education.quote: All physical therapists and physical therapist assistants must obtain twenty-five units of continuing competence every two years to be eligible for licensure renewal.

compact.value: North Dakota is a PT Compact member state; a North Dakota compact privilege for a PT costs $85 in total ($40 state fee plus $45 commission fee), and the jurisprudence exam must be passed before applying.
compact.quote: North Dakota PT Fees $85 Total CP Fee $40 State CP Fee $45 Commission CP Fee

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the board's online license application, linked from the Physical Therapist Initial Application Instructions page.
apply_url.quote: Complete the online license application as a Physical Therapist. Once your application is received, a BCI fingerprint packet will be mailed to you.

board.value: North Dakota State Board of Occupational Therapy Practice
board.quote: © 2026 North Dakota State Board of Occupational Therapy Practice. All Rights Reserved.

education.value: Applicants must hold a degree from an occupational therapy program accredited by ACOTE, or a foreign occupational therapy degree that NBCOT deems comparable.
education.quote: The applicant has a degree from an occupational therapy program accredited by the accreditation council for occupational therapy education or a degree from a foreign occupational therapy program

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT occupational therapist registered (OTR) certification examination.
national_exam.quote: The applicant has passed the occupational therapist registered certification examination administered by the national board for certification in occupational therapy.

state_exam.value: All new and reciprocity applicants must complete an open-book jurisprudence exam of 20 questions on the laws and rules governing OT practice in North Dakota; the license is not issued until it is completed.
state_exam.quote: This is an exam over the laws and rules governing OT Practice in ND. It is 20 questions and is open book.

background_check.value: The board reported in February 2026 that it has received authority under North Dakota law to perform criminal history checks through BCI, with FBI final approval still pending.
background_check.quote: The Board has received authority by ND law to perform Criminal History Checks through BCI. BCI is working with the FBI for final approval which may take a few months.

application_fee.value: Occupational therapist applicants pay a combined initial application and license fee of $200, or $125 if the application is received after 6/30 and on or before 12/31 of an odd year.
application_fee.quote: Initial Application and License fee based on date application received by board office:

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed in another state apply by reciprocity and must have license verifications sent from every state where they currently hold or have held a license, send a copy of another state's laws and rules, and complete the jurisprudence exam.
endorsement.quote: Those applying for a license by reciprocity will need to have verifications sent from every state in which you currently hold or have held licensure

temporary_or_provisional.value: Recent graduates who have not yet passed the NBCOT exam may apply for a limited permit, which is issued for four months and can be extended once for another four months; applicants must take the exam within four months of completing their education and experience requirements.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Applicants for a limited permit must take the examination within four months of completion of the education and experience requirements.

renewal.value: Licenses must be renewed every 2 years, by June 30 of even-numbered years.
renewal.quote: The Law requires all licensees to renew their license every 2 years, by June 30 of the even-numbered years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete a minimum of twenty contact hours of continuing education within the twenty-four months before renewal; those first licensed partway through a cycle need 10 or 0 hours for that first period. Continuing education must relate to occupational therapy practice and the licensee's current or intended area of practice.
continuing_education.quote: 20 contact hours are required if initially licensed after June thirtieth of the even-numbered year and before July first of the odd-numbered year.

compact.value: North Dakota has enacted the OT Licensure Compact (ND Century Code 43-40.1, effective 8/1/2025), but the compact is not yet issuing licenses or accepting applications.
compact.quote: ND Century Code 43-40.1 - Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact Effective 8/1/2025. However, it is not yet issuing licenses or accepting applications.

processing_time.value: The board states that licenses are typically issued within a week after all completed documents are received.
processing_time.quote: Licenses are typically issued within a week after all completed documents are received.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the board's online application, which accepts credit card payment and document uploads, linked from the Requirements for Licensure page.
apply_url.quote: You may now apply for a license by completing the online application and paying with a credit card.

board.value: North Dakota State Board of Examiners on Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology
board.quote: Welcome to the official site for the North Dakota State Board of Examiners on Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology!

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's degree in speech-language pathology from an educational institution recognized by the board, and must have official graduate and undergraduate transcripts sent directly to the board.
education.quote: Master's degree in Speech-Language Pathology from an educational institution recognized by the Board and (b) a passing score on a national exam (Praxis Exam).

national_exam.value: Applicants must provide proof of a passing Praxis score; applicants without that documentation may upload proof of current ASHA certification instead.
national_exam.quote: Proof of passing PRAXIS test score. If you do not have documentation of passing PRAXIS test score, then upload proof of current ASHA certification.

application_fee.value: Applicants pay a $100.00 application fee; the board's fee schedule also lists a $250.00 re-licensing fee.
application_fee.quote: Credit card payment must be remitted at time of application submission. Applications withdrawn after submission are subject to a non-refundable application processing fee.

endorsement.value: The board may license an applicant who holds a current license in good standing in another state if that state imposes at least substantially the same standards as North Dakota.
endorsement.quote: The board may grant licensure to an applicant who holds a current license in good standing to practice as an audiologist, speech-language pathologist, or speech-language pathology licensed assistant in another state or jurisdiction

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may grant a temporary license, for a maximum of six months, to an applicant who holds a current license in good standing in another state or has held one within the past five years.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Temporary licensure may be granted for a maximum of six months, at which time documentation necessary for full licensure is required or licensure is suspended.

renewal.value: Licenses renew annually and expire each year on December 31st; the annual renewal fee is $75.00, and renewals received after December 31st are subject to a late fee.
renewal.quote: The North Dakota State Board of Examiners on Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology License expires each year on December 31st.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least ten (10) clock hours of approved continuing education each year; courses must be preapproved by the board unless they are approved by ASHA, AAA or IHS.
continuing_education.quote: Proof of attendance for at least ten (10) clock hours of approved continuing education for the year.

processing_time.value: The board states that review of applications is usually completed within 7-10 business days; incomplete applications take longer.
processing_time.quote: they do their best to review applications as quickly as possible and is usually within 7-10 business days.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply through the board's online application, linked from the New Application Instructions page.
apply_url.quote: Contact your educational institution and request OFFICIAL graduate and undergraduate transcripts to be mailed (or emailed) directly to the board office.

board.value: Ohio Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, and Athletic Trainers Board
board.quote: The mission of the Ohio Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, and Athletic Trainers Board is to actively promote and protect the health of Ohioans

education.value: Applicants must provide proof of graduation from a professional physical therapy program accredited by a national physical therapy accreditation agency approved by the board's physical therapy section.
education.quote: Proof of graduation from a professional physical therapy program that is accredited by a national physical therapy accreditation agency approved by the physical therapy section.

national_exam.value: Applicants licensed by examination must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) for physical therapists, administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy, plus the board-approved Ohio laws and rules examination.
national_exam.quote: The national physical therapy examination (NPTE) for physical therapists administered by the federation of state boards of physical therapy

state_exam.value: All applicants for initial PT licensure must pass the Ohio Jurisprudence Assessment Module (OH JAM), an online 50-question, 90-minute module costing $48; takers must answer 80% of the questions correctly to pass.
state_exam.quote: All individuals applying for initial PT or PTA licensure in Ohio must take and achieve a passing score on the OH JAM as a licensure requirement.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit fingerprints for criminal records checks by the Ohio BCI and the FBI under Ohio Revised Code 4755.70; applicants in Ohio or within 75 miles use WebCheck, and the BCI fee is $22 and the FBI fee $25.25, plus any vendor fee.
background_check.quote: In addition to the $22 BCI fee and the $25.25 FBI fee, the electronic fingerprinting company or law enforcement agency may charge its own fee to process the fingerprints.

application_fee.value: The non-refundable application fee is $100.00, paid by card with the online application.
application_fee.quote: Non-refundable application fee of $100.00. Pay fee with online application. Acceptable forms of payment are: Master Card, Visa, or Discover.

endorsement.value: The physical therapy section may issue a license by endorsement to a PT currently licensed in another state whose requirements are substantially similar to Ohio's under Ohio Revised Code 4796.03; applicants out of practice for five or more years must retake the NPTE or complete an approved action plan.
endorsement.quote: The physical therapy section may issue a license by endorsement to an applicant who is currently licensed as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant under the laws of another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: Military members or spouses of military members who hold a license in another state may apply for a seven-year temporary license.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: If you or your spouse is a member of the military, and you have a license in another state, you may apply for a seven-year temporary license.

renewal.value: PT licenses expire January 31 of even-numbered years; renewal opens November 1 before expiration, costs $70 plus a $3.50 eLicense Ohio fee, and late renewal is not allowed.
renewal.quote: Physical Therapist licenses expire on January 31 of even numbered years (January 31, 2026).

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least twenty-four units (clock hours) of continuing education each two-year renewal cycle, including at least two hours of ethics through a renewal jurisprudence module; no continuing education is required for the first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: A physical therapist shall complete a minimum of twenty-four units of continuing education activities within the two year renewal cycle.

compact.value: Ohio participates in the PT Compact under Ohio Revised Code 4755.57; applicants seeking an Ohio compact privilege must pass the Ohio Jurisprudence Assessment Module (JAM) before practicing in Ohio and again before each privilege renewal after the first.
compact.quote: all physical therapy compact privilege applicants seeking to obtain a compact privilege in Ohio are also required to successfully pass the Ohio jurisprudence assessment module (JAM)

processing_time.value: The board states that applications are reviewed within five business days of submission, after which the applicant is emailed whether the application is approved or more documentation is needed.
processing_time.quote: You will receive an email letting you know if your application is approved or if additional documentation is needed.

apply_url.value: Applicants register and apply online through the eLicense Ohio system, linked from the board's PT licensing page.
apply_url.quote: Information about how to apply for licensure in Ohio as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant.

board.value: Ohio Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, and Athletic Trainers Board
board.quote: The mission of the Ohio Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, and Athletic Trainers Board is to actively promote and protect the health of Ohioans

education.value: Applicants must have completed an occupational therapy program accredited by ACOTE, or show completion of a substantially equivalent educational program.
education.quote: Have completed an occupational therapy program accredited by the accreditation council for occupational therapy education (ACOTE) of the American occupational therapy association (AOTA)

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the certification examination of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) for occupational therapists.
national_exam.quote: An applicant has satisfied the examination requirements of the occupational therapy section if they passed the certification examination of the national board for certification in occupational therapy

state_exam.value: Applicants must take the Ohio OT Jurisprudence Exam for Licensure Applicants online through myicourse, score at least 90%, and have the transcript sent to the board.
state_exam.quote: select the Ohio OT Jurisprudence Exam for Licensure Applicants and request that a transcript be sent. The minimum passing score is 90% or better.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a BCI/FBI criminal records check; if the license is not issued within 6 months of the board receiving the results, new checks are required.
background_check.quote: Please note that if your license is not issued within 6 months of the date the Board receives the criminal records check results, you will be required to submit new criminal records checks.

application_fee.value: The non-refundable application fee is $100.00, paid by card with the online application.
application_fee.quote: Non-refundable application fee of $100.00. Pay fee with online application. Acceptable forms of payment are: Master Card, Visa, or Discover.

endorsement.value: Endorsement applicants must meet the education and NBCOT examination requirements and hold a current, valid OT license in another state or U.S. territory or current, valid NBCOT certification; those out of practice more than five years may face additional requirements.
endorsement.quote: Hold a current, valid license to practice as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another state or United States territory or possess current, valid certification from NBCOT.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Military members or spouses of military members who hold a license in another state may apply for a seven-year temporary license.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: If you or your spouse is a member of the military, and you have a license in another state, you may apply for a seven-year temporary license.

required_courses.value: Applications for initial OT licensure must include viewing a required presentation about the board's safe haven program.
required_courses.quote: Accompanied by such evidence, statements, or documents as specified on the application including viewing a required presentation about the board's safe haven program.

renewal.value: OT licenses expire June 30 of odd-numbered years; renewal opens April 1 before expiration, costs $70 plus a $3.50 eLicense Ohio fee, and late renewal is not allowed.
renewal.quote: Occupational Therapist licenses expire on June 30 of odd numbered years (June 30, 2025).

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete twenty contact hours of continuing education each two-year renewal cycle, including at least one contact hour of ethics, jurisprudence, or cultural competence and one contact hour of mental health and/or substance use; no continuing education is required for the first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: the license holder has completed twenty contact hours of continuing education activities within the two year renewal cycle.

compact.value: Ohio participates in the OT Compact under Ohio Revised Code 4755.14; applicants seeking an Ohio compact privilege must pass the Ohio occupational therapy jurisprudence examination before practicing in Ohio and again before each privilege renewal after the first.
compact.quote: all occupational therapy compact privilege applicants seeking to obtain a compact privilege in Ohio are also required to successfully pass the Ohio occupational therapy jurisprudence examination

processing_time.value: The board states that applications are reviewed within five business days of submission, after which the applicant is emailed whether the application is approved or more documentation is needed.
processing_time.quote: You will receive an email letting you know if your application is approved or if additional documentation is needed.

apply_url.value: Applicants register and apply online through the eLicense Ohio system, linked from the board's OT licensing page.
apply_url.quote: How to apply for an Ohio OT or OTA license. Applicants must first register in the eLicense system at

board.value: Ohio Speech and Hearing Professionals Board
board.quote: Welcome to the Ohio Speech and Hearing Professionals Board

education.value: Applicants must submit an official transcript showing at least a master's degree in speech-language pathology or the equivalent, with coursework from colleges or universities accredited by organizations the board recognizes.
education.quote: an official transcript demonstrating that the person has at least a master's degree in speech-language pathology or the equivalent as determined by the board.

national_exam.value: Applicants must score one hundred sixty-two or above on the Praxis Speech-Language Pathology (5331) test administered by the Educational Testing Service.
national_exam.quote: Received an examination score of one hundred sixty-two or above on the "Praxis Speech-Language Pathology: 5331" test

background_check.value: Under Ohio Revised Code 4753.061, all initial license applicants must submit fingerprints for criminal records checks by the Ohio BCI and the FBI.
background_check.quote: requires all individuals applying for an initial license issued by the Ohio Speech and Hearing Professionals Board to submit fingerprints for a criminal records check

application_fee.value: The application fee is $200.00 for a speech-language pathology license and $210.00 for a conditional speech-language pathology license, plus a $3.50 eLicense maintenance fee.
application_fee.quote: Application $200.00 Audiology $200.00 Speech-Language Pathology $210.00 Conditional Speech-Language Pathology

endorsement.value: The board waives the examination, educational, and professional experience requirements for applicants who show a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence in speech-language pathology in good standing.
endorsement.quote: Presents proof to the state speech and hearing professionals board of a current certificate of clinical competence in speech-language pathology or audiology that is in good standing

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants completing the required supervised professional experience must hold a conditional license, which allows practice under the supervision of a fully licensed person and is valid for eighteen months.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A conditional license is valid for eighteen months unless suspended or revoked

renewal.value: Licenses renew online through eLicense every 2 years, between 10/2 and 12/31 of each even-numbered year; the renewal fee is $120, with an added $120 late fee if not renewed by 12/31.
renewal.quote: Renew OSHPA license online through eLicense every 2 years between 10/2 to 12/31 of each even year

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn twenty continuing education hours in each two-year licensure period, including at least two hours related to ethics and ten hours specific to the clinical practice of speech-language pathology; no CE is required for the first renewal.
continuing_education.quote: A licensee shall earn twenty continuing education hours within the two-year licensure period immediately preceding the licensee's renewal application.

compact.value: Ohio is an operational ASLP-IC member; since February 9, 2026, Ohio-licensed practitioners can register and begin the privilege-to-practice process.
compact.quote: Licensed practitioners in Ohio can register and begin the privilege to practice process.

apply_url.value: Applicants create an account and apply for a license through eLicense Ohio, linked from the board's Getting Licensed page.
apply_url.quote: To apply for an individual or business license, open eLicense.Ohio.gov and follow the instructions.

board.value: Oklahoma State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision
board.quote: The Physical Therapy Committee assists the State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision in conducting examinations for applicants

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from a physical therapy school accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE) or an approved successor organization.
education.quote: A qualified physical therapist must have graduated from a school of physical therapy accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education or approved successor organization.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the nationally accepted standardized physical therapy examination, with the passing point set at a scaled score of 600 on a scale of 200 to 800.
national_exam.quote: This passing point will be set equal to a scaled score of 600 based on a scale ranging from 200 to 800.

background_check.value: The Board may require physical therapist applicants, as a condition of initial licensure, to submit a full set of fingerprints, and it is authorized to obtain state and national criminal history record information.
background_check.quote: as a condition for eligibility for initial licensure, to submit a full set of fingerprints in a form and manner prescribed by the Board.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists currently licensed by examination in another U.S. state, the District of Columbia or Puerto Rico are eligible for licensure by endorsement if their exam and grade standard are acceptable to the Board; national exam scores must be submitted through the Interstate Reporting Service and meet the Oklahoma passing score.
endorsement.quote: Any person who is currently registered or licensed by examination as a Physical Therapist or Physical Therapy Assistant in another state of the United States of America

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board may issue a temporary permit to a first-time applicant who has applied for a license and is eligible to take the examination; the permit expires upon notice that the applicant has or has not passed the examination.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: the Board may issue a temporary permit to a person who has applied for a license pursuant to the provisions of Section 887.7 of this title

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses expire on January 31 of each year and may be renewed during January upon application, evidence of completed continuing education, and payment of fees.
renewal.quote: all licenses shall expire on January 31 of each year. A license may be renewed during the month of January of each year upon:

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 40 hours of approved continuing education every two years, with the cycle ending January 31 of every even year; at least half must be professional development coursework and three hours must be ethics education covering the APTA Guide for Professional Conduct and APTA Code of Ethics.
continuing_education.quote: If you are a Physical Therapist you must obtain forty (40) hours of approved continuing education every two (2) years

compact.value: Oklahoma is a Physical Therapy Compact state; physical therapists and PTAs whose home state is also a member may apply through the compact for privileges to practice in Oklahoma.
compact.quote: Oklahoma recently became a PT Compact state. If your home state is also a member, you may quickly and easily apply through the compact for privileges to practice in Oklahoma as a PT or PTA.

board.value: Oklahoma State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision
board.quote: We are grateful to the Oklahoma Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision for the support of this site.

education.value: Occupational therapist applicants must complete an educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) and at least six months of supervised fieldwork experience.
education.quote: For an occupational therapist the educational program shall be accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE).

national_exam.value: The Board recognizes the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) examination for licensure, and applicants must have passing scores submitted through a Board-approved reporting service.
national_exam.quote: recognizes and approves the Examination of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) as an examination acceptable for licensure of an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant.

background_check.value: The Board's occupational therapist forms list includes an Extended Background Check (EBC) consent to perform a criminal history background check.
background_check.quote: Extended Background Check (EBC) Consent to Perform Criminal History Background Check in Compliance with the FCRA (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists currently licensed by examination in another U.S. state, the District of Columbia or Puerto Rico are eligible for licensure by endorsement if their exam was the NBCOT exam or another Board-approved exam, with proof of passing required.
endorsement.quote: Any person who is currently licensed by examination as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another state of the United States of America

temporary_or_provisional.value: The Board may issue a temporary license for no more than 90 days to an endorsement applicant once it receives the application and a completed Verification of Supervision form; new graduates who meet the academic and clinical requirements may practice under direct on-site supervision in graduate status for up to one year.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The Board may issue a temporary license to any applicant for licensure by endorsement for no more than ninety (90) days upon the Board's receipt of an application

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses must be renewed yearly on October 31, with fees set by the Board and late fees for late renewal.
renewal.quote: license is required to be renewed yearly on October 31 upon forms provided by the Board and shall be accompanied by fees set by the Board.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 20 hours of approved continuing education every two years, with the cycle ending October 31 of every even year; no hours may be carried over.
continuing_education.quote: You must obtain twenty (20) hours of approved continuing education every two (2) years

compact.value: Oklahoma enacted the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact through Senate Bill 1653, effective November 1, 2026.
