compact.quote: The Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact is hereby enacted into law and the Governor shall enter into the Compact on behalf of the State of Oklahoma

board.value: Oklahoma Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: Oklahoma Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology (632)

education.value: Speech-language pathology applicants must hold at least a master's degree or equivalent with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology from an accredited institution, and must complete at least 36 weeks of full-time paid clinical fellowship (waived for holders of the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence).
education.quote: Each speech-language pathology applicant shall hold not less than a master's degree, or its equivalent, with a major emphasis in speech-language pathology from an accredited academic institution

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the ETS Praxis II Speech-Language Pathology exam (or another Board-recognized national exam) within two years after Board approval of their first clinical fellow application; the exam is waived for ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence holders.
national_exam.quote: The Board designates as its approved examinations the most current versions of the Educational Testing Service (ETS) Praxis II Audiology Exam and the Praxis II Speech-Language Pathology Exam

background_check.value: A national criminal background check is completed on each applicant.
background_check.quote: A national criminal background check will be completed on each applicant.

application_fee.value: The application fee is $85, which is forfeited if the applicant is not found eligible for licensure.
application_fee.quote: The application must be accompanied by eighty-five dollars ($85.00) in the form of an electronic payment, check, cashier's check or money order.

endorsement.value: The Board may license without examination a person holding a current speech-language pathology license in another state or country whose qualifications and exams meet or exceed Oklahoma's, upon payment of the licensure fee and proof of licensure in good standing.
endorsement.quote: The Board may issue a license without examination to a person who holds a current license in another state or country

temporary_or_provisional.value: Persons completing the supervised clinical fellowship must hold a clinical fellow license and practice under a licensed speech-language pathologist's supervision; the clinical fellow license is valid for one calendar year from Board approval and may be extended once for one year on written request.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: must obtain a clinical fellow license and practice under the supervision of a licensed speech-language pathologist until the Board issues the clinical fellow a speech-language pathologist license.

renewal.value: Licenses are renewed each calendar year; the $85 renewal fee is due on or before December 31, and renewals postmarked after December 31 incur increasing late penalties.
renewal.quote: The license renewal fee shall be eighty-five dollars ($85.00) each calendar year. The renewal fee is due on or before December 31st of each year.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete at least 20 clock hours of acceptable continuing education every two years, including at least three clock hours of professional ethics; the period begins in January of every odd-numbered year.
continuing_education.quote: A minimum of twenty (20) clock hours of acceptable continuing education will be required for renewal of a license to practice Audiology, Speech-Language Pathology, or Speech-Language Pathology Assistants in a two year period.

compact.value: Oklahoma is a member of the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact (ASLP-IC); practitioners seeking privileges to practice in Oklahoma must apply through ASLP-IC and pay the compact fee plus the $85 Oklahoma application fee.
compact.quote: The state of Oklahoma is a current member of the ASLP-IC.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online through the OBESPA Online Licensing system linked from the board's New Applicants page.
apply_url.quote: Begin by clicking on the OBESPA Online Licensing button below and follow the instructions to set up a login account:

board.value: Oregon Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: Oregon Board of Physical Therapy You are here: Oregon Board of Physical Therapy Welcome Page

education.value: Applicants must graduate from a CAPTE-accredited physical therapy education program, and official transcripts showing the date the degree was awarded must be sent to the Board by the school.
education.quote: Official transcripts must be sent from your school. Transcripts must show the date that the degree was awarded.

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT), and have their score sent to Oregon.
national_exam.quote: The Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) is the administrator of the NPTE, and determines if you are eligible to take the exam

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Oregon Jurisprudence Assessment Module (OR-JAM), a timed 90-minute exam of 50 multiple-choice questions on Oregon physical therapy statutes and rules, taken within the 6 months before application approval.
state_exam.quote: The OR-JAM is a timed 90-minute exam of 50 multiple-choice questions covering Oregon Statutes and Administrative Rules related to physical therapy.

background_check.value: Applicants must answer background questions on the application and complete a fingerprint-based criminal history check through Fieldprint, with results processed by the Oregon State Police.
background_check.quote: There are two components to the background check: the applicant must respond to several questions on the application and they must submit to a fingerprint-based criminal history check.

temporary_or_provisional.value: New CAPTE-program graduates who have not yet taken the NPTE may receive an Exam Temporary Permit to work under on-site supervision of a licensee for up to 90 days, at an additional $50 charge.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Temporary permits allow the applicant to work for up to 90 days after the permit is issued. The applicant MUST take the NPTE within these 90 days.

required_courses.value: All applicants must complete the free 1-hour Oregon Pain Management Commission pain management module and upload the completion certificate before submitting the application.
required_courses.quote: all applicants must complete this free 1 hour course before submitting their application.

renewal.value: Licenses are valid for up to two years and expire on March 31st of even-numbered years; the physical therapist renewal fee is $200.
renewal.quote: Licenses are valid for up to two years, and expire on March 31st of even years.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete 24 hours of continuing competency per certification period (fewer for recently licensed people), including the Oregon Pain Management Commission module and a cultural competency course of at least one hour every renewal.
continuing_education.quote: Licensees MUST take a course in cultural competency every renewal period. Licensees may choose from a variety of courses. The course must be a minimum of one hour.

compact.value: Oregon is a member of the Physical Therapy Compact and accepts compact privileges; therapists licensed in another member state can buy an Oregon privilege after passing the OR-JAM.
compact.quote: If you currently hold a license in a PT Compact Member State, your license allows you to purchase Compact Privileges in 26 other states, including Oregon!

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted online through the Board's Applicant Portal, linked from the Applying for Licensure page.
apply_url.quote: Applications are submitted online through the Applicant Portal.

board.value: Oregon Occupational Therapy Licensing Board
board.quote: Mission: To protect the public by supervising occupational therapy practice; and to ensure safe and ethical delivery of occupational therapy services.

state_exam.value: All applicants must pass the Oregon Law/Ethics exam, an open-book online exam, before receiving a license.
state_exam.quote: All applicants must take and pass the Oregon Ethics/Law exam before they can receive their new license.

background_check.value: All applicants must pass a fingerprint background check before licensure, with prints taken at a Fieldprint office; the $50 background check cost is added to the licensure fee.
background_check.quote: the OT Licensing Board requires that all applicants pass a background check prior to licensure in Oregon.

application_fee.value: Starting March 1, 2026, the OT application fee is $330 ($280 plus a $50 fingerprint background check fee) for a two-year license; application fees are non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: Starting March 1, 2026, the current two-year fee is $330 ($280+$50 fingerprint background check fee), for a license active through May 31, 2028

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists coming from another state apply through the same application; they do not need to send school transcripts or NBCOT verification, but must have official verifications sent from every state where they were licensed and worked.
endorsement.quote: You are not required to order your NBCOT verification to be sent to us. We are able to look up your certification directly on the NBCOT website.

temporary_or_provisional.value: A one-time limited permit is available to applicants waiting to take the NBCOT exam; it costs $25, is valid for 90 days, and requires supervision by an Oregon-licensed OT.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Limited Permits are available only once for those who are applying to take the NBCOT examination. The Limited permit costs $25 and is valid for 90 days.

required_courses.value: Applicants must complete the free Oregon Health Authority Pain Commission 1-hour pain management course as a condition of licensure and upload the completion certificate.
required_courses.quote: Applicants are required to complete the FREE Oregon OHA Pain Commission 1 hour Pain Management Course as a condition of licensure.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must earn at least 30 points of CE in the two years before renewal (current NBCOT certification satisfies this), plus 1 hour of cultural competency and the OHA pain management module every renewal.
continuing_education.quote: All current licensees shall obtain a minimum of 30 points of CE from Board approved categories during the two years immediately preceding the date of the license renewal;

compact.value: Oregon is not part of the OT Licensure Compact, so an Oregon license is required; the 2025 bill (HB 2357) to enact the compact did not pass.
compact.quote: The Oregon OT Licensing Board is not part of the OT Licensure Compact. You must have an Oregon License to practice occupational therapy in Oregon.

processing_time.value: The Board states it issues the license within 3 days once all documentation is received.
processing_time.quote: How long does it take? Once we receive all documentation, we license within 3 days.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through the Board's online Applicant Portal, linked from the OT & OTA Applications page.
apply_url.quote: To apply as an OT, click on the APPLICANT PORTAL link:

board.value: Oregon Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology & Audiology
board.quote: It is declared to be a policy of this state that it is necessary to provide regulatory authority over persons offering speech-language pathology and audiology services to the public

background_check.value: A fingerprint background check must be completed with every application, with prints taken through Fieldprint, Inc.
background_check.quote: A background check must be completed with every application by our agency. The prints must be taken through Fieldprint, Inc.

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed elsewhere use the standard application and must have a letter of good standing sent directly from every jurisdiction where they have held a professional license; ASHA CCC verification may be submitted instead of a Praxis score report.
endorsement.quote: We need to have a letter of good standing from every other state or other jurisdiction

temporary_or_provisional.value: A conditional SLP license lets a clinical fellow practice for a limited time while completing clinical fellowship year requirements; applicants need an official master's transcript and a background check.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Only valid for limited time to complete clinical fellowship year requirements for full licensure.

continuing_education.value: SLPs must complete 20 hours of professional development per renewal period, including 1 hour in cultural competency.
continuing_education.quote: SLP/Audiologist: 20 hours with 1 hour in cultural competency.

compact.value: Oregon has not enacted the ASLP-IC: HB 2357 (2025 Regular Session), which would have enacted the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, is listed as still in House committee.
compact.quote: Enacts the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact. Permits the State Board of Examiners of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology to disclose specified information to the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Compact Commission.

apply_url.value: Applications are submitted through the Board's online Applicant Portal, linked from the Applications page.
apply_url.quote: All other applications are submitted through the Applicant Portal, click here to begin the application process.

board.value: Pennsylvania State Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: The Pennsylvania State Board of Physical Therapy is responsible for regulating the practice of physical therapy through licensure, registration, certification and discipline

education.value: Applicants for licensure by examination must have graduated from a physical therapy program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education or another Board-recognized national accreditor; the Board lists the degree requirement as a Doctor of Physical Therapy.
education.quote: An applicant for licensure by examination shall have graduated from a physical therapy program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE).
national_exam.quote: Applicant must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE)

application_fee.value: The initial licensing fee for a physical therapist license is $30.00.
application_fee.quote: Initial Licensing Fee: $30.00 Licensure Renewal Fee: $90.00 Biennial renewal of license.

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed or registered in another U.S. state, territory or the District of Columbia may apply for licensure by endorsement if that jurisdiction's requirements were substantially equal to Pennsylvania's at the time of licensure; they must also complete at least 3 hours of approved child abuse recognition and reporting training.
endorsement.quote: evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant is licensed or otherwise registered as a physical therapist in another state or territory of the United States

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who have applied for or are awaiting results of the licensure examination may receive a temporary license to work only under direct on-premises supervision of a licensed physical therapist with at least 2 years of experience. The temporary license must be surrendered upon failure of the first examination or 6 months after issuance, whichever occurs first.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: must be surrendered to the Board immediately upon the failure of the first examination or 6 months after the date of issuance, whichever occurs first.

required_courses.value: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.
required_courses.quote: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses renew biennially and expire December 31 of every even-numbered year; the Board emails renewal notices approximately 60 days before expiration.
renewal.quote: Licenses expire December 31 of every even-numbered year

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete at least 30 contact hours of continuing education each biennial renewal period, including at least 2 contact hours in law or ethics and at least 2 contact hours in child abuse recognition and reporting. Continuing education is not required during the renewal cycle in which the licensee was first licensed.
continuing_education.quote: a licensee shall complete qualifying continuing education equal to at least 30 contact hours of continuing physical therapy education, including at least 2 contact hours in law or ethics applicable to the practice of physical therapy

compact.value: Pennsylvania fully implemented the PT Compact on July 7, 2025; Pennsylvania physical therapists can apply for compact privileges in other member states, and out-of-state physical therapists can request compact privileges to work in Pennsylvania.
compact.quote: Pennsylvania fully implemented the PT Compact on July 7, 2025, and Pennsylvania physical therapists and physical therapist assistants can now apply for a compact privilege

apply_url.value: All applications must be submitted electronically through PALS, the Pennsylvania licensing system.
apply_url.quote: All applications must be submitted electronically and can be found at www.pals.pa.gov

board.value: State Board of Occupational Therapy Education and Licensure
board.quote: The State Board of Occupational Therapy Education and Licensure regulates and licenses persons providing occupational therapy services to the general public in Pennsylvania.

education.value: Applicants must have met the academic requirements of an occupational therapy program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE), or one approved by the Board and nationally accredited, and must complete 6 months of supervised fieldwork experience.
education.quote: Applicant has met the academic requirements of an educational program in occupational therapy accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE)

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Occupational Therapist Registered (OTR) licensure examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), or qualify for a waiver of that examination.
national_exam.quote: Applicant has passed the Occupational Therapist Registered (OTR) licensure examination or has qualified for a waiver of the licensure examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT).

application_fee.value: The initial licensing fee for an occupational therapist license is $30.00.
application_fee.quote: Initial Licensing Fee: $30.00 Licensure Renewal Fee: $55.00 Biennial renewal of license.

endorsement.value: Applicants with a current license in good standing from a jurisdiction with substantially equivalent standards may be licensed by endorsement if they have actively practiced for at least 2 of the 5 years immediately preceding the application, have not been disciplined, and have completed 3 hours of child abuse recognition and reporting training.
endorsement.quote: has actively engaged in the licensed practice as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant under a license, certificate, registration or permit in a substantially equivalent jurisdiction or jurisdictions, for at least 2 of the 5 years immediately preceding

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants who meet licensure requirements and have applied to take the licensure examination may receive a temporary license that authorizes practice only as an assistant under the direct supervision of a licensed occupational therapist. Nonresidents licensed in a substantially equal jurisdiction or NBCOT-certified may also receive a temporary license to perform services for no longer than 6 consecutive months in a calendar year.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: authorizes the practice of occupational therapy only as an assistant under the direct supervision of an occupational therapist licensed under the act and this chapter.

required_courses.value: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.
required_courses.quote: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses expire June 30 of every odd-numbered year and are renewed through an online-only process; the Board emails renewal notices 70 to 60 days before expiration.
renewal.quote: Licenses expire June 30 of every odd-numbered year

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete at least 24 contact hours of continued competency activities each biennial period, including at least 2 hours in child abuse recognition and reporting. Apart from the 2 child abuse hours, licensees are exempt for the first biennial renewal period after initial licensure.
continuing_education.quote: an occupational therapist shall complete a minimum of 24 contact hours in each biennial period in acceptable continued competency activities

compact.value: Pennsylvania enacted legislation to join the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact: House Bill 482 became Act No. 28 of 2026, approved by the Governor on July 20, 2026.
compact.quote: Last Action: Act No. 28 of 2026, July 20, 2026

apply_url.value: Applications for Pennsylvania professional licenses are submitted and renewed online in the Pennsylvania Licensing System (PALS).
apply_url.quote: If your job requires a professional or occupational license to work in Pennsylvania, you can apply for or renew it in our Pennsylvania Licensing System (PALS).

board.value: State Board of Examiners in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The State Board of Examiners in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology regulates the practice and licensure of persons offering speech-language and hearing services in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's degree or higher in speech-language pathology from an accredited academic program, and must complete supervised professional experience of no less than 1,260 hours over no less than 9 months but no more than 2 years.
education.quote: Applicants for a license as a Speech-Language Pathologist must possess a master's degree or higher in speech-language pathology from an academic program accredited by an accrediting agency

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis examination in speech-language pathology.
national_exam.quote: Applicants for licensure must pass the Praxis examination in speech-language pathology as a requirement for licensure.

application_fee.value: The initial licensing fee for a speech-language pathologist license is $50.00.
application_fee.quote: Initial Licensing Fee: $50.00 Licensure Renewal Fee: $65.00 Biennial renewal of license.

endorsement.value: Applicants licensed in good standing in a jurisdiction with substantially equivalent standards may be licensed by endorsement if they show competency through practice for at least 2 of the 5 years before applying or 20 hours of continuing education in the preceding 24 months, have not been disciplined, and complete 3 hours of child abuse recognition and reporting training.
endorsement.quote: in a jurisdiction or jurisdictions that have substantially equivalent licensure standards for at least 2 of the 5 years immediately preceding the filing of the application with the Board.

temporary_or_provisional.value: Applicants completing the supervised professional experience needed for the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence may receive a provisional license valid for 18 months, renewable one time, and must practice under a supervisor. Applicants who have completed all licensure requirements may receive a 6-month provisional license, and out-of-state licensees applying in Pennsylvania may receive one valid for 90 days.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Applicants who are completing the supervised professional experience necessary to receive an ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence. A provisional license granted under this subparagraph will be valid for 18 months and may be renewed one time

required_courses.value: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.
required_courses.quote: Applicants must complete 3 hours of Board-approved continuing education in child abuse recognition and reporting for initial licensure.

renewal.value: Speech-language pathologist licenses expire July 31 of every even-numbered year, and the renewal fee is $65.00; the Board emails renewal notices approximately 60 days before expiration.
renewal.quote: Licenses expire July 31 of every even-numbered year

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete 20 clock hours of continuing education per license each biennial period, including at least 2 hours in child abuse recognition and reporting; excess hours may not be carried over.
continuing_education.quote: Each speech-language pathologist or audiologist shall have completed 20 clock hours of continuing education per license during each preceding biennial period, including at least 2 hours of approved courses in child abuse recognition and reporting

compact.value: House Bill 80, which would authorize Pennsylvania to join the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, had not become law; its last action was a re-referral to Appropriations on March 16, 2026.
compact.quote: An Act authorizing the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to join the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact; and providing for the form of the compact.

apply_url.value: Applications for Pennsylvania professional licenses are submitted and renewed online in the Pennsylvania Licensing System (PALS).
apply_url.quote: If your job requires a professional or occupational license to work in Pennsylvania, you can apply for or renew it in our Pennsylvania Licensing System (PALS).

board.value: Rhode Island Board of Physical Therapy (within the Rhode Island Department of Health)
board.quote: "Board" means the Board of Physical Therapy within the Department established pursuant to the provisions of R.I. Gen. Laws

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from a physical therapy education program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE) or another accrediting agency approved by the department.
education.quote: Has graduated from an education program in physical therapy accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE)

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) of the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT), or another approved physical therapy certification examination.
national_exam.quote: Has passed the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE) of the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT)

background_check.value: Applicants must submit a full Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) check from the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office. Out-of-state (endorsement) applicants must obtain their full BCI report from their state of residence.
background_check.quote: Full Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) check from the Rhode Island Attorney General’s Office.

application_fee.value: The physical therapist application fee is $155.00, nonrefundable, payable by check or money order to the RI General Treasurer; it covers the first license up to the next expiration date.
application_fee.quote: made payable (in U.S. funds only) to the RI General Treasurer in the amount of ($155.00-Physical Therapist) OR ($50.00 Physical Therapy Assistant)

endorsement.value: A physical therapist licensed by examination in another state, territory or the District of Columbia may be licensed in Rhode Island without examination by endorsement if the board finds the applicant meets Rhode Island's qualifications.
endorsement.quote: A license to practice physical therapy may be issued without examination to an applicant who has been licensed by examination as a physical therapist under the laws of another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: New graduates may apply for a graduate license (permit) within 30 days of graduation; it is valid for 90 days, cannot be renewed, and is revoked if the applicant fails the exam. Foreign-educated graduates are not eligible.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The application must be submitted within 30 days of graduation. These permits are valid for 90 days and may not be renewed.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses expire on the first day of May of the next even year (a biennial cycle), and the renewal application and fee must be filed on or before the thirty-first day of March of each even year.
renewal.quote: shall expire on the first day of May of the next even year following the date of original licensure

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must attest to completing 24 hours of continuing education every two years in scope of practice-specific offerings; clinical supervision of students in APTA-approved programs counts for at most 3 hours per cycle.
continuing_education.quote: physical therapists shall attest to completion of twenty-four (24) hours biennially in scope of practice-specific offerings

compact.value: Rhode Island has passed PT Compact legislation, but the compact is not currently operational in the state, so compact privileges are not yet available.
compact.quote: While this legislation has passed in RI, the compact is not currently operational.

apply_url.value: Applicants use the paper Instructions and Application for License as a Physical Therapist from the Rhode Island Department of Health; applications are valid for 1 year from the day RIDOH receives them.
apply_url.quote: Applications are valid for 1 year from the day they are received at RIDOH. If you are not licensed within the year you must submit a new application.

board.value: Rhode Island Board of Occupational Therapy Practice (within the Rhode Island Department of Health)
board.quote: There is created within the division of professional regulation in the department of health a board of occupational therapy practice.

education.value: Applicants must complete an occupational therapy education program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (or another board-approved accreditor), including at least 24 weeks of supervised fieldwork for occupational therapists.
education.quote: Have successfully completed the academic requirements of an education program in occupational therapy accredited by the American Occupational Therapy Association’s Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Certification Examination for Occupational Therapists, Registered, of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), or another board-approved certification exam.
national_exam.quote: Have successfully passed the National Certification Examination for Occupational Therapists, Registered, or National Certification Examination for Occupational Therapy Assistants, of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT)

application_fee.value: The occupational therapist application fee is $140.00, nonrefundable, payable by check or money order to the RI General Treasurer; it covers the first license up to the next expiration date.
application_fee.quote: made payable (in U.S. funds only) to the RI General Treasurer in the amount of $140.00 and attached to the upper left-hand corner of the first (Top) page of the application.

endorsement.value: Occupational therapists licensed or regulated in another state, territory or the District of Columbia apply by endorsement and must have the board of each state where they hold or have held licensure send a statement of their licensure status. On receiving a receipt from the division they may practice under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist until the board reviews the application.
endorsement.quote: A statement from the board of occupational therapy in each state in which the applicant has held or holds licensure, or is otherwise subject to state regulation

temporary_or_provisional.value: New graduates may apply for a graduate license (permit) that is valid for 90 days, cannot be renewed, and is revoked if the applicant fails the certification exam. Foreign-educated graduates are not eligible.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: If you are a new graduate you can apply for a graduate license. These permits are valid for 90 days and may not be renewed.

renewal.value: Occupational therapy licenses are renewed biennially and expire on March 31 of each even year; the renewal application, continuing education evidence and fee are due on or before March 31 of each even year.
renewal.quote: The license, unless sooner suspended or revoked, shall expire on the thirty-first (31st) day of March, of each even year (biennially).

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must show proof of 20 hours of continuing education every two years, through activities such as presentations, clinical instruction, publications, research, inservice programs, AOTA-approved courses, university courses or self-study.
continuing_education.quote: must show proof of participation in twenty (20) hours biennially in presentations, clinical instruction, publications, research, inservice programs

compact.value: Rhode Island has passed OT Compact legislation, but the compact is not currently operational in the state, so compact privileges are not yet available.
compact.quote: While this legislation has passed in RI, the compact is not currently operational.

apply_url.value: Applicants use the paper Instructions and Application for License as an Occupational Therapist from the Rhode Island Department of Health; applications are valid for 1 year from the day RIDOH receives them.
apply_url.quote: Applications are valid for 1 year from the day they are received at RIDOH. If you are not licensed within the year you must submit a new application.

board.value: Rhode Island State Board of Examiners for Speech Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: "Board" means the "State Board of Examiners for Speech Pathology and Audiology."

education.value: Applicants need a master's or doctoral degree (or equivalent) in speech-language pathology from an institution accredited by ASHA's Council on Academic Accreditation (CAA) or another board-approved association, plus supervised clinical practicum experience.
education.quote: indicating possession of a master’s degree or a doctorate degree or equivalent in speech-language pathology from an educational institution accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation (CAA)

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass a national examination in speech-language pathology as required by ASHA (or another board-approved association) and present verification of a certificate of clinical competence.
national_exam.quote: Pass a national examination in speech-language pathology as required by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA)

endorsement.value: Applicants who have held or hold a license in another state must present evidence from the speech-language pathology board of each such state attesting to their licensure status, in addition to meeting the standard requirements including ASHA certification.
endorsement.quote: present evidence from the board of speech-language pathology in each state in which the applicant has held or holds licensure

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows completing the postgraduate professional experience must hold a provisional license; it is renewed annually if the experience runs past one year, may not exceed 36 months past the start of the experience, and expires 90 days after it ends.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license shall not exceed thirty-six (36) months past the initiation of the professional experience and will expire ninety (90) days after the end of the postgraduate professional experience.

renewal.value: Speech-language pathology licenses are renewed biennially in even years, with the renewal fee payable before July 1 of even years; licenses not renewed by June 30 lapse and require a late fee to reinstate.
renewal.quote: a biennial license renewal fee payable before July 1 of even years (biennially)

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 20 clock hours of continuing education in the two years before June 30 of even years (30 hours for those licensed in both speech-language pathology and audiology), from ASHA, AAA, IACET-authorized or other approved sponsors.
continuing_education.quote: shall complete not less than twenty (20) clock hours of continuing education within the preceding two (2) years and be able to present satisfactory evidence of completion to the Department

compact.value: Rhode Island has passed ASLP-IC (Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact) legislation, but the compact is not currently operational in the state, so compact privileges are not yet available.
compact.quote: While this legislation has passed in RI, the compact is not currently operational.

apply_url.value: Applicants use the Department of Health's paper Application for a License as a Speech Language Pathologist or Audiologist, which covers both examination and endorsement applicants.
apply_url.quote: Application for a License as a Speech Language Pathologist or Audiologist Refer to the Application Instructions when completing these forms.

board.value: South Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
board.quote: The SC Board of Physical Therapy Examiners regulates physical therapists and physical therapist assistants in the state of South Carolina.

education.value: Applicants must be graduates of a board-approved physical therapy educational program, or show that their education is equivalent to that of physical therapists educated in United States programs.
education.quote: be a graduate of a physical therapy educational program approved by the board or provide satisfactory evidence that your education is equivalent to the requirements of physical therapists educated in United States educational programs

national_exam.value: Applicants for initial licensure must pass the National Physical Therapy Exam (NPTE), registering and paying for it through FSBPT; a person who has failed it six or more times may not be licensed.
national_exam.quote: An applicant for initial licensure must pass the National Physical Therapy Exam

background_check.value: Since February 1, 2023, all applicants for a license with the South Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners are subject to a state and national fingerprint criminal background check.
background_check.quote: Effective February 1, 2023, all applicants applying for a license with the SC Board of Physical Therapy Examiners will be subject to a state and national fingerprint criminal background check.

application_fee.value: The initial license application fee is $110 for a physical therapist.
application_fee.quote: Initial License Application Fee Physical Therapist, $110 Physical Therapist Assistant, $110

endorsement.value: The board may license, without examination, a physical therapist licensed in another state or territory whose licensure requirements were equivalent; endorsement applicants must have exam scores reported directly to the board and undergo state and FBI fingerprint criminal records checks.
endorsement.quote: as a physical therapist or as a physical therapist assistant, without examination, on the payment of the applicable fee, an applicant who is a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant licensed under the laws of another state or territory

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may issue a provisional license, for example to an applicant who has met all requirements except the clinical practice hours or the official transcript; it is valid for up to one year, cannot be renewed, and requires supervision by a physical therapist licensed in South Carolina.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license is valid for up to one year from the date of issue and may not be renewed.

renewal.value: Physical therapist licenses are renewed every two years; the current reporting period runs January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026, and the renewal deadline is December 31, 2026.
renewal.quote: The biennial reporting period for the 2026 renewal is January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must earn 3.0 CEUs (30 hours) of continuing education per biennium, including 15 hours of certified activities, three hours of which must be in ethics or professionalism.
continuing_education.quote: shall earn 3.0 CEUs or thirty (30) hours of acceptable continuing education credit per biennium year, which must include 15 hours of certified activities, which must include three hours of ethics or professionalism

compact.value: South Carolina is an active member of the PT Compact, which lets eligible PTs and PTAs work in member states beyond their home state without applying for a license in each one; practitioners apply for a privilege to practice through the PT Compact.
compact.quote: The South Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is now an active member of the PT Compact.

apply_url.value: First-time applicants can apply through the board's electronic application system, which accepts document uploads and card or electronic check payment.
apply_url.quote: You may apply for licensure through our electronic application system. This electronic application will allow you to upload the required documentation and make payment via credit card or electronic check.

board.value: South Carolina Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: The Board of Occupational Therapy examines and issues licenses to qualified occupational therapists and occupational therapy assistants.

education.value: Applicants must have graduated from an occupational therapy program approved by ACOTE (or another AOTA-endorsed accreditor, or a substantially equivalent program) and completed at least six months of supervised fieldwork.
education.quote: have graduated from an occupational therapy educational program approved by ACOTE or other AOTA endorsed accrediting body for occupational therapy

national_exam.value: Applicants for initial licensure must pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) exam.
national_exam.quote: An applicant for initial licensure must pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

state_exam.value: Applicants must also pass the board's Jurisprudence Exam, which tests knowledge of the South Carolina Occupational Therapy Practice Act and Regulations.
state_exam.quote: as well as the Jurisprudence Exam, which tests an applicant's knowledge of the SC Occupational Therapy Practice Act and Regulations.

background_check.value: The Occupational Therapy Practice Act requires a national fingerprint-based FBI criminal records check, which the statute ties to determining eligibility for a compact privilege; the applicant pays the cost.
background_check.quote: for the purpose of determining an applicant's eligibility for an initial compact privilege, the department shall require a national criminal records check, supported by fingerprints, by the Federal Bureau of Investigation

application_fee.value: The initial application fee is $135 for an occupational therapist, paid by certified check or money order with a paper application.
application_fee.quote: Submit a certified check or money order in the amount of $135 for OT and $115 for OTA.

endorsement.value: The board may license without examination an occupational therapist who holds a current, valid license in another state with substantially equivalent requirements and who is certified and in good standing with NBCOT.
endorsement.quote: The board may license without examination a person who holds a current and valid license as an occupational therapist or as an occupational therapy assistant in another state if

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board discontinued temporary licenses for new graduates on July 15, 2003, citing NBCOT's on-demand exam scheduling.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The South Carolina Board discontinued the use of temporary licenses for new graduates on July 15, 2003, due to NBCOT offering on-demand computer test scheduling

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses are renewed every two years; the current reporting period runs March 16, 2025 to March 15, 2027, and the renewal deadline is March 15, 2027. NBCOT certification must stay active.
renewal.quote: The biennial reporting period for the 2027 renewal is March 16, 2025 to March 15, 2027.

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete sixteen hours of continuing education per biennium and remain certified and in good standing with NBCOT; no specific mandatory topics are listed.
continuing_education.quote: As a condition of license renewal, a licensee must complete satisfactorily sixteen hours of continuing education per biennium as defined in regulation

compact.value: The OT Compact Commission lists South Carolina as not yet accepting applications for OT Compact privileges.
compact.quote: South Carolina Not Yet Info Coming Soon SC OT

apply_url.value: Applicants can apply through the board's online application, submitting the board's online application forms as part of the process; paper applications are also available.
apply_url.quote: These forms must be completed and submitted to the Board as part of the online application process.

board.value: South Carolina Board of Examiners in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
board.quote: The SC Board of Examiners in Speech Language Pathology and Audiology licenses and regulates the practice of Speech Language Pathologists

education.value: Applicants must have earned a post-graduate degree in speech-language pathology from a school or program the board finds equivalent to ASHA-accredited programs.
education.quote: Have earned a post-graduate degree in Speech-Language Pathology or Audiology from a school or program determined by the board to be equivalent to those accredited by the Council on Professional Standards

application_fee.value: The initial license application fee is $200 for a speech-language pathologist and $100 for a speech-language pathologist intern.
application_fee.quote: Audiologist Intern $100 Speech-Lang Pathologist $200 Speech-Lang Pathologist Intern $100

endorsement.value: The board may license a speech-language pathologist who holds a current license in another state with substantially equivalent standards, subject to any other requirements the board sets, such as continuing education.
endorsement.quote: The board may issue a license to a person who holds a current speech-language pathology or audiology license in another state if the standards for licensure in that state are at least the substantial equivalent

temporary_or_provisional.value: A Speech-Language Pathologist Intern License is issued to graduates who still need to pass the exam and/or complete Supervised Professional Employment of at least 30 hours per week for nine months, totaling not less than 1,260 hours under a licensed SLP.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: needs to complete the Supervised Professional Employment requirement for licensure consisting of a minimum of 30 hours per week of professional employment in speech-language pathology for at least nine months--totaling not less than 1,260 hours

renewal.value: Speech-language pathology licenses are renewed every two years; the current reporting period runs April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2027, and the renewal deadline is March 31, 2027.
renewal.quote: The biennial reporting period for the 2027 renewal is April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2027.

continuing_education.value: Speech-language pathologists must complete 16 hours of continuing education each license period, at least one-half of which must pertain to clinical practice in the area of licensure.
continuing_education.quote: In order to maintain your license as a Speech Language Pathologist or Audiologist in the State of South Carolina, you must complete 16 hours of Continuing Education each license period.

compact.value: The ASLP-IC commission lists compact privilege registration as open only in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, and West Virginia, so South Carolina is not yet issuing ASLP-IC privileges.
compact.quote: Registration for compact privileges to practice is open for licensed practitioners in Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, and West Virginia.

apply_url.value: First-time applicants can apply through the board's electronic application system, which accepts document uploads and card or electronic check payment.
apply_url.quote: You may apply for licensure through our electronic application system. This electronic application will allow you to upload the required documentation and make payment via credit card or electronic check.

board.value: South Dakota Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: On July 1, 2023, physical therapist and physical therapist assistant licensure transitioned from the South Dakota Board of Medical and Osteopathic Examiners to the South Dakota Board of Physical Therapy.

education.value: Applicants must have official transcripts sent directly to the board showing completion of a physical therapy program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), or evidence of recognized educational equivalence.
education.quote: An official transcript showing evidence of degree completion from a program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE);

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NPTE and are responsible for having the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) send their score report directly to the board.
national_exam.quote: If yes, you are responsible for contacting the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) and having your score report sent directly to this Board.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a fingerprint-based criminal background check using the cards the board office sends after it receives the application; the board forwards the completed cards to the Division of Criminal Investigation (DCI).
background_check.quote: Complete Criminal Background Check: The Board office will send a packet upon receipt of an application. You must use the cards the board office provides.

application_fee.value: The application fee for a physical therapist license is $120, payable to the SD Board of Physical Therapy.
application_fee.quote: Application Fee of $120 (payable to the SD Board of Physical Therapy)

endorsement.value: The board may license, without examination, an applicant who holds a physical therapy license from another state, a U.S. territory or the District of Columbia, if that jurisdiction's requirements were substantially equal to South Dakota's at the date of issuance.
endorsement.quote: The State Board of Physical Therapy may, without examination, issue a license to any applicant who holds a license or certificate issued by a board empowered by law to issue a license to practice physical therapy

renewal.value: A physical therapist license expires on January first of the second year after it is issued (a two-year cycle); failing to renew by July first of that second year forfeits the license.
renewal.quote: A license issued by the State Board of Physical Therapy, pursuant to this chapter, expires on January first of the second year following its issuance.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must document 30 continuing education hours during each two-year license cycle; no more than 15 hours may come from Category 2 participatory activities, and extra hours do not roll over.
continuing_education.quote: Licensees must document 30 continuing education hours during the two-year license cycle

compact.value: Physical therapists can obtain a PT Compact privilege for South Dakota; the total PT privilege fee is $169 ($124 state fee, which is $120 plus a $4 processing fee, and a $45 Commission fee), and no jurisprudence exam is required.
compact.quote: Note: South Dakota’s state fee is $120 plus a $4 processing fee.

processing_time.value: The board states that fingerprint background check processing by the Division of Criminal Investigation (DCI) can average 3-4 weeks, and that delays in submitting fingerprint cards delay application review.
processing_time.quote: Board submits cards by mail to DCI DCI processing time can average 3-4 weeks

apply_url.value: The board's Licensing Requirements page provides the application checklist and the notarized application form for physical therapists.
apply_url.quote: Find instructions, application checklists, and application forms to help you get licensed as a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant.

board.value: South Dakota Board of Medical and Osteopathic Examiners
board.quote: The mission of the South Dakota Board of Medical and Osteopathic Examiners is to protect the health and welfare of the state's citizens

education.value: Applicants must complete the academic requirements of an accredited occupational therapy educational program recognized by the board, plus at least six months of supervised fieldwork experience.
education.quote: For an occupational therapist, a minimum of six months of supervised fieldwork experience is required;

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the certification examination of the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT), which is the examination approved by the board.
national_exam.quote: The examination approved by the board is the certification examination of the National Board for Certification of Occupational Therapy.

background_check.value: Applicants must submit a full set of fingerprints for a state and federal criminal background check by the Division of Criminal Investigation and the FBI and pay the background check fees; the board may not issue a license before receiving the results.
background_check.quote: an applicant for licensure as an occupational therapist or an occupational therapy assistant shall submit to the board of examiners a full set of the applicant's fingerprints

application_fee.value: The fee for an initial occupational therapist license is $50.
application_fee.quote: An applicant applying for the initial license shall pay a fee of $50;

endorsement.value: The board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements for an applicant who proves current OT licensure in another state, the District of Columbia or a U.S. territory whose licensure standards the board considers equivalent.
endorsement.quote: The board may waive the examination, education or experience requirements and grant a license to any applicant who shall present proof of current licensure as an occupational therapist

temporary_or_provisional.value: The board may grant a limited permit to a person who has completed the education and experience requirements, allowing practice under the supervision of or in consultation with a licensed OT until licensure or until exam results are available; the permit expires if the person fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The board may grant a limited permit to any person who has completed the education and experience requirements of this chapter.

renewal.value: Occupational therapist licenses are renewed each year: a license expires on the first day of January following issuance, and failure to renew on or before the first day of March forfeits the license.
renewal.quote: Any license issued by the board, pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, shall expire on the first day of January of the year next succeeding the issuance thereof.

continuing_education.value: To renew, occupational therapists must complete 12 continuing competency points in a one-year period in professional education activities related to occupational therapy.
continuing_education.quote: an applicant for renewal must complete 12 continuing competency points in a one-year period in professional education activities updating competency in occupational therapy and practice.

compact.value: South Dakota is an OT Compact member state but is listed as not yet accepting OT Compact privilege applications; the listed South Dakota state fee is $50 for OTs, plus the $75 compact fee.
compact.quote: South Dakota Not Yet not required SD OT Law SD OT Rules $50 $50 $75

apply_url.value: Applicants start the application by creating or logging in to a MySD Account, as directed on the board's occupational therapist page.
apply_url.quote: All applications types can be found through this account.

board.value: South Dakota Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology
board.quote: The mission of the South Dakota Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology is to protect the health and safety of the public

education.value: Applicants must hold a master's or doctoral degree from an institution accredited (or in accreditation candidate status) by ASHA's accrediting agency and approved by the U.S. Department of Education, and must complete supervised clinical practicum and a supervised postgraduate professional experience.
education.quote: Possesses a master's or doctoral degree from an educational institution that is accredited, or has been awarded accreditation candidate status, by the accrediting agency of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association

national_exam.value: Applicants who are not ASHA certified must have Praxis scores sent directly from ETS using code 0279 (South Dakota Board of SLP & Audiology).
national_exam.quote: Praxis Scores directly from ETS (use code: South Dakota Board of SLP & Audiology, 0279)

application_fee.value: The fee for a speech-language pathologist license is $250, made up of a $100 application fee and a $150 licensure fee.
application_fee.quote: Speech-Language Pathologist — $250 (includes $100 application fee/$150 licensure fee)

endorsement.value: The board shall license an applicant who holds a current, unrestricted license from a state with substantially equivalent licensure standards, or an ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology, and who applies on the board's form and pays the fee.
endorsement.quote: Holds a current, unrestricted license from a state with substantially equivalent licensure standards, or a Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association;

temporary_or_provisional.value: Graduates completing the supervised postgraduate professional experience (clinical fellowship) under a licensed SLP can hold a provisional license, which lasts 24 months and may be renewed only once; applicants submit a plan for their CFY naming their South Dakota supervisor.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: The term of a provisional license is 24 months and may be renewed only one time.

renewal.value: Licenses renew biennially and expire on the first day of October of the second year after issuance; a renewal submitted 30 to 180 days after expiration owes a $50 late fee, and after 180 days the licensee must reapply.
renewal.quote: All licenses expire on the first day of October of the second year succeeding the issuance of the license.

continuing_education.value: Licensees must complete at least 20 contact hours (2.0 units) of continuing education each two-year renewal period, through ASHA, ASHA-approved providers, or formal courses approved by the board.
continuing_education.quote: all licensees are required to complete a minimum of 20 contact hours or 2.0 units of continuing education for each two-year renewal period.

apply_url.value: The board's licensing requirements and forms page provides the Application for Licensure and the required application materials checklists.
apply_url.quote: Please review the required application materials. This will guide you in what forms you will need to fill out in order to become licensed.

board.value: Tennessee Board of Physical Therapy
board.quote: Licenses and regulates those qualified to practice as physical therapists in Tennessee.

education.value: Applicants for licensure by examination must be graduates of a physical therapy program accredited by CAPTE and must be of good moral character.
education.quote: If sitting for the physical therapist examination, be a graduate of a school of physical therapy accredited by CAPTE

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), applying for it directly with FSBPT; the passing point is a scaled score of 600.
national_exam.quote: The Board adopts as its examination for physical therapists and physical therapist assistants the NPTE endorsed by the FSBPT or successor examinations.

background_check.value: Applicants must complete a criminal background check as specified by the Board during the application process.
background_check.quote: An applicant must complete the criminal background process as specified by the Board during the application process.

application_fee.value: The physical therapist application fee is $150 and is nonrefundable; applicants also pay a $10 state regulatory fee, a $45 license fee before the license is issued, and, if applying by reciprocity, a $100 reciprocity fee.
application_fee.quote: (4) Fee Schedule: PT PTA (a) Application Fee $150.00 $140.00 (b) Duplicate (Replacement) License Fee

endorsement.value: Physical therapists licensed elsewhere may apply for licensure by reciprocity if they hold a current, unrestricted license from another U.S. jurisdiction, graduated from a CAPTE-accredited program, passed the licensing exam, and obtain verification of licensure from every state where they hold or have held a license.
endorsement.quote: To qualify for licensure by reciprocity a physical therapist or physical therapist assistant must possess a current and unrestricted license from another U.S. jurisdiction

temporary_or_provisional.value: A provisional license is issued to internationally or foreign educated applicants who meet every licensure qualification except the supervised clinical practice period; it is valid for 12 to 48 weeks, cannot be renewed, and requires direct on-site supervision by a Tennessee-licensed physical therapist.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A provisional license shall be issued for an internationally or foreign educated applicant who has complied with all the licensure qualifications

required_courses.value: Foreign-educated applicants for licensure by examination must submit proof of completing 4 hours of ethics and jurisprudence training within 6 months of applying for licensure.
required_courses.quote: within six (6) months of applying for licensure successfully completed four (4) hours of ethics and jurisprudence training

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years (the biennial renewal fee is $140 for physical therapists), and renewal is due by the expiration date indicated on the licensee's renewal certificate.
renewal.quote: The due date for license renewal is the expiration date indicated on the licensee's renewal certificate.

continuing_education.value: Physical therapists must complete 30 hours of continuing competence in the 24 months before the renewal month, at least 20 of them from Class I activities, including 4 hours of ethics and jurisprudence every renewal cycle; new licensees by examination must complete those 4 hours during their initial licensure period.
continuing_education.quote: Thirty (30) hours are required for the twenty-four (24) months that precede the licensure renewal month.

compact.value: Tennessee participates in the PT Compact and compact privileges can be purchased for Tennessee; the total privilege fee for a physical therapist is $240, and a Tennessee jurisprudence course must be completed within 30 days after the privilege is issued.
compact.quote: The Tennessee jurisprudence requirement is a course that must be completed within 30 days after the compact privilege is issued.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online for an initial license through the Tennessee Department of Health's online licensure system, linked from the Board's Applications section, and can pay by credit card, debit card or e-check.
apply_url.quote: allows you to pay for your initial application utilizing a credit card, debit card or e-check.

board.value: Tennessee Board of Occupational Therapy
board.quote: Licenses and regulates those qualified to practice occupational therapy in Tennessee.

education.value: Applicants must have completed an ACOTE-accredited occupational therapist educational program and the supervised fieldwork experience required by ACOTE, and must be of good moral character.
education.quote: Have successfully completed the academic requirements of an educational program for occupational therapists accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) or its predecessor organization

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the NBCOT certification examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, and the Board adopts NBCOT's passing scores.
national_exam.quote: Pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy Examination administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

background_check.value: Applicants must have the results of a criminal background check sent to the Board directly from the vendor named in the application materials.
background_check.quote: directly from the vendor identified in the Board's licensure application materials, the result of a criminal background check.

application_fee.value: The occupational therapist application fee is $125 and is nonrefundable; applicants also pay a $10 state regulatory fee with the application.
application_fee.quote: (a) Application $125.00 $100.00 (b) Duplicate License $25.00 $25.00

endorsement.value: The Board may license by reciprocity an occupational therapist who holds current licensure or certification in another state, D.C. or a U.S. territory and whose education and experience meet or exceed Tennessee's requirements; verification of licensure must be sent from every state where the applicant is or has been licensed.
endorsement.quote: The Board of Occupational Therapy may grant a license to an applicant who presents proof of current licensure or certification as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another state

temporary_or_provisional.value: A limited permit may be issued to applicants who have completed the educational and fieldwork requirements and are scheduled to take the NBCOT exam; holders must practice under a licensed occupational therapist's supervision, must take the exam within 90 days, and the permit is non-renewable (fee $25).
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A limited permit may be issued by the Board to applicants for licensure as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant who have paid the Limited Permit Fee

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years (the biennial renewal fee is $135 for occupational therapists), due by the last day of the licensee's birth month.
renewal.quote: The due date for licensure renewal is the last day of the month in which a licensee's birthday falls

continuing_education.value: Occupational therapists must complete 24 continued competence credits in the 24 months before the renewal month, including 1 hour on ethics and 1 hour on Tennessee occupational therapy law and rules; they must also complete a 2-hour Board-approved suicide prevention training at least once every 4 years.
continuing_education.quote: Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants are required to complete twenty-four (24) continued competence credits during the twenty-four (24) months that precede the licensure renewal month.

compact.value: Tennessee is an OT Compact member that began accepting applications for OT Compact privileges on May 20, 2026; the Tennessee state fee is $125 for OTs plus the $75 compact fee, and no jurisprudence exam is required.
compact.quote: Tennessee May 20, 2026 not required TN OT Practice Act $125 $100 $75

processing_time.value: Applications are accepted throughout the year, and completed files are ordinarily processed at the next Board meeting scheduled for reviewing files.
processing_time.quote: Applications will be accepted throughout the year and completed files will ordinarily be processed at the next Board meeting scheduled for the purpose of reviewing files.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online for an initial license through the Tennessee Department of Health's online licensure system, linked from the Board's Applications section, and can pay by credit card, debit card or e-check.
apply_url.quote: allows you to pay for your initial application utilizing a credit card, debit card or e-check.

board.value: Tennessee Board of Communication Disorders and Sciences
board.quote: Safeguarding the health, safety, and welfare of Tennesseans by requiring those who practice the profession of speech pathology and audiology in Tennessee to be qualified.

education.value: Applicants must hold at least a master's degree in speech-language pathology from an accredited institution and either a current ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence or documented completion of 400 clock hours of supervised clinical practicum, a clinical fellowship and the Praxis exam.
education.quote: An applicant in the area of Speech Language Pathology must possess at least a master's degree in Speech Language Pathology from an accredited institution

national_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Praxis examination, which the Board adopts as its licensure exam, using ASHA's passing score; the testing agency must send results directly to the Board.
national_exam.quote: The Board adopts the Praxis Test, or its successor examination, as its licensure examination.

state_exam.value: Applicants must pass the Tennessee Jurisprudence Exam on the Board's rules and statutes before licensure or reinstatement.
state_exam.quote: The Tennessee Jurisprudence Exam, established by the Board on the rules and statutes, must be successfully completed prior to licensure and/or reinstatement of licensure.

background_check.value: Applicants must have the results of a criminal background check sent to the Board directly from the vendor named in the application materials.
background_check.quote: directly from the vendor identified in the Board's licensure application materials, the result of a criminal background check.

application_fee.value: The speech-language pathologist application fee is $50, and an initial licensure fee of $100 is due once licensure is granted; all fees are nonrefundable, and a $10 state regulatory fee is also charged.
application_fee.quote: 1. Application $50.00 2. Duplicate License Fee 25.00 3. Inactive Volunteer Licensure Renewal Fee 0.00 4. Initial Licensure Fee 100.00

endorsement.value: SLPs licensed in another state may be licensed by reciprocity if the Board finds the other state's licensure standards, when they were licensed there, at least equivalent to Tennessee's current requirements; each state where they hold or held a license must send an official statement directly to the Board.
endorsement.quote: An individual who seeks licensure in the State of Tennessee and who holds a current license in another state may be granted a Tennessee license

temporary_or_provisional.value: Clinical fellows must hold a provisional license and work under the supervision of a Tennessee-licensed or ASHA-certified speech-language pathologist, whom they must register with the Board.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: Clinical Fellows must hold a provisional license and must work under the supervision of a Tennessee Licensed or ASHA Certified Speech Language Pathologist

renewal.value: Licenses renew every two years (biennial renewal fee of $60), and renewal is due by the expiration date on the renewal certificate, with the renewal and state regulatory fees and an attestation of continuing education.
renewal.quote: The due date for license renewal is the expiration date indicated on the renewal certificate.

continuing_education.value: SLPs must complete 20 hours of continuing education during the two calendar years before the renewal year, at least 10 of them in their own area of practice.
continuing_education.quote: All Speech Language Pathologists and Audiologists must complete twenty (20) hours of continuing education during the two calendar years

compact.value: Tennessee is an ASLP-IC member state and has been issuing compact privileges to practice since May 28, 2026.
compact.quote: Update May 28, 2026: Tennessee is now issuing privileges to practice.

processing_time.value: If a completed application arrives before the 30th day of the month preceding the next Board meeting, an initial determination is made before that meeting; the license is not issued until the full Board ratifies it.
processing_time.quote: If the completed application was received before the thirtieth (30th) day of the month preceding the next Board meeting, an initial determination shall be made prior to the next Board meeting.

apply_url.value: Applicants apply online for an initial license through the Tennessee Department of Health's online licensure system, linked from the Board's Applications section, and can pay by credit card, debit card or e-check.
apply_url.quote: allows you to pay for your initial application utilizing a credit card, debit card or e-check.

board.value: Texas Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
board.quote: is a State of Texas agency charged with protecting the health, safety, and welfare of the people of Texas by supporting the Board of PT Examiners and the Board of OT Examiners

education.value: Graduation from a CAPTE-accredited physical therapy program, with an official transcript sent to the Board directly by the school. Foreign-educated applicants submit an educational evaluation in place of the transcript.
education.quote: This applies only to graduates of CAPTE-accredited programs

national_exam.value: Pass the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE), administered by the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT). Texas uses FSBPT's Alternate Approval Pathway, so FSBPT decides exam eligibility. The board's pages do not give a numeric passing score.
national_exam.quote: The Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) has the final authority to determine who is eligible to sit for the National Physical Therapy Examination (NPTE)

state_exam.value: Required: the Texas Jurisprudence Assessment Module (TX JAM), taken through FSBPT before the license is issued, whether applying by exam or by endorsement. It has 75 questions and needs 60 correct (80%) to pass, and it is free for initial applicants.
state_exam.quote: Individuals applying for initial PT or PTA licensure in Texas will need to take the TX JAM as a licensure requirement.

background_check.value: A criminal background check by fingerprinting (state DPS and FBI) is required before a license is issued.
background_check.quote: A Criminal Background Check via Fingerprinting is required prior to issuance of a license.

application_fee.value: $190 for a PT, covering the application and permanent license ($125 for a PTA). Set by 22 TAC 651.2 in the board's May 2026 rules compilation. The fee is non-refundable.
application_fee.quote: (a) Application/Permanent License. (1) PT--$190. (2) PTA--$125. (b) Application to Retake the Examination. (1) PT--$25.

endorsement.value: PTs licensed in another state apply by endorsement. They submit the online application and fee, a transcript, an NPTE score transfer from FSBPT, license verification showing at least one current, active, unencumbered license, the TX JAM and fingerprints. Endorsement applicants cannot get a temporary license.
endorsement.quote: At least one verification needs to show current, active licensure without any encumbrance.

temporary_or_provisional.value: An optional temporary license is available to applicants by exam who have never taken the NPTE and have met every other requirement. It costs $80 for a PT and requires on-site supervision by a Texas-licensed PT. It lasts until the permanent license is issued or until the last day of the third month after it was issued, and it becomes void if the applicant fails the exam.
temporary_or_provisional.quote: A Temporary License is valid until issuance of the permanent license, or until the last day of the third month after the month the license is issued.

renewal.value: PT licenses are renewed every two years, by the end of the licensee's birth month. Renewal can start three months before expiration.
renewal.quote: Licensees are required to renew their licenses every two years by the end of their birth month.

continuing_education.value: PTs need 30 continuing competence units (CCUs) per two-year cycle. These must include the TX JAM (worth 2 CCUs) and an HHS-approved human trafficking prevention course.
continuing_education.quote: for PTs, 30 units (CCUs) during each two-year renewal cycle, for PTAs, 20 units (CCUs). All licensees must complete the Jurisprudence Assessment Module (TX JAM) and an HHS-approved Human Trafficking Prevention Training course

compact.value: Texas is a member of the PT Compact (enacted by SB 317 in 2017), and compact privileges into and out of Texas have been issued since January 2, 2019. A Texas privilege costs $50 (plus a $45 commission fee), and the applicant must pass the TX JAM.
compact.quote: Compact privileges for Texas licensees to practice in another member state and for licensees of other member states to be able to practice in Texas became available January 02, 2019.

apply_url.value: Apply online through the ECPTOTE Online Licensing System after creating an account; the board page linked here has the portal link.
apply_url.quote: Create an Online Licensing System Account. You must create an online account in order to start a new application.

board.value: Texas Board of Occupational Therapy Examiners
board.quote: is a State of Texas agency charged with protecting the health, safety, and welfare of the people of Texas by supporting the Board of PT Examiners and the Board of OT Examiners

education.value: Completion of the academic and supervised fieldwork requirements of an accredited occupational therapy program. The OT rules define an accredited program as one accredited or approved by ACOTE. Foreign-trained applicants must show substantially equivalent education.
